body.text: Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna
body.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna</s> (The Legend of the Golden-Colored One)

body.text:
Sva Roy 1,1
om namo buddhāya ||
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 1,1 - 5
[1] evam anuśrūyate sthavira mahākāśyape parinirvṛte sthavirānando mahātmā śāradvatīputrasamanuprajñayā samanvāgatas tathāgata iva kāruṇyāt teṣu teṣu grāmanagaranigamapallīpattanādiṣu tāṃs tān vaineyāṃs tais tair upāyaviśeṣair vinayati sma | yāvad apareṇa samayena vineyavaśād anekāni sattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahastrāṇi saddharmmadeśanāmṛtavarṣābhiṣekeṇa santarpayan vaiśālyām viharaty āmrapālīvane |
body.translated_text: [1] Thus it has been heard: When the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> had attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), the great-souled elder <s>Ānanda</s>, endowed with wisdom equal to that of <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, like the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, out of compassion, was disciplining various beings to be trained in various villages, cities, towns, hamlets, and ports by means of various skillful methods. In due course, by the power of those to be trained, satisfying many hundreds of thousands of millions of beings with the consecration of the nectar-rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> teaching, he was dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s> in the <s>Āmrapālī</s> grove.

body.text:
Sva Roy 1,5 - 3,2
[2] tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājagṛhe nagare divākaro nāma sārthavāhaḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratisparddhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam | sa tayā sārddha krīḍati ramate paricārayati sma | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato na putro na duhitā | so 'putraḥ putrahetor utkaṇṭhitaḥ paritapyate | deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣv anyatamasya puṇyamaheśākhyasya devaputrasya pañcapūrvanimittāni prādurbhūtāni | sa buddhotpādavibhūṣitaṃ lokam avalokya nirvāṇābhilāṣīcchati manuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ grahītum |
body.translated_text: [2] Now at that time, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there lived a caravan leader named <s>Divākara</s>, who was wealthy, of great riches, of great resources, with vast and extensive possessions, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing. Together with her he enjoyed pleasures, delighted, and made merry. As he enjoyed, delighted, and made merry, there was neither a son nor a daughter. Without a son, longing for a son, he was tormented. Among the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, for a certain son of the gods named <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit), the five premonitory signs of death had appeared. He, looking down at the world adorned by the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, desiring <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, wished to take rebirth among humans.

body.text:
Sva Roy 3,2 - 4,5
[3] adrākṣīc chakro devendras taṃ devaputraṃ cyavanadharmmāṇaṃ buddhotpādavibhūṣitaṃ lokam avalokya nirvāṇābhilāṣī icchati manuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ grahītum iti dṛṣṭvā ca punas taṃ devaputram upasaṃkramyovāca | sa cet tvaṃ mārṣa icchasi manuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ grahītum | rājagṛhe nagare divākarasya sārthavāhasya patnyāḥ kukṣau pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhāṇeti | sa kathayati kauśikaṃ aśrāddho 'sau sārthavāhas tasya buddhe prasādo nāstīti | śakraḥ kathayati | mārṣa gṛhāṇa tvaṃ ahan tathā kariṣyāmi yathāsau sārthavāho buddhaśāsane 'bhiprasīdatīti | devaputraḥ kathayati | kauśika sa ced asau sārthavāhaḥ sapatnīko yāvajjīvaṃ ratnatrayaṃ śaraṇaṅ gacched evam ahaṃ tasya sārthavāhasya patnyāḥ kukṣau pratisandhiṃ grahīṣyāmīti |
body.translated_text: [3] <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, saw that son of the gods who was subject to the law of passing away, and that looking at the world adorned by the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, desiring <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, he wished to take rebirth among humans. Having seen this, he approached that son of the gods and said: 'If you, sir, wish to take rebirth among humans, take rebirth in the womb of the wife of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.' He replied: '<s>Kauśika</s>, that caravan leader is without faith; he has no devotion to the <s>Buddha</s>.' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Sir, take rebirth there. I shall act in such a way that the caravan leader develops faith in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>.' The son of the gods said: '<s>Kauśika</s>, if that caravan leader together with his wife takes refuge in the Three Jewels for life, then I shall take rebirth in the womb of that caravan leader's wife.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 5,1 - 7,3
[4] tataḥ śakro devendro devebhyas trayastriṃśebhya antarīkṣe rājagṛhe nagare divākarasya sārthavāhasya gṛhe uparime talake pratyasthāt | śakrasya devendrasya varṇānubhāvena sarvatra gṛhaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsitam adrākṣīd divākaraḥ sārthavāhas tu divyam avabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar vismayotphullalocanaś caturdiśam avalokayitum ārabdhaḥ yāvat paśyati śakraṃ devendraṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sahasaiva tasya padayor praṇipatyovāca devendra lābhā me sulabdhā me tvaṃ gṛham āyātaḥ pavitrīkṛtañ cedaṃ gṛhaṃ yuṣmad āgamanena | tadājñāpyatāṃ kim āgamanaprayojanam iti | śakro devendraḥ kathayati | sārthavāha tvam aputraḥ putrābhinandī tad adyāgreṇa sapatnīko yāvajjīvaṃ ratnatrayaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha | putras te bhaviṣyatīti || divākaraḥ sārthavāho hṛṣṭatuṣṭa udagramanāḥ kathayati | devendra yathā tvam ājñāpayasi tathā karomy eṣo 'ham adyāgreṇa sapatnīko jāvajjīvaṃ ratnatrayaṃ śaraṇaṅ gacchāmīty atha śakro devendro divākaraṃ sārthavāhaṃ sapatnīkaṃ śaraṇagamane pratiṣṭhāpya rājagṛhād antarhito deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣv pratyaṣṭāt | tasya devaputrasya bhavane tataḥ śakro devendras tasya devaputrasyaitat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇākhyātavān |
body.translated_text: [4] Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, from the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> gods, through the sky, appeared in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> on the upper terrace of the house of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. By the radiance of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the entire house was illuminated with divine splendor. The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> saw the divine radiance, and upon seeing it, with eyes wide open in amazement, he began to look in all four directions. He then saw <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and upon seeing him, immediately prostrating at his feet, he said: 'Lord of the gods, what good fortune, what great gain for me that you have come to my house! This house is purified by your arrival. Command me—what is the purpose of your coming?' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said: 'Caravan leader, you are without a son, yet you desire a son. Therefore, from this day forward, together with your wife, take refuge in the Three Jewels for life. You shall have a son.' The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, delighted, pleased, and elated in mind, said: 'Lord of the gods, as you command, so I shall do. From this day forward, together with my wife, I take refuge in the Three Jewels for life.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having established the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> together with his wife in taking refuge, disappeared from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and reappeared among the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> gods, at the abode of that son of the gods. There <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, related the entire matter in detail to that son of the gods.

body.text:
Sva Roy 7,3 - 9,10
[5] yāvad asau devaputro devebhyas trayastriṃśebhyaś cyuto rājagṛhe nagare divākarasya sārthavāhasya patnyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ | sa yata eva tasyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntas tata eva tasyāḥ sārthavāhapatnyāḥ śarīre parā varṇapuṣkalatā prādurbhūtā | manojñaś ca gandhaḥ pravātum ārabdhaḥ | pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme | katame pañca | raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti | viraktaṃ jānāti | kālaṃ jānāti | ṛtuṃ jānāti | garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti | yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti | dārakaṃ jānāti | dārikāṃ jānāti | sa ced dārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśṛtya tiṣṭhati | sa ced dārikā bhavati | vāmaṃ kukṣin niḥsṛtya tiṣṭhati | sā āttamanāttamanā svāmine ārocayati | diṣṭyāryaputra varddhase | āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | śrutvā ca punaḥ so 'py āttamanātamanāḥ pūrvakāyam abhyunnamayya dakṣiṇam bāhum abhiprasāryodānam udānayati | apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyaṃ jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ kṛtyāni me kurvvīta bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyād dāyādyaṃ pratipadyet | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syād asmākañ cātyatītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtam vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā asmākañ ca nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyate | idaṃ tayor yatra tatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti
body.translated_text: [5] Then that son of the gods, having passed away from the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> gods, descended into the womb of the wife of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. From the very moment he descended into her womb, a supreme beauty of complexion appeared in the body of the caravan leader's wife. And a delightful fragrance began to emanate. There are five distinctive qualities in certain wise women of noble birth. What five? She knows when a man is passionate; she knows when he is dispassionate; she knows the time; she knows the season; she knows when a conception has descended. She knows from whom the conception comes; she knows if it is a boy; she knows if it is a girl. If it is a boy, he settles resting on the right side of the womb. If it is a girl, she settles resting on the left side of the womb. She, overjoyed, announced to her husband: 'Good fortune to you, noble husband! I have become pregnant with a being. And since it rests on the right side of my womb, it will certainly be a boy.' Upon hearing this, he too, overjoyed, raising his upper body and extending his right arm, uttered an exclamation: 'May I indeed see the face of a son long desired! May he be born to me, not stillborn. May he perform my duties, maintain what I have maintained, and receive the inheritance. May my family lineage endure for a long time. And for us, when we have passed away, having given gifts, great or small, and made merit, may he dedicate the offering in our name—may this follow those two wherever they are reborn and go.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 10,2 - 12,3
[6] āpannasattvāñ caināṃ viditvā upariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati | śīte śītopakaraṇai uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhārair hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrtrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharimāṃ bhūmiṃ | na cāsyāḥ kiñcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya | sā aṣṭānām vā navānām vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ sarvajanamanonayanaharaḥ suvarṇapītair vastrair avaguṇṭhitavigrahaḥ sarvaśarīrāc cāsya candanagandho vāti | mukhāc cāsya nīlotpalagandhaḥ | tasya jātamātrasya tasmin gṛhe vastravarṣaṃ karṇikārakusumavarṣañ ca patitam | tāni ca vastrāṇi suvarṇavarṇāni |
body.translated_text: [6] Having learned that she was with child, he kept her on the upper floor of the mansion, unrestrained. With provisions for cold in the cold season, with provisions for heat in the hot season, with foods prescribed by physicians—not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, with foods free from bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent extremes—her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, not going to the ground floor. Nor was there any hearing of unpleasant sounds for her, all for the ripening of the embryo. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born—handsome, beautiful, charming, endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs, possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold, captivating the minds and eyes of all people, his body wrapped in golden-yellow garments. And from his entire body emanated the fragrance of sandalwood, and from his mouth the fragrance of blue lotus. At the very moment of his birth, a rain of garments and a rain of <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers fell upon that house. And those garments were golden in color.

body.text:
Sva Roy 12,3 - 14,3
[7] tatas tām atyadbhutāṃ tasya ca rūpaudāryasampadāṃ dṛṣṭvā divākarasya sārthavāhasya patnī parijanaś ca param vismayam āpannaḥ | divākaraś ca sārthavāho gṛhasya bahir dvārakoṣṭhake sthitaḥ | tasya niveditaṃ sārthavāho diṣṭyā varddhase putras tu jāta iti | sa hṛṣṭatuṣṭodagramanā gṛhaṃ praviṣṭo yāvat paśyati kumāram atyantam abhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ | prāsādikaṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaṃ | uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataṃ sarvajanamanonayanaharaṃ suvarṇapītair vastrair avaguṇṭhitavigrahaṃ kāyāc cāsya candanagandho vāti mukhāc ca nīlotpalagandhaḥ | vastravaryaṃ karṇikārakusumavarṣañ ca patitaṃ | tāni ca vastrāṇi suvarṇavarṇāni dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paramaprītiprāmodya udānam udānayati aho lābhā me sulabdhāḥ aho paripūṇo me manoratho yasya me īdṛśaḥ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ putro jāta iti | hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditamanās tāni ca vastrāṇi śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavebhyo dattāni |
body.translated_text: [7] Then, upon seeing that most wondrous excellence of beauty and form, the wife of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> and the attendants were struck with supreme wonder. The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> was standing outside at the entrance hall of the house. It was announced to him: 'Caravan leader, good fortune to you—a son has been born!' Delighted, pleased, and elated in mind, he entered the house and saw the prince, supremely handsome, beautiful, charming, endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs, possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold, captivating the minds and eyes of all people, his body wrapped in golden-yellow garments. And from his body emanated the fragrance of sandalwood, and from his mouth the fragrance of blue lotus. A rain of excellent garments and a rain of <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers had fallen, and those garments were golden in color. Upon seeing this, with supreme joy and delight, he uttered an exclamation: 'Oh, what good fortune, what great gain for me! My heart's desire is fulfilled, for such a son named <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit) has been born to me!' With a heart delighted, pleased, and overjoyed, he distributed those garments to ascetics, brahmins, the wretched, beggars, friends, relatives, and kinsmen.

body.text:
Sva Roy 14,3 - 17,3
[8] tasya ca kumārasya trīṇi saptakāny ekaviṃśati divasān vistareṇa jātamātrasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate | kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ucur ayaṃ kumāra uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ | tasmād bhavatu kumārasya suvarṇavarṇa iti nāma suvarṇavarṇa iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradattaḥ | dvābhyām aṅkadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyāṃ yāvad āśu varddhate hradastham iva paṅkajam sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ tadā lipyām upanyastaḥ saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāṃ uddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ vastraparīkṣāyāṃ vastraparīkṣāyāṃ ibhiparīkṣāyāṃ aśvaparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ kumāraparīkṣāyāṃ kumārikāparīkṣāyāṃ so 'ṣṭāsu parīkṣāsūdghāṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ samvṛttaḥ | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ ātmahitaparahitaṃ pratipannaḥ | kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmmakāmaḥ satvatsalas tena ca śāstrāṇy adhītāni | so 'tyantaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyo yac cintayati | yat prārthayati | vastrādikan dhanaṃ sarvan tat tathaiva sampadyate | kin tu na vijānāty aham eva puṇyamaheśākhya iti | divākaraś ca sārthavāho ratnatrayaśaraṇagamanaprabhāvān me putro jāta iti bhūyasyā mātrayā bhagavac chāsane 'bhiprasannaḥ sa kālena kālaṃ bhagavacchāsane kārāṅ karoti sma |
body.translated_text: [8] For that prince, over three sets of seven—twenty-one days—elaborately celebrating the birth festival, a name was established. 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'This prince is possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold. Therefore, let the prince's name be <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> (Golden-colored).' Thus the name <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> was established. The prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses—two nurses to hold him, two wet-nurses, two nurses for bathing, and two nurses for play. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, he was set to learning writing, arithmetic, calculation, seals, assessment, deposit, storage, examination of goods, examination of cloth, examination of elephants, examination of horses, examination of timber, examination of gems, examination of boys, and examination of girls. In all eight examinations he became a skillful, articulate, learned, and clever practitioner. He was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, and tender toward beings. He had studied the treatises. He was supremely endowed with great merit—whatever he thought of, whatever he wished for, wealth such as garments and all else came to pass exactly so. But he did not know that he himself was called <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit). The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, believing that his son was born through the power of taking refuge in the Three Jewels, became even more devoted to the teaching of the Blessed One, and from time to time he made offerings to the teaching of the Blessed One.

body.text:
Sva Roy 17,3 - 19,5
[9] tena khalu samayena rājagṛhe nagare vimalo nāma sārthavāho mahāsamudrāt saṃsiddhayānapātro 'bhyāgatas tenārddhatrayodaśaparivāraṃ buddham bhagavantaṃ bhojayitvā ekaiko bhikṣus tricīvareṇācchāditas tasya yaśasā sarvo loka āpūrṇaḥ sārthasya saphalaṃ mahāsamudrāvataraṇaṃ sārthavāhaśabdaś ca yenaivaṃ bhagavacchāsane kārāḥ kṛtā iti | divākarasya sārthavāhasya śrutvā sparddhā jātā | aham api mahāsamudram avatarāmi | yadi tataḥ saṃsiddhayānapātro 'bhyāgacchāmi | yāvantaḥ ke cana bhagavacchrāvakā jambūdvīpe prativasanti bhagavantaṃ vijñapya tān aikadhya sannipātya praṇītenāhāreṇa santarpya ekaikaṃ bhikṣuṃ mahārheṇa tricīvareṇācchādayiṣyāmīti | tena patnyā eṣa vṛttānto niveditaḥ | sā kathayati svāmin ṛdhyantu tava saṅkalpāḥ | paripūryantām manorathā iti | tato divākaraḥ sārthavāho rājagṛhe nagare yāvat trir api ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṅ kārayitvā pañcavaṇikaśataparivāro mahāsamudram avatīrṇas tasya tasmin mahāsamudre 'vatīrṇasya bhagavān parinirvṛtas tatra sthitasyaiva cāsya sthaviramahākāśyapo 'pi parinirvṛto
body.translated_text: [9] Now at that time, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a caravan leader named <s>Vimala</s> returned from the great ocean with a successful voyage. Having fed the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, together with a retinue of twelve and a half, and having clothed each <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) with a set of three robes, his fame filled the entire world—the ocean voyage of the caravan had been fruitful, and the title of caravan leader was merited because such offerings had been made to the teaching of the Blessed One. When the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> heard this, rivalry arose in him: 'I too shall venture into the great ocean. If I return from there with a successful voyage, I shall request the Blessed One, assemble all the disciples of the Blessed One dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> together in one place, satisfy them with excellent food, and clothe each <s>bhikṣu</s> with a set of three robes of great value.' He informed his wife of this plan. She said: 'My lord, may your intentions be fulfilled! May your heart's desires be realized!' Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, having had a bell proclamation made three times throughout the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, descended into the great ocean accompanied by a retinue of five hundred merchants. While he had descended into that great ocean, the Blessed One attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), and while he was still there, the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> too attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 19,5 - 21,3
[10] yāvad apareṇa samayena suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro veṇuvanaṅ gatas tatra bhikṣur anityatāpratisaṃyuktā gāthā svādhyāyati sma |
body.translated_text: [10] In due course, the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> went to the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), where a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) was reciting verses connected with impermanence.

body.text: āyur divā ca rātrau ca carato vā sthitasya vā |

children.text: sroto mahānadīnām vā yāty eva na nivartate |1|
children.translated_text: Like the current of great rivers, passes on and never returns. [1]
For those whose lifespan becomes shorter with each night's stay,

children.text: alpodake ca matsyānāṃ kā nu teṣāṃ rati bhavet |2|
children.translated_text: Like fish in dwindling water—what pleasure could there be for them? [2]
This form is worn out, a nest of disease, fragile;
This putrid mass will break apart, for life ends in death. [3]

children.text: na cirād vata kāyo 'yaṃ pṛthivīm adhiśeṣyate |
children.translated_text: Before long, alas, this body will lie upon the earth,

children.text: śūnyo vyapeta vijñāno nirastaṃ vā kaḍaṅgaraṃ |4|
children.translated_text: Empty, devoid of consciousness, cast aside like a useless log. [4]
What use is this body that constantly oozes foulness?
By this body, always afflicted by disease, fearful of old age and death, |5|
foul, fragile, and ailing—

children.text: mīmita paramāṃ śāntiṃ yogakṣemam anuttaram iti |6|
children.translated_text: one should seek the supreme peace, the unsurpassed <s>yogakṣema</s> (spiritual security). |6|

body.translated_text: Life, whether by day or by night, whether one is moving or standing still,

body.text:
Sva Roy 21,3 - 23,1
[11] athaitā gāthāḥ śrutvā suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ samvignaḥ saṃsārān nirvāṇānuśaṃsadarśī | tasya bhikṣor vandanāṃ kṛtvā pṛcchati | ārya kim idam iti bhikṣuṇābhihitam āyuṣman buddhavacanam iti | tasya śrutvā bhagavacchāsane mahān prasāda utpannaḥ pravrajyābhilāṣo mokṣābhilāś ca | tatas tasya bhikṣoḥ satkṛtya pādayor nipatya kathayaty ārya pravrajitum icchāmi | tadanukampām upādāya māṃ pravrājayitum arhasīti | bhikṣuṇābhihitam āyuṣman kim anujñāto 'si mātāpitṛbhyām iti | sa kathayati neti | bhikṣuḥ kathayati gacchāyuṣmān mātāpitarau tāvad avalokaya na hy ananujñātaṃ mātāpitṛbhyām vayaṃ pravrājayāma iti | sa kathayaty evaṅ karomīti |
body.translated_text: Then, having heard these verses, Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, filled with spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>), seeing the benefits of <s>nirvāṇa</s> over <s>saṃsāra</s>, paid homage to that <s>bhikṣu</s> and asked: 'Venerable one, what is this?' The <s>bhikṣu</s> replied: 'Venerable sir, it is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.' Upon hearing this, great faith arose in him toward the teaching of the Blessed One, and a desire for renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and a longing for liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Then, having honored that <s>bhikṣu</s> and fallen at his feet, he said: 'Venerable one, I wish to renounce. Out of compassion, please ordain me.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> replied: 'Venerable sir, do you have the permission of your parents?' He said: 'No.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> said: 'Go, venerable sir, first consult your parents, for we do not ordain one who has not been permitted by his parents.' He said: 'I will do so.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 23,1 - 26,5
[12] tataḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ saṃsārabhayodvignamanāḥ svaniveśanaṃ gatvā mātuḥ pādayor nipatya kathayaty ambānujānīhi māṃ pravrajāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye | iti śrutvāsya mātā paramaviṣādam āpannā | urasi prahāraṃ dattvā kathayati | putra tvam me ekaputrakaḥ priyo manāpaḥ kānto 'pratikūlo manorathaśataiḥ pratilabdhaḥ | kathan nāma tvaṃ mām apahāya pravrajasīti | sa kathayaty ambāvaśyaṃ bhāvī priyaviprayogas tad anujānīhi māṃ pravrajāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaya iti | tasya śrutvā mahān samvego jātaḥ sā bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhī provāca | putra mā māṃ trir api vakṣyasi | mā me uṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ mukhād āgamiṣyatīti | sā saṃlakṣayati | yādṛśo 'sya vyavasāyo na śakṣyam evaṃ mayā nivārayitum | upāyasamvidhānaṅ karomīti | tataḥ sā kathayati | putra tava pitā buddhaśāsane kārāṅ kariṣyātīti mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | sa yāvan nāgacchati | tāvat tvān nānujānāmi | yady asāv āgata tvām anujñāsyati pravrajiṣyasīti | sa mātṛbhaktaḥ saṃlakṣayati | yadi bhūyo 'py enāṃ vakṣyāmi kadācid eṣā mahāntaṃ samvegam āpasyate | tad yāvan me pitā nāgacchati tāvat tiṣṭhāmīti | sa tuṣṇīm avasthitaḥ | yadā ca suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro vīthīm avatarati | tadā lokas tasya rūpodāryasampadaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirīkṣamāṇo na_atra tṛptim upayāti | sa mahājanakāyasya vallabho jātas tasya rūpaudārya sampadā samākṛṣṭamanaso 'tyantaṃ kāmavimukhatāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātā saṃlakṣayati | dhik kaṣṭaṃ yādṛśo 'sya vyavasāyas tadāpy eṣa mām apahāya pravrajiṣyatīti | tato nityaṃ śaṅkitamanasā tasyānukūlaṃ pravartitum ārabdhā ||
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, his mind agitated by fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, went to his own residence and, falling at his mother's feet, said: 'Mother, please permit me—I wish to renounce in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Hearing this, his mother was overcome with the deepest sorrow. Striking her breast, she said: 'Son, you are my only child, dear, beloved, cherished, not unwelcome, obtained through hundreds of wishes. How can you abandon me and renounce?' He said: 'Mother, separation from loved ones is inevitable. Therefore permit me—I wish to renounce in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Upon hearing this, great agitation arose in her. She spoke with a voice choked with tears: 'Son, do not ask me a third time! Lest hot blood come forth from my mouth!' She reflected: 'Given the firmness of his resolve, I will not be able to restrain him in this way. I shall devise a stratagem.' Then she said: 'Son, your father has crossed the great ocean to conduct trade for the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. Until he returns, I will not permit you. If he comes back and permits you, you may renounce.' He, being devoted to his mother, reflected: 'If I press her further, she may at some point be overcome with great distress. I shall wait until my father returns.' He remained silent. And whenever Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> went out into the streets, the people, seeing the splendor of his beauty, gazed at him and could not be satisfied. He became beloved of the great multitude. Seeing that despite his splendor of beauty, which captivated everyone's hearts and eyes, he was utterly averse to sensual pleasures, his mother reflected: 'Alas, woe! Given the firmness of his resolve, he will surely abandon me and renounce.' From then on, with a constantly anxious mind, she began to act in accordance with his wishes.

body.text:
Sva Roy 26,3 - 27,28
[13] suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro 'bhīkṣṇam paṇḍitān śramaṇān brāhmaṇān sevate | sa tatra yat subhāṣitaṃ mokṣamātrānukūlaṃ śṛṇoti | tatpustake 'bhilikhati | divākarasya ca sārthavāhasya rājagṛhān nagarād bahir udyānaṃ puṣpaphalasalilasampannaṃ | tataḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāras tat paitṛkam udyānaṃ dine dine gatvā subhāṣitapustakaṃ vācayaṃs tiṣṭhati | tena khalu samayena rājagṛhe nagare kāśisundarī nāma veśyā prativasati | strīrūpayauvanasampannā mahājanavallabhā rājñaś cājātaśatroḥ pracaṇḍanāmāmātyas tasya rājño 'tyartham bahumataḥ | sa kāśisundaryāṃ dārikāyām atyartaṃ saṃraktacittas tayā saha dine dine svam udyānaṅ gatvā ratikrīḍām anubhavati |
body.translated_text: Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> frequently visited learned <s>śramaṇa</s>s and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s. Whatever well-spoken words conducive solely to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) he heard there, he wrote down in a book. Now the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> had a garden outside the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, endowed with flowers, fruit, and water. Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> would go to that paternal garden every day and remain there reading the book of well-spoken words. At that time, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there lived a courtesan named <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, endowed with feminine beauty and youth, beloved of the people. And King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s minister named <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> was greatly esteemed by that king. He, being passionately attached to the courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, would go day after day with her to his own garden and enjoy amorous pleasures.

body.text:
Sva Roy 28,1 - 31,4
[14] yāvad apareṇa samayena kāśisundarīdārikā sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitā rājagṛhān nirgatya pracaṇḍasyāmātyasyodyānaṃ saṃprasthitā | suvarṇavarṇaś ca kumāro rājagṛhān nagarān nirgatya svam udyānaṅ gacchati | adrākṣīt kāśisundarī dārikā suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram atyantam abhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetam uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataṃ | sarvajanamanonayanaharaṃ suvarṇavarṇapītair vastrair avaguṇṭhitavigrahaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyā etad abhavat | aho rūpaudāryasampadaḥ | aho varṇapuṣkalatā kṛtabhāgyā sā nārī yasyā eṣa bharttā bhaviṣyatīti | sā tasmin atyantam ākṣiptā saṃlakṣati | mandabhāgyā sā nārī sā īdṛśena puruṣeṇa sārddhaṃ ratikrīḍān nānubhavati | vayaṃ rūpajīvinyaḥ | sādhāraṇapuruṣāṇām eṣa ca kumāraḥ pratyagrayauvanasamanvāgataḥ | yan nv aham enaṃ tathā pralobhayeyaṃ yathā mamānena saha saṃyogo bhaved iti | sā tasya purataḥ sthitvā nimittam upadarśayitum ārabdhā | sa mahātmā prakṛtyaiva kāmavimukhatvān nirvāṇapravaṇatvād vā ca na tāṃ samanvāharati |
body.translated_text: Then, on another occasion, the courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, adorned with all ornaments, departed from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and set out for Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>'s garden. Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> also departed from the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and went to his own garden. <s>Kāśisundarī</s> saw Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>—exceedingly handsome, beautiful, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor bodily features, possessed of a complexion like refined gold in its fullness of color, captivating the hearts and eyes of all people, his body draped in golden-yellow garments—and upon seeing him, this thought arose in her: 'Oh, what splendor of beauty! Oh, what fullness of color! Fortunate is the woman whose husband he will be!' She, being extremely attracted to him, reflected: 'Unfortunate is the woman who does not enjoy amorous pleasures with such a man. We are those who live by beauty, common to [all] men. And this prince is endowed with the freshest youth. What if I were to entice him so that a union between us might occur?' She stood before him and began to display amorous signs. But he, being a great soul, naturally averse to sensual pleasures and inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, did not attend to her.

body.text:
Sva Roy 31,4 - 35
[15] sā saṃlakṣayati nūnam eṣa lajjīyate | teneha māṃ na samanvāharaty eṣa codyānaṃ samprasthito 'ham api tatraiva gacchāmi | tatra cainaṃ pracchanne pralobhayiṣyāmīti sā tasya pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhā suvarṇavarṇena kumāreṇopalakṣitā tenāgrataḥ praviśya tasyodyānasya dvāraṃ baddhaṃ | kāśisundarī dārikā kathayati | kumāra katham evaṃ yujyate | ahaṃ tvām uddiśyāgatā | na yuktaṃ tava mayy evaṃ naiṣṭhuryam upadarśayitum iti | sa naiva tasyāḥ prativacanaṃ dadāti | sā saṃlakṣayati | dvābhyām atra bhavitavyaṃ | atha vātyantaṃ kāmair anarthī | athavā mahatā dainyenāvaṣṭabdhaḥ | sarvathā na śakyam eṣa mayā rūpeṇa vā vacasā vā ārādhayituṃ sparśenainam ārādhayiṣyāmi | eṣa ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā dvāraṃ badhnāti | ka upāyaḥ syād yenāham enaṃ pracchannam āsādayeyaṃ | atha vāpratisaṃviditam evāsya śvaḥ prathamataram āgatya etam udyānaṃ praviśya sthāsyāmi parata enam āgatam āliṅganādibhiḥ gātrasaṃsparśanais tathārādhayiṣyāmi yathā me vaśago bhaviṣyatīti | saivam anuvicintya pratinivṛtya nagaraṃ praviṣṭā | taṃ ca divasaṃ pracanṇḍasyāmātyasyodyānaṃ na gatā ||
body.translated_text: She reflected: 'Surely he is shy. That is why he does not attend to me here. He is heading to the garden—I too shall go there. There, in secret, I shall entice him.' She followed behind him. Noticed by Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, he entered ahead and locked the door of the garden. <s>Kāśisundarī</s> said: 'Prince, how is this fitting? I have come on your account. It is not proper for you to show me such cruelty.' He gave her no reply whatsoever. She reflected: 'It must be one of two things: either he is utterly indifferent to sensual pleasures, or he is constrained by great humility. In any case, I cannot win him over by beauty or words—I shall win him through touch. But he locks the door upon seeing me. What stratagem could I use to approach him in secret? I know—tomorrow, very early, before he is aware, I shall enter this garden and wait. Then when he arrives, I shall win him over with embraces and bodily contact, so that he shall be in my power.' Having deliberated thus, she turned back and entered the city. And that day she did not go to Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>'s garden.

body.text:
Sva Roy 33-35
[16] pracaṇḍo 'py amātyaḥ sve udyāne tām udīkṣamānaś ciraṃ parikhinnaḥ sūryasyāṣṭaṅgamanakālasamaye nagaraṃ praviṣṭas tena sve gṛhe kāśisundaryā dūto 'nupreṣitaḥ kim arthaṃ tvam adya mamodyānaṃ nāgateti | kāśisundarī dārikā vyākṣepaṃ kṛtavatī āryaputrādya me śirorujātīva bādhate yenodyānaṃ nāgateti | mitrāmitramadhyamo lokas tasyāpareṇākhyātaṃ | na tasyāḥ śirorujā bādhate 'pi tv eṣā suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya sakāśam udyānaṃ gatā | tasmād udyānān mayā pratyāgacchantī dṛṣṭeti | śrutvā pracaṇḍasyāmātyasya krodhaparyavasthānam utpannaṃ | tataḥ saṃlakṣayati tādṛśam anarthaṃ kariṣyāmi | yathā śvaḥ kāśisundarī dārikā na bhaviṣyati | suvarṇavarṇaś ca kumāra iti | pratikruṣṭaṃ caitad vairāṇāṃ yad uta strīvairam iti | sa krodhāgninā dahyamānahṛdayas tān niśāṃ kṛcchreṇātināmitavān | tataḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām anyatamam āptapuruṣam āmantrayate | khaḍgam gṛhāṇa rājagṛhād bahir udyānaṃ gamiṣyāmi tatrāsti me kiñcid ātyayikaṃ prayojanam ity evaṃ svāminn iti sa puruṣaḥ khaḍgam ādāya tasya pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhas tataḥ pracaṇḍo 'mātyas tena puruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ rājagrān nirgatya divākarasya sārthavāhasyodyānaṃ praviśyāvasthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, waiting for her in his garden, was distressed after a long time. At sunset, he entered the city and sent a messenger to <s>Kāśisundarī</s> at his own house: 'Why did you not come to my garden today?' <s>Kāśisundarī</s> made an excuse: 'Noble lord, today a headache has been troubling me, which is why I did not come to the garden.' The world, being friend, foe, and neutral, told him through another: 'She has no headache. Rather, she went to the garden where Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> was. I saw her coming back from that garden.' Hearing this, a fit of anger arose in Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>. Then he resolved: 'I shall bring about such a calamity that tomorrow neither <s>Kāśisundarī</s> nor Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> shall exist.' It is well proclaimed that of all enmities, enmity over a woman is the most bitter. With his heart burning with the fire of anger, he passed that night with great difficulty. Then, when dawn broke, he summoned a trusted servant: 'Take a sword. I shall go to the garden outside <s>Rājagṛha</s>. I have some urgent business there.' 'Yes, master,' the man said, took the sword, and followed behind him. Then Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, together with that man, left <s>Rājagṛha</s> and entered the garden of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, where he stationed himself.

body.text:
Sva Roy 36,1 - 39,1
[17] kāśisundary api dārikā vicitravastrālaṅkārālaṅkṛtaśarīrā rājagṛān nāgarān nirgatya divākarasya sārthavāhasyodyānaṅ gatā | sā tatra praviṣṭā yāvat paśyati pracaṇḍam amātyaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃtrastā | saṃlakṣayaty eṣa prakṛtyaiva pracaṇḍo niyataṃ me 'dya mahāntam anarthaṅ karotīti pratinivarttitukāmābhūt | tataḥ pracaṇḍo 'mātyas tāṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhāgnijvalitamanās triśikhāṃ lalāṭe bhṛkurṭiṃ kṛtvā pradhāvitas tatas tāṃ sarabhasaṃ keśeṣu gṛhītvā nirdayam avāṅmukhīṃ pṛthivyāṃ pātayitvā samākṛṣṭavān evañ cāha tvam ihāgatya suvarṇavarṇena kumāreṇa sārddhaṃ paricārayasi | mama caivaṅ kathayasi | śirorujātīva me bādhate | yena tvatsakāśaṇ nāgateti | tad adya te tādṛśam maryādābandhāṃ karomi yena punar na bhavatī jīvalokaṃ drakṣyati | suvarṇavarṇena kumāreṇa sārddhaṃ paricārayiṣyāmīti | tac chrutvā kāśisundarī dārikā tadākarṣaṇaparākarṣaṇajaṃ duḥkham agaṇayitvā maraṇabhayabhītā bāṣpoparuddhyamānagadagadakaṇṭhī hā idānīn na bhaviṣyāmīti | kampamānagātrī pracaṇḍasyāmātyasya pādayor nipatya karuṇadīnavilamvitair akṣarair uvāca prasīdatv āryaputro nārhasi māṃ praghātayitum iti nityāparādho mātṛgrāmaḥ | itaḥ prabhṛti na bhūya evaṅ kariṣyāmi | yāvajjīvan te dāsī bhaviṣyāmi | tad alam anena sāhasena prayaccha jīvitam iti | tasya durātmana evaṃ karuṇadīnavilamvitair akṣarair ucyamānasya krodhāgnir vardhata eva | tatas taṃ sahāyakam uvāca śīghram asyā anena khaḍgenotkṛttamūlaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā pṛthivyān nipātayety ||
body.translated_text: The courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, too, her body adorned with various garments and ornaments, departed from the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and went to the garden of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. Having entered, she saw Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, and upon seeing him, she was terrified. She reflected: 'He is fierce by nature. Surely today he will bring great calamity upon me.' She wished to turn back. Then Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, upon seeing her, his mind blazing with the fire of anger, furrowing his brows into three ridges on his forehead, rushed forward and seized her roughly by the hair. Mercilessly throwing her face-down on the ground, he dragged her and said: 'You come here and consort with Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>! And to me you say: "A headache is troubling me, which is why I did not come to you." Today I shall impose such a punishment on you that the lady shall never again see the world of the living, nor consort with Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>!' Hearing this, <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, disregarding the pain caused by being dragged back and forth, frightened by the fear of death, her voice choked and stuttering with tears, crying 'Alas, now I shall be no more!'—her limbs trembling, she fell at Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>'s feet and spoke in pitiful, wretched, faltering syllables: 'May the noble lord be pleased! You should not have me killed! The female sex is always at fault. From now on, I will never do this again. I shall be your servant as long as I live. Enough of this violence—grant me my life!' But as she spoke these pitiful, wretched, faltering words, the fire of anger in that evil-minded one only grew stronger. Then he said to his companion: 'Quickly, cut off her head at the root with this sword and cast it upon the ground!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 39,1 - 43,2
[18] atha sa puruṣas tasya durātmano 'nyāyavaco duraktam upaśrutya kampitum ārabdhaḥ | cintayati ca | aho nairghṛṇyam eṣā hi strī bahuprakāram asyopayuktā | tat kathan nāma svalpasyāparādhasyārthe praghātayitum icchati | aho vayam api jīvikābhayabhītā yena nāmāsyāśīviṣaprakhyasya puruṣādhamasya pārṣve tiṣṭhāmaḥ | sarvathāhaṃ mahāsaṅkaṭam anupraviṣṭaḥ | kim atra prāptakālaṃ atha vā sphuṭam enaṃ vakṣyāmi kadācid eva sphuṭam ucyamānaḥ pratinivartetāsmāt pāpakād asaddharmād iti | viditvā samvignamanās tasyāś ca striyās tair atikaruṇair vilāpair dravīkṛtasantāno bāṣpāmbupariplutaq_īkṣaṇaḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ pracaṇḍam amātyam uvāca | prasīdatu svāmī nārhasi mām evaṃvidhe 'kārye niyojayitun nāhaṃ niṣādo nāpi vadhyaghātakaḥ kathaṃ hi nāma yat karmma vadhyaghātakānām api notsahate manas tatkarmaṇi pratārayati māṃ svāmī | eṣā ca strī prakāśātyartham abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvakalābhijñā rājagṛhanivāsino nānādigdeśābhyāgatasya ca vidagdhajanasyātīva vallabhā | sāmānyam idaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ratisthānaṃ | kathaṃ hi nāma svāmin prajñātamanuṣyasya vicakṣaṇasyāsminn anunayasthāne dveṣa utpannas tad alam īdṛśena lokadvayavirudhāvāhakena vyavasāyena | prasīda nārhasi mām ātmanañ cānena duścaritāgninā dagdhum | api ca svāmin |
body.translated_text: Then that man, hearing the unjust and wicked words of that evil-minded one, began to tremble. He thought: 'Oh, what cruelty! This woman has served him in so many ways. How can he wish to have her killed for such a small offense? Alas, we too, frightened by fear for our livelihood, stand at the side of this vilest of men, like a poisonous serpent. In any case, I have entered a great predicament. What is the right thing to do now? Perhaps I shall speak frankly to him. Perhaps, being spoken to frankly, he may turn away from this evil and unrighteous deed.' Realizing this, with an agitated mind, his heart melted by the woman's exceedingly pitiful laments, his eyes flooded with tears, with hands joined in reverence, he said to Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>: 'May the master be pleased! You should not employ me in such a deed. I am not a hunter nor an executioner. How can it be that the master commands me to perform a deed that even executioners' hearts would not endure? This woman is manifestly exceedingly beautiful, lovely, and pleasing, skilled in all arts, and most beloved of the cultured people dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> and coming from various regions and countries. This is a common place of pleasure for all people. How can it be, master, that in one who is recognized as wise and discerning, hatred has arisen in this place of affection? Enough of this enterprise that leads to ruin in both worlds! Be pleased! You should not burn yourself and me with this fire of misconduct. Moreover, master:

body.text: eṣā hi sukumārāṅgī rūpayauvanaśālinī |

children.text: prītim etām manuṣyāṇāṃ manye mārtimatīm iva |1|
children.translated_text: I consider her to be joy incarnate among mankind. |1|

children.text: karuṇaiḥ karuṇair dīnair madhurair akṣarair iyaṃ |
children.translated_text: With pitiful, pitiful, wretched, and sweet syllables, she—

children.text: vijñapayati svāmiṃs te dṛṇāti mama mānasaṃ |2|
children.translated_text: She petitions: 'My lord, your words pierce my heart. [2]

children.text: kampate hṛdayam me 'dya śrutvā dīptaṃ vacas tava |
children.translated_text: My heart trembles today, having heard your fierce words;

children.text: ko 'sau nirghṛṇacittaḥ syād ya imāṃ hantum edhate |3|
children.translated_text: Who could be so merciless of mind as to endeavor to kill her? [3]

children.text: mlecchā api naināṃ hantum utsahante sunirghṛṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even barbarians, utterly merciless, would not dare to kill her;

children.text: kathan nu mama tāṃ hantuṃ svāmin utsahate manaḥ |4|
children.translated_text: How then, my lord, can your mind dare to kill her? [4]

children.text: paśūnām api yāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavaty anunayo mahān |
children.translated_text: Even animals, upon seeing her, feel great tenderness;

children.text: tasyāḥ ko manuṣyo bhūtvā śastreṇa prahariṣyati |5|
children.translated_text: Who, having become a human being, would strike her with a weapon? [5]

children.text: tat prasīda tavāyuktam api śrotum idam vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, be gracious—it is improper even to hear these words,

children.text: prāg eva acarituṃ svāmin karmmedam atidāruṇam iti |6|
children.translated_text: Much less to carry out this exceedingly cruel deed, my lord.' [6]

children.text:
Sva Roy 43,2 - 45,46
[19] atha sa durātmā vipannāśayatvād evam api hṛdayagrāhakair vacobhis tena puruṣeṇābhidhiyamāno naiva svacittaṃ pratilabhate || saroṣabhrūlatābhaṅgaraudreṇa ca mukhena taṃ puruṣam uvāca || bhoḥ puruṣa kas tavāsyāṃ upary anunayo yan nāma madīyām ājñāṃ vilaṅghya necchasy enāṃ praghātayituṃ sarvathā yadi tvam enāṃ praghātayiṣyasīty evaṃ kuśalan no cen na praghātayiṣyasi tavādya jīvitaṃ ca bhaviṣyatīti | tato 'sau puruṣas tasya tat karkaśaṃ vyavasāyaṃ buddhvā bhītaś cintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | aho paramaśaṅkaṭam anupraviṣṭo 'smi | sa ced asyājñāṃ na kariṣyāmi niyatam adya māṃ jīvitād vyaparopayiṣyati | yo hi nāmaivaṃvidhiṃ mātṛgrāmaṃ bahuprakāram upayuktaṃ praghātayitum udyataḥ sa māṃ na praghātayiṣyatīti | kuta etat kathañ ca nāma manuṣyo 'ham ity ātmānam manye | īdṛśyā janapadakalyāṇinyāḥ striyāḥ śarīre śastraṃ nipātayiṣyāmi | sarvathā kāmaṃ svajīvitavināśo na tv evāsyāḥ prahāraṃ dāsyāmīti niścayaṃ kṛtavāṃs tasya buddhir utpannā yady ahaṃ khaḍgam ādāya niṣpalāyeyaṃ evaṃ mayā tv ātmā parirakṣito bhaviṣyati | kāśisundarī dāriketi | sa khaḍgam ādāya tasmād udyānād niṣkramya sarvajavena niḥpalānaḥ | pracaṇḍo py amātyas tasya pṛṣṭhato dvārakoṣṭhaṃ yāvad anubaddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: [19] Then that wicked man, due to his depraved disposition, even though being addressed with such heart-seizing words by that man, did not recover his senses at all. With a face made terrible by the knitting of angry brows, he said to that man: 'Fellow! What concern of yours is she, that you dare transgress my order and refuse to have her killed? By all means, if you will kill her, very well; but if you will not kill her, today your life shall be forfeited.' Then that man, understanding his harsh determination, became frightened and began to think: 'Alas, I have entered into an extremely difficult situation. If I do not carry out his order, he will certainly take my life today. For one who is prepared to have killed a woman of such kind, who has been enjoyed in many ways—he will surely not hesitate to kill me. How could it be otherwise? And how can I, considering myself a human being, bring down a weapon upon the body of such a beautiful woman, the jewel of the land? By all means, let my own life be destroyed rather than that I should ever strike her.' Having made this resolve, an idea arose in him: 'If I were to take the sword and flee, then I would have saved myself—and also the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>.' He took the sword and, rushing out of that garden at full speed, fled. The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> too pursued him from behind as far as the entrance gate.

body.translated_text: For she has delicate limbs, graced with beauty and youth;

body.text:
Sva Roy 46,1 - 48,49
[20] tataḥ kāśisundarī dārikā gatapratyāgataprāṇam ivātmānam manyamano tvaritatvaritam utthāya niḥpalāyāmīti prākārasamīpam abhigatā | sā coccaḥ prākāraṃ na śaknoti vilaṅghayituṃ | pracaṇḍaś cāmātyaḥ pratinivṛtya yāvat tasmin pradeśe kāśisundarīṃ dārikān na paśyati | itaś cāmutaś ca vyavalokayitum ārabdho yāvat paśyati prākārasamīpam abhigatāṃ sa tvaritatvaritaṃ tasyāḥ samīpaṃ gantum ārabdhaḥ | tatra ca kṛṣṇasarppo 'vasthitaḥ | tena sā dakṣiṇe caraṇe daṣṭā sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣpalānaḥ | kāśisundarī dārikā saṃlakṣayati | eṣaḥ ca pracaṇḍo mām āgatya praghātayiṣyatīti | tadgatamānasā maraṇabhayatrastā na vijānāti | yathāhaṃ kṛṣṇasarpeṇa daṣṭeti | pracaṇḍaś cāmātyas tam atimuktakalatāgahanam anuprāptaḥ | tatas tena durātmanā nirghṛṇahṛdayena tīvradveṣaparyākulīkṛtamanasā kāśisundarīṃ dārikāṃ tasmād atimuktakalatāgahanād ākṛṣya tasyāḥ śirasi pārṣṇiprahāro dattaḥ | sukumārā sā strī tena prahāreṇa viṣavegena ca mūrcchitā pracaṇḍo 'py amātyas tān nirīkṣitum ārabdho yāvat paśyati niśceṣṭāṃ bhūmau nipatitāṃ tasyaitad abhavan mṛteyam idānīṃ gacchāmīti | tataś ca māṃ mā kaścid drakṣyatīti | prākāraṃ vilaṅghyānyena pathā rājagṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tena praviśya rājapuruṣāḥ samājñāptā | gacchata divākarasya sārthavāhasyodyānaṃ pratyavekṣadhvam iti | te saṃprasthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: [20] Then the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, thinking herself to be as if with life gone and returned, hastily rose up and fled toward the enclosure wall. But she was unable to leap over the high wall. The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, having turned back, did not see the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> at that spot. He began looking here and there, and then saw her near the wall. He began to go quickly toward her. A black serpent was stationed there, and it bit her on the right foot. Seeing it, he fled. The girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> thought: 'This <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> will come and kill me.' With her mind fixed on that, terrified by fear of death, she did not realize that she had been bitten by a black serpent. The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> reached the thicket of <s>atimuktaka</s> creepers. Then that wicked man, merciless of heart, his mind agitated by intense hatred, dragged the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> from that thicket of <s>atimuktaka</s> creepers and struck her on the head with a heel-blow. She, a delicate woman, fainted from that blow and the force of the poison. The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> too began to look at her, and saw her lying motionless on the ground. He thought: 'She is dead now; I shall leave, and let no one see me.' Leaping over the wall, he entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> by another path. Having entered, he commanded the king's men: 'Go to the garden of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> and investigate.' They set out.

body.text:
Sva Roy 49,1 - 50,5
[21] suvarṇavarṇaś ca kumāro rājagṛhān niṣkramya svam udyānam anuprāptaḥ | yāvat paśyati kāśisundarīṃ dārikām itaś cāmutaś ca samāhṛṣṭāṃ muktakeśīṃ niśceṣṭāṃ bhūmau nipatitāṃ dṛṣṭvā cāsya mahāsamvega utpannaḥ | tenopalakṣitaṃ kenāpy eṣā durātmanā nirghṛṇahṛdayena tyaktaparalokena vairānubaddhenāhānīya praghātitā bhaviṣyati | dhik kaṣṭam īdṛśā api nāma sattvā bhavanti | ya evaṃvidhe mātṛgrāme nirdayāḥ praharantīti | tena tad udyānaṃ sarvaṃ pratyavekṣitaṃ yāvan na kiñcit paśyati tasyaiva tad abhavad eṣā strī prajñātā 'sminn udyāne praghātitā | atra na kiñcit paśyāmi | sarvathā durātmanā kenāpi svadaurātmyam antargataṃ prakaṭīkurvatā mana mastake 'yaśo 'śanir nipātita iti | sa caivaṃ samvignamanāḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: [21] The prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, having left <s>Rājagṛha</s>, arrived at his own garden. There he saw the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, disheveled here and there, with hair loose, motionless, lying fallen on the ground. Upon seeing her, a great sense of urgency arose in him. He perceived: 'Some wicked person with a merciless heart, one who has abandoned concern for the next world, driven by enmity, must have brought her here and killed her. Alas, how terrible! There are indeed such beings who are merciless enough to strike such a woman.' He searched the entire garden but saw nothing. He then thought: 'This well-known woman has been killed in this garden. I see nothing here. Surely some wicked person, making manifest his inner villainy, has brought down the thunderbolt of infamy upon my head.' Thus, with an agitated mind, resting his cheek on his hand, he stood absorbed in thought.

body.text:
Sva Roy 50,5 - 52,3
[22] te ca rājapuruṣāḥ saṃprāptaḥ | praviśya ca tad udyānaṃ pratyavekṣitum ārabdhāḥ | yāvat paśyanti kāśisundarīṃ dārikām itaś cāmutaś ca samāhṛṣṭāṃ muktakeśīṃ niśceṣṭāṃ bhūmau nipatitāṃ | dṛṣṭvā suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya pūrvakarmavipākasāmarthyān na tāṃ kaścit paricchinatti | yatheyaṃ mūrcchiteti | kintarhi kālagateti | tatas te rājapuruṣāḥ parasparam ūcuḥ | bhavantaḥ eṣā strī kenāpi praghātiteti | tais tad udyānaṃ sarvaṃ pratyavekṣitaṃ | suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ muktvā na kañcid anyaṃ paśyanti | taiḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ pṛṣṭaḥ | kumāra eṣā strī kena praghātiteti | sa kathayati bhavanto 'ham api na jāne mayāpy eṣā eva dṛṣṭeti |
body.translated_text: [22] Those king's men arrived and, entering the garden, began to investigate. They saw the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, disheveled here and there, with hair loose, motionless, lying fallen on the ground. Upon seeing her, due to the power of the ripening of the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>'s past <s>karma</s>, none of them discerned that she was merely unconscious; rather, they concluded she was dead. Then those king's men said to one another: 'Sirs, this woman has been killed by someone.' They searched the entire garden. Apart from the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, they saw no one else. They asked the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>: 'Prince, by whom was this woman killed?' He said: 'Sirs, I too do not know. I too found her in just this condition.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 52,3 - 54,5
[23] atha te rājapuruṣāḥ parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | bhavanta eṣa kumāro 'tyantavinīto nāsyedaṃ karma saṃbhāvyate | atra ca na kañcid anyaṃ paśyāmaḥ sarvathā paramasaṅkaṭam anupraviṣṭāḥ smaḥ | kathamatra pratipatavyam iti | tatraikaḥ kathayati | bhavanto na vayaṃ paricchettuṃ samarthā | etāṃ striyaṃ kumārañ ca karaṇamaṇḍapaṃ nayāmas tatrāmātyā eva paricchetsyantīti | tatas te rājapuruṣās tāṃ striyaṃ śivikām āropya suvarṇavarṇañ ca kumāram ādāya karaṇamaṇḍapaṅ gatās tatra ca karaṇamaṇḍape pracaṇḍo 'mātyaḥ pratipattyaivānukūlair vyavahāribhiḥ sārddhaṃ sanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt | sannipatito yadbhūyasā tān eva rājapuruṣān āgamayamānas tena te dūrata eva dṛṣṭāḥ | pṛṣṭāś ca bhavantaḥ kim idam iti | tair ākhyātam eṣāsmābhiḥ strī divārakasya sārthavāhasyodyāne kālagatā dṛṣṭā tañ codyānam asmābhiḥ pratyavekṣitatam | suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ muktvā na kañcid anyaṃ paśyāmaḥ eṣa cāsmābhiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kumāraḥ | iyaṃ strī kena praghātiteti | anenākhyātam aham api bhavanto na jāne mayāpy eṣā evam eva dṛṣṭeti | tad idānīṃ svāmina evaṃ pravicārayantv iti |
body.translated_text: [23] Then those king's men began to deliberate among themselves: 'Sirs, this prince is extremely well-mannered; such a deed is not to be attributed to him. And we see no one else here. We have entered into an extremely difficult situation. What should be done here?' One of them said: 'Sirs, we are not able to determine the matter. Let us take this woman and the prince to the court of justice; the ministers themselves will decide.' Then those king's men, placing the woman on a palanquin and taking the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, went to the court of justice. There in the court, the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> was already seated, deliberately, with sympathetic officials around him. He had gathered there, for the most part, awaiting those very king's men. He saw them from afar and asked: 'Sirs, what is this?' They reported: 'This woman was found dead by us in the garden of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. We searched that garden; apart from the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, we see no one else. We asked this prince: "By whom was this woman killed?" He said: "I too, sirs, do not know. I too found her in just this condition." So now let the lords themselves investigate.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 54,5 - 56,4
[24] pracaṇḍo 'mātyaḥ kathayati | bhavanto mūhūrtaṃ tāvad avīkṣadhvaṃ yāvad ahaṃ rājño nivedayāmīti | tena rājño 'jātaśatror gṛhaṃ gatvā daurvārikaḥ puruṣaḥ pṛṣṭo bhoḥ puruṣadevaḥ kiṃ karotīti | tenākhyātam upariprāsādatalagato niḥpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati | labdhapraṇayo 'sau tena pratihārī preṣitā gaccha devasya nivedayāmātyā vijñapayanti | divākarasya sārthavāhasya putreṇodyāne kāśisundarī dārikā praghātitā | sa ca na_ubhyupagacchati | katham atrāsmābhiḥ pratipattavyam iti | tayā gatvā rājño niveditaṃ rājā tatra ratikrīḍāyām atīva śaktaḥ kathayati | gacchāmātyān evam vada yūyam evaṃ nipuṇaṃ pravicārayadhvam iti | tayā nirgatya pracaṇḍasyāmātyasya niveditam evaṃ devaḥ samājñāpayatīti |
body.translated_text: [24] The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> said: 'Sirs, wait a moment while I inform the king.' He went to the palace of King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> and asked the doorkeeper: 'Fellow, what is the king doing?' He replied: 'He has gone to the upper floor of the palace and is enjoying himself with instrumental music, without attendants, delighting and making merry.' Having gained audience, a female messenger was sent: 'Go, inform the king that the ministers report: the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> has been killed in the garden by the son of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. And he does not confess. What should we do in this matter?' She went and informed the king. The king, being deeply engrossed in that amorous play, said: 'Go, tell the ministers: you yourselves investigate the matter carefully.' She went out and informed the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>: 'Thus the king commands.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 56,4 - 58,4
[25] tataḥ pracaṇḍo 'mātyaḥ karaṇamaṇḍapam āgatya tān rājapuruṣān uvāca | gacchata bhavanto vadhyaghātakān āhūyateti | tair āhūtāḥ pracaṇḍo 'mātyo vadhyaghātakān uvāca | bhavanto 'nena kumāreṇeyaṅ kāśisundarī dārikā udyāne praghātitā | gacchatainaṃ durācāraṃ paścād bāhubandhanaṃ gāḍhaṃ kṛtvā kharasvareṇa paṭena vādyamānena rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu śravaṇamukheṣv anuśrāvya dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa nirṇamayya mahāśmaśān nītvā śūle samāropayata mṛtañ cainaṃ kāśisundaryā dārikayā sahaikāñ citām āropya dhyāpayateti | atha te vadhyaghātakāḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram atyartham abhirūpam uttaptasuvarṇaparvvataśṛṅgam iva paramayā śriyā jvalantam udvīkṣya samvignāḥ parasparam ūcuḥ | bhavantaḥ kiñcāpi vayam vadhyaghātakās tat katham īdṛśamatidurllabhadarśanaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṃ praghātayiṣyāmaḥ | sarvathā kāmam asmākaṃ svajīvitavināśo na tv evainaṃ praghātayiṣyāmaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: [25] Then the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, having come to the court of justice, addressed those king's men: 'Go, sirs, summon the executioners.' They were summoned. The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> addressed the executioners: 'Sirs, this girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> has been killed in the garden by this prince. Go, bind this evildoer tightly with his arms behind his back, and with a harsh-voiced drum being beaten, proclaim his crime through the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections, at every hearing point. Then lead him out through the southern city gate, take him to the great cremation ground, and impale him on a stake. And having placed this dead man together with the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> on a single pyre, cremate them.' Then those executioners, looking up at the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, who was exceedingly handsome, blazing with supreme splendor like the peak of a mountain of refined gold, were moved with compassion and said to one another: 'Sirs, although we are executioners, how can we kill such an extraordinarily rare and exceptional man? By all means, let our own lives be destroyed rather than that we should ever kill him.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 58,4 - 61,4
[26] pracaṇḍo 'mātyas tān parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurvāṇāṅ dṛṣṭvā pṛcchati | bhavantaḥ kiṃ sthīyate | śīghramenaṃ nayatheti | te kṛtāñjalayo vijñapayitum ārabdhāḥ | prasīda svāmin | kiñcāpi vayam vadhyaghātakā api notsahāmahe īdṛśaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṃ mahājanavallabhaṃ praghātayitum iti | pracaṇḍo 'mātyaḥ kupitaḥ kathayati | bhavanto yadi yūyam enaṃ na praghātayiṣyatha | yuṣmākam evādya saputrakalatrabāndhavānāṃ jīvitāni na bhaviṣyantīti | te santrastāḥ parasparam ūcuḥ | bhavanto 'syāmātyasyānyāyānurūpo vyavahāraḥ | yo hi nāma suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram evam atidurlabhadarśanaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṃ parityaktum udyataḥ yo 'smān saputrakalatrabandhavān praghātayiṣyatīti | kuta etat | tad atisaṅkaṭam anupraviṣṭāḥ smaḥ | katham atra pratipattavyam iti | teṣāṃ maraṇabhayabhītānāṃ buddhir utpannā | eṣā kumāro mahājanavallbhas tad enan tāvad vīthīm avatarāmaḥ | sthānam etad vidyate yan mahājanakāya evainaṃ pratimocayiṣyati | ko hy enaṃ praghātyamānam upekṣituṃ samartha iti | te tasya samīpam upasṛṣṭāḥ | paścād bāhum enam badhnīma iti | tañ ca tathā rūpaudāryasampadā vibhrājamānam ālokya na śaknuvanti spraṣṭuṃ tato vepamānāṅgapratyaṅgā bāṣpoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhāḥ kranditum ārabdhāḥ | hā kaṣṭam īdṛśā api vayaṃ pāpakarmakāriṇo yenaivamvidhe kārye niyojyāmahe iti |
body.translated_text: [26] The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, seeing them deliberating among themselves, asked: 'Sirs, why do you delay? Take him away quickly.' They, with folded hands, began to petition: 'Be gracious, my lord. Although we are executioners, we cannot bring ourselves to kill such an exceptional man, beloved of the people.' The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, angered, said: 'Sirs, if you will not kill him, then today your own lives, together with those of your sons, wives, and relatives, shall be forfeited.' They, terrified, said to one another: 'Sirs, the conduct of this minister is unjust. He who is prepared to have the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, such an extraordinarily rare and exceptional man, put to death—he will surely kill us together with our sons, wives, and relatives. How could it be otherwise? We have entered into an extremely difficult situation. What should be done here?' Stricken with fear of death, an idea arose in them: 'This prince is beloved of the people. Let us therefore take him down into the streets. There is a possibility that the great multitude itself will free him. For who would be able to stand by while he is being put to death?' They approached him to bind his arms behind his back. But looking upon him, radiant with the excellence of beauty and form, they were unable to touch him. Then, trembling in all their limbs and parts, with voices choked by tears, they began to wail: 'Alas, how terrible! We too are doers of evil deeds, that we should be employed in such a task!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 61,4 - 64,2
[27] tataḥ pracaṇḍenāmātyena bhūyaḥ sakarkaśam ājñaptāḥ kim parivilambadhve | te santrastāḥ sakāśam abhyupagatāḥ | tair asau bāṣpāmbupariplutekṣaṇair vepamānair gṛhītas tenaiva suvarṇapītena vastreṇa paścād bāhuko baddhaḥ | tañ ca paścād bāhugāḍhabandhanabaddham ālokya pracaṇḍam amātyaṃ muktvā sarva eva karaṇamaṇḍapastho janakāyas tadviyogamanyudravīkṛtasantāno 'śrūṇi prapātayitum ārabdho hā kaṣṭam idānīm eva durlabhadarśanaḥ kumāro na bhaviṣyatīti | tatas tair vadhyaghātakair vīthyām avatārito yathāsminn antare kolāhalo jātas tañ ca kolāhalam upaśrutya sastrīpuruṣadārakadārikā rājagṛhanivāsīnānādigdeśābhyāgataś ca janakāyaḥ sannipatitaḥ | suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ paścād bāhugāḍhabandhanabaddham ālokya samvignamanāḥ sasambhramaṃ praṣṭum ārabdha | bhavantaḥ kim idam iti | tatas te vadhyaghātakāḥ bāṣpoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhāḥ krandanta ūcuḥ | bhavanto 'nena kumāreṇa kila kāśisundarī dārikā praghātiteti vadhāya parityakto rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv anuśrāvyate | na cirād eva mahāśmaśānaṃ nītvā praghātyata iti |
body.translated_text: [27] Then the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> commanded them again harshly: 'Why do you delay?' They, terrified, approached him. With eyes overflowing with tears, trembling, they seized him with that same golden-yellow garment and bound his arms behind his back. Seeing him bound tightly with his arms behind his back, everyone present in the court hall, except the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, their hearts melted with grief at the separation from him, began to shed tears: 'Alas, what misery! Now the prince, so rare to behold, shall be no more!' Then the executioners led him down into the street. At that moment a tumult arose, and hearing that tumult, the people of <s>Rājagṛha</s>—men, women, boys, and girls—along with people who had come from various other regions, assembled. Seeing prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> bound tightly with his arms behind his back, with agitated hearts they began to ask anxiously: 'Good sirs, what is this?' Then the executioners, their voices choked with sobs, weeping, said: 'Good sirs, this prince, it is said, has killed the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>—he has been condemned to death and is being proclaimed through the streets, roads, crossroads, and intersections. Before long, he will be taken to the great cremation ground and executed.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 64,2 - 66,4
[28] tac chrutvā sa mahājanakāyas tadviyogaduḥkhābhyāhata ekaraveṇoccair vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | hā hā katham ayaṃ kumāra evamabhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopeta uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ sarvajanamanonayanaharaḥ | paṇḍito vinītaḥ peśalo dakṣaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmmakāmaḥ sattvavatsalaḥ praghātyate | kim astaṅgatāḥ sādhavaḥ kim antarhito dharmaḥ kim adharmasyaiva niḥsapatnaṃ rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ | dhik kaṣṭam bhoḥ |
body.translated_text: [28] Hearing this, that great crowd, stricken by the grief of separation from him, began to cry out aloud in a single roar: 'Alas, alas! How can this prince, so handsome, beautiful, charming, endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs, possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold, captivating the minds and eyes of all people—learned, well-mannered, eloquent, skillful, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward beings—be executed? Have the virtuous disappeared? Has <s>Dharma</s> been concealed? Has the unchallenged sovereignty and dominion of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) alone arrived? Fie, what misery, alas!'

body.text: rūpalāvaṇyasampadbhir uttamābhir alaṅkṛtaṃ |

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā yam asmākaṃ parā prītir abhūt purā |1|
children.translated_text: Seeing whom again and again, supreme delight arose in us before— [1]

children.text: tam enaṃ sāmprataṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyaghātair adhiṣṭhitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Seeing that very one now, attended by executioners,
Our hearts, overcome by intense grief, seem about to burst. [2]
He who was dear to the great multitude because he captivated minds and eyes—

children.text: tasyopari kathan nāma rājñā daṇḍo nipātyate |3|
children.translated_text: How can punishment be inflicted upon such a one by the king? [3]

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā yan nityaṃ tṛptin nāyānti dehinaḥ |
children.translated_text: He at whom beings gaze constantly and are never satisfied—

children.text: vadhāya sa kathaṃ tyakto ghṛṇā tyaktādya mantribhiḥ |4|
children.translated_text: How has he been condemned to death? Compassion has been abandoned today by the ministers. [4]

children.text: cāritryaṃ vinayopetaṃ yasya khyātaṃ muner iva |
children.translated_text: He whose conduct, endowed with discipline, was renowned like that of a sage—

children.text: kathaṃ saṃbhāvyate tasya hy aparādho 'yam īdṛśaḥ |5|
children.translated_text: How can such an offense be attributed to him? [5]

children.text: adharmo vata jāgarti dharmaḥ supto 'tha vā mṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Truly <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is awake, and <s>Dharma</s> is asleep or dead,

children.text: yad evaṃ guṇino 'py asya viyogo 'yam upasthitaḥ |6|
children.translated_text: Since such a separation from one so endowed with virtues has come to pass. [6]

body.translated_text: Him who was adorned with the supreme endowments of beauty, grace, and splendor,

body.text:
Sva Roy 66,4 - 67,4
[29] sa ca strīṇāṃ atīva priyas tatra kāścit striyas tadviyogaduḥkhābhyāhatāḥ pṛthivyām āvartanaparivartanaṃ kurvanti | kāścid uras tāḍayanti | kāścit sammoham āpadyante | ekaikās tatra putraviyogasadṛśaṃ viyogaduḥkham anubhavanti sma | mahājanavallabho 'sau mahātmā rājagṛhanagaranivāsī janakāyo yadbhūyasā tadviyogaduḥkhābhyāhato vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | rājagṛhaṃ nagaram ākulākulaṃ jñāyate | tadviyogābhyāhataṅ kampata iti |
body.translated_text: [29] He was especially dear to the women. There, some women, stricken by the grief of separation from him, rolled back and forth upon the ground. Some beat their chests. Some fell into a swoon. Each and every one of them experienced grief of separation comparable to the loss of a son. That great-souled one, beloved of the multitude—the people dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, for the most part stricken by the grief of separation from him, began to cry out. The city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was in great commotion. Stricken by the grief of separation from him, it trembled.

body.text:
Sva Roy 67,4 - 69,1
[30] divākarasya sārthavāhasya gṛhād dārikā vīthīm avatīrṇā | tayā eṣa vṛttāntaḥ śrutas tataḥ krandamānā uras tāḍayantī tvaritatvaritaṃ gṛhaṃ gatvā yena suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya mātā tenopasaṃkrāntā upasaṃkramya tasyāḥ purata ātmānaṃ kṣiptavatī | tataḥ suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya mātā saṃtrastā pṛcchati | dārike kiṃ kathayasīti | sā uccair vikrośantī kathayitum ārabdhā | ārye suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ paścād bāhugāḍhabandhanabaddho vadhyaghātakair adhiṣṭhito 'nena kilodyāne kāśisundarī dārikā praghātitety avicāryaiva vadhāya parityakto rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv anuśrāvyate | na cirād eva mahāśmaśānaṃ nītvā praghātyata iti |
body.translated_text: [30] From the house of <s>Divākara</s> the caravan leader, a maidservant had gone down into the street. She heard this account. Then, weeping and beating her chest, she hurried as fast as she could to the house and approached the mother of prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>. Having approached, she threw herself down before her. Then the mother of prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, alarmed, asked: 'Girl, what are you saying?' She, crying out aloud, began to say: 'Noble lady! Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, bound tightly with his arms behind his back, attended by executioners—it is said that he killed the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> in the garden—without any inquiry he has been condemned to death and is being proclaimed through the streets, roads, crossroads, and intersections. Before long, he will be taken to the great cremation ground and executed!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 69,1 - 70,3
[31] tac chrutvā suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya mātā tīvraduḥkhābhyāhatā mūrcchitā bhūmau nipatitā | tato jalābhiṣekapratyāgataprāṇā utthāya hā putra hā putreti vikrośantī keśā luñcamānā uras tāḍayantī kampamānā muhur muhur moham upagacchantī gṛhān nirgatya vīthīm avatīrṇā | sā putraviyogaśokābhyāhatā viklavahṛdayā tattad vilapantī ekaikaṃ pṛcchati | katareṇa pathā suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro nīto bhaviṣyatīti | hā putrakaṃ na paśyāmi paritrāyadhvaṃ paritrāyadhvaṃ putrakam me darśayateti | viruvantī vīthīmadhyena saṃsthitā |
body.translated_text: [31] Hearing this, the mother of prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, stricken by intense grief, fainted and fell to the ground. Then, revived by a sprinkling of water, rising up, crying out 'O my son! O my son!', tearing her hair, beating her chest, trembling, falling into a swoon again and again, she went out from the house and descended into the street. She, stricken by the grief of separation from her son, her heart distraught, lamenting this and that, asked each person: 'By which road will prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> have been taken?' 'Alas, my little son! I cannot see him! Save him, save him! Show me my little son!' Wailing, she stood in the middle of the street.

body.text:
Sva Roy 70,3 - 73,3
[32] yathā yathā sārthavāhapatnī suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāran na paśyati | tathā tathā tīvrataraśokaduḥkhābhyāhatā uccair vikrośantī ekaikasya pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭī vijñāpayati | paritrāyadhvaṃ paritrāyadhvam me śīghram avakāśam anuprayacchata yāvat kumāro nātikramyate anena pathā | anena pathā putrako me suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro nīyate yathā ca taṃ paśyāmi tathā me prasādaṃ kartum arhatheti | sā ca tatrāvakāśam alabhamānā hā kathaṃ bhoḥ putra na labha iti | sarvāṅgikayā pṛthivyām ātmānaṃ kṣiptavatī | tato jaloddhṛteva matsī pṛthivyām āvarttanaparivartanaṅ kartum ārabdhā | hṛtapoteva kurarī karuṇakaruṇaṃ virauti sma | praṇaṣṭavatseva gaur bahuvidhahambhāravair vilapitā | hā putraka | hā priya | manapa | hā kānta | hā apratikūla | hā manorathaśatair labdha | hā abhirūpa darśanīya prāsādika | hā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopeta | hā uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgata | hā sarvajanamanonayanahara | hā sarvajanavallabha | hā netrānandakara | hā paṇḍita vinīta viśārada manojña dakṣa | hā karuṇika dharmakāma sattvavatsala | hā me kulodyotakara | hā me putrakulapradīpa | hā me hṛdayavallabha | hā me hṛdayasarvasva | hā me sārasamuccaya | hā me netrāmṛta | hā me prītinibandhana | hā me kuśalasarvasva | hā katham avicāryaivam anātho vadhāya nīyate sa iti |
body.translated_text: [32] The more the caravan leader's wife could not see prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, the more she was stricken by ever more intense grief and sorrow, and crying out aloud, falling at the feet of each person, with palms joined together, she implored: 'Save him, save him! Quickly give me passage so that the prince is not taken away by this road! By this road my little son, prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, is being led. Please be gracious to me so that I may see him!' And she, finding no passage there, cried: 'Alas, how, my lord, can I not reach my son!' She threw herself upon the ground with her whole body. Then, like a fish drawn from water, she began to roll back and forth upon the ground. Like a female osprey whose young has been seized, she wailed most piteously. Like a cow that has lost its calf, she lamented with many kinds of bellowing cries: 'O my little son! O my dear one! O beloved! O darling! O one never unkind! O one obtained through a hundred heart's desires! O handsome, beautiful, charming one! O one endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs! O one possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold! O captivator of the minds and eyes of all people! O one dear to all people! O bringer of delight to the eyes! O learned, well-mannered, accomplished, charming, skillful one! O compassionate, <s>Dharma</s>-loving, tender toward beings! O illuminator of my family! O lamp of my son's lineage! O darling of my heart! O everything to my heart! O essence of all that is precious to me! O nectar of my eyes! O foundation of my joy! O all my store of merit! O how, without any inquiry, is he, the helpless one, being led to execution!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 73,3 - 75,76
[33] punar api ca kṛtakarapuṭā paurān vijñapayantī | viklavahṛdayā provāca |
body.translated_text: [33] And again, with palms joined together, imploring the citizens, with distraught heart she spoke:

body.text: hā hatāsmi nirānandā kim idaṃ vartate mama |

children.text: svapno 'yam atha vā moha āhosvic cittavibhramaḥ |1|
children.translated_text: Is this a dream, or delusion, or a disturbance of the mind? [1]
That virtuous woman, her mind deranged by the intense grief of separation from her son,

children.text: paurān vijñāpayām āsa viruvantī muhur muhuḥ |2|
children.translated_text: Implored the citizens, wailing again and again: [2]

children.text: avinīto virūpo vā na ca me hṛdayapriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He is not undisciplined nor ill-favored, nor is he not dear to my heart—

children.text: yad evam adhyupekṣadhvaṃ nīyamānaṃ sutam mama |3|
children.translated_text: Yet you thus look on with indifference as my son is being led away! [3]

children.text: anukampā sa ced asti pakṣapāto guṇeṣu vā |
children.translated_text: If compassion exists, if there is partiality toward virtues,

children.text: tathā me kriyatāṃ paurā yathā paśyāmi putrakaṃ |4|
children.translated_text: Then, O citizens, act so that I may see my little son! [4]
Not yet today have I anointed him with sandalwood and other unguents,
Nor adorned him in many ways with gorocanā, armlets, and ornamental dots. [5]
With bracelets and other ornaments I have not adorned him,

children.text: na viśrabdha pariṣvakto bahuśo nāpi cumbitaḥ |6|
children.translated_text: Nor embraced him at ease, nor kissed him many times. [6]
He has not circumambulated me, nor has he made obeisance today—

children.text: evam eva kathan nāma nīyate bhoḥ suto mama |7|
children.translated_text: How then, alas, can my son be led away thus? [7]

children.text: śūnyā me 'dya diśaḥ sarvā vepate me kaḍevaraṃ |
children.translated_text: All directions are empty for me today; my body trembles;

children.text: dahyate hṛdayañ cāpi moham eti ca mānasaṃ |8|
children.translated_text: My heart is burning, and my mind falls into a swoon. [8]
Swiftly, swiftly he is led away by the cruel executioners—

children.text: hā hā na bhūyo drakṣyāmi sutaṃ hṛdayavallabhaṃ |9|
children.translated_text: Alas, alas! Never again shall I see my son, the darling of my heart! [9]

children.text: nūnaṃ kṛtan mayā pāpam anyajanmani dāruṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: Surely I committed terrible sins in another birth,
For I am thus burned by the grief of losing my son, as dry grass is burned by fire. [10]

children.text: yena satyena cittam me śatruṣv api na pāpakaṃ |
children.translated_text: By the truth that my mind harbors no evil even toward enemies,

children.text: mucyatāṃ vyasanād asmāt tena satyena me suta iti |11|
children.translated_text: By that truth, may my son be freed from this calamity!' [11]

body.translated_text: 'Alas, I am ruined, bereft of joy—what is happening to me?

body.text:
Sva Roy 76,1 - 77,5
[34] divākaraś ca sārthavāhaḥ samudrāt saṃsiddhayānpātro rājagṛham anuprāptaḥ | sa rājagṛhan nagaraṃ praviśan nimittāny apraśastāni paśyati | tasya hṛdayaṃ kampitum ārabdhaṃ aṅgāni sīditum ārabdhāni | netraṃ sphuritum ārabdhaṃ śakunayaś cāsya purataḥ kharam vāśitum ārabdhāḥ | sa nimittakuśalaḥ śakunirute ca kṛtavī cintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | yathaitāni nimittāny apraśastāni samanupaśyāmi dhruvam adya suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya mahān upadravaḥ samupasthito bhaviṣyati | tathā hy etāni nimittāni tadviyogaṃ sūcayantīty āha ca |
body.translated_text: [34] Now the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> had returned from the ocean with a successful voyage to <s>Rājagṛha</s>. As he was entering the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, he saw inauspicious omens. His heart began to tremble; his limbs began to grow weak. His eye began to twitch, and birds before him began to cry harshly. He, skilled in reading omens and versed in the cries of birds, began to reflect: 'As I observe these inauspicious omens, surely a great calamity has befallen prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> today. For these omens indicate separation from him.' And he spoke:

body.text: yathā sphurati netram me yathā rauti vihaṅgamaḥ |

children.translated_text: Surely separation from my son has come upon me today. [1]

children.text: yathā cāṅgāni sīdanti vepate hṛdayañ ca me |
children.translated_text: As my limbs grow weak and my heart trembles,
Surely a terrible separation from my son has arrived today.' [2]

body.translated_text: 'As my eye twitches and as the bird cries,

body.text:
Sva Roy 77,5 - 80,81
[35] sa evam anarthaśatasahasrāṇi cintayan sīdamānāṅgapratyaṅgaḥ | vepathur apragalbhapadasañcāraḥ kathañcid rājagṛham anupraviṣṭo yāvac chṛṇoti mahājanakāyasya krandanaśabdaṃ | sa tam ākrandanaśabdam anusaran vīthīm avatīrṇo yāvat paśyati mahājanakāyaṃ rākṣasopadrutam iva nagaraṃ viyogaduḥkhābhyāhataṃ krandamānaṃ tena sammukhāgato 'nyatamaḥ puruṣaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ | bhoḥ puruṣa kim idam iti | sa ca tan na jānāti yathāyam evāsau divākaraḥ sārthavāha iti | tenākhyātaṃ divākarasya sārthavāhasya putraḥ suvarṇavarṇo nāma kumāro 'tyantaṃ rūpādiguṇasampadā yuktas tena kilodyāne kāśisundarī dārikā praghātitety avicāryaiva vadhāya parityakto rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv aṇuśrāvyate | na cirād eva mahāśmaśānaṃ nītvā praghātyata iti | tac chrutvā divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ putraviyogaduḥkhābhyāhataḥ sahasaiva mūrcchito bhūmau nipatitaḥ | tato jalābhiṣekapratyāgataprāṇa utthāya bāṣpormitaraṅgāpūryamāṇavadanakamalaḥ sambhrāntaḥ sa nirīkṣamāṇa hā katareṇa pathā suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro nīto bhaviṣyatīti | vīthīmadhyena tvaritatvaritaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | yāvat paśyati tāvat paśyati bhāryāṃ muktakeśīm ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyām uras tāḍayantīṃ ārtasvaraṃ tat tadvilapantīṃ sutaviyogajāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanaāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punas tīvramanyūparuddhagadgadāyamānakaṇṭho bāṣpāmbupariplutekṣaṇas tasyāḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: [35] He, thus reflecting upon hundreds of thousands of calamities, with weakening limbs, trembling, with faltering steps, somehow entered <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Then he heard the wailing sound of the great crowd. Following that sound of lamentation, he descended into the street and saw the great crowd weeping, stricken by the grief of separation, as if the city were beset by <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons). He encountered a certain man face to face and asked: 'Good sir, what is this?' And that man did not know that this was <s>Divākara</s> the caravan leader himself. He told him: 'The son of <s>Divākara</s> the caravan leader, a prince named <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, supremely endowed with beauty and other virtuous qualities—it is said that he killed the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> in the garden—without any inquiry he has been condemned to death and is being proclaimed through the streets, roads, crossroads, and intersections. Before long, he will be taken to the great cremation ground and executed.' Hearing this, <s>Divākara</s> the caravan leader, stricken by the grief of separation from his son, suddenly fainted and fell to the ground. Then, revived by a sprinkling of water, rising up, his lotus-face flooded with waves of tears, bewildered, looking around—'Alas, by which road will prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> have been taken?'—he set off swiftly through the middle of the street.
