Then he saw—he saw his wife with hair disheveled, beating her chest with both hands, lamenting this and that in a voice of anguish, experiencing a grief born of separation from her son—intense, sharp, bitter, disagreeable. And seeing her, his throat choked by intense grief, his eyes overflowing with tears, he approached her.

body.text:
Sva Roy 81,2 - 83,5
[36] sā taṃ dṛṣṭvā dviguṇataraśokaśalyābhyāhata bāṣpormmitaraṅgāpūryamāṇavadanakamalā sasambhramā tvaritaṃ tvaritam utthāya tasya purata ātmānaṃ kṣiptavatī | sā tato divākareṇa sārthavāhenārtasvaraṃ krandamānā pariṣvajyotthāpitā | sā tasya pādayor nipatyovāca | sārthavāhaṃ paritrāyasva paritrāyasva putrabhikṣām me 'nuprayacchety āha ca |
body.translated_text: [36] She, seeing him, stricken by a grief doubled in intensity, her lotus-face flooded with waves of tears, anxiously and hurriedly rose up and threw herself before him. She, weeping and wailing in a voice of anguish, was then embraced and raised up by <s>Divākara</s> the caravan leader. Falling at his feet, she said: 'Caravan leader, save him, save him! Grant me the gift of my son!' And she spoke:

body.text: mandabhāgyāṃ nirānandā mām āśvāsaya sāṃprataṃ |

children.translated_text: Being separated from my son, wailing, deeply afflicted. [1]

children.text: yasya janmani te svāmin ānandaaḥ paramo 'bhavat |
children.translated_text: He at whose birth, O lord, your supreme joy arose—

children.text: sa eva māraṇāyādya nīyate vallabhaḥ sutaḥ |2|
children.translated_text: That very beloved son is now being led to his death. [2]
Well-mannered, eloquent, skillful, accomplished in many treatises,
And incomparable in beauty—my learned son is being led away. [3]
Your family lineage is being severed; your family tradition is being broken;
The illustrious lamp that illuminates your family is being extinguished.' [4]
This is the entirety of [my] heart, this is the bond of [my] joy;
this nectar of the eyes of men is being led away by the executioners! [5]

children.text: sarvam etad dhi kriyate etac cakṣur nirudhyate |
children.translated_text: All this is indeed being done — this eye is being obstructed;
the heart that is called 'son' — this is being torn out and taken away! [6]

children.text: tac chīghraṃ kriyatāṃ yatna[ḥ] sutasya parimuktaye |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let effort be made quickly for the release of [my] son;

children.text: sarvasvam api dattvādya putraṃ māñ ca vimocaya |7|
children.translated_text: giving away even everything I own today, free my son and me! [7]

children.text: ṛdhyantu tava saṅkalpā ṛdhyatv āśāsitum manaḥ |
children.translated_text: May your intentions be fulfilled! May your heart's wishes prosper!

children.text: apy eva tañ ca jīvantaṃ drakṣyāmi tava putrakam iti |8|
children.translated_text: And may I indeed see that little son of yours alive!' [8]

body.translated_text: 'Console me now, the unfortunate one, bereft of joy,

body.text:
Sva Roy 83,5 - 86,87
[37] atha divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ putraviyogaśokaduḥkhābhyāhato 'pi dhairyam avalaṃbya cittena kṛtakarapuṭaḥ paurān uvāca || bhoḥ bhoḥ paurāḥ śrūyatāṃ kathan nāma yuktaṃ bhavatāmamedaṃ vyasanam upasthitam upekṣituṃ | katham aṭavyām ivāvicārya nagaramadhyena yuṣmākaṃ paśyatām eva prakāśaguṇo 'pi me kumāro vadhāya nīyate | katham alpotsukās tiṣṭhatha | kathaṃ pratīkāravirdhir na cintyate | kathaṃ kumārasya muktaye na prayatnadhvam iti | te kathayanti sārthavāha īdṛśo 'yaṃ kumāro guṇavāṃs tavaivaiaksyedaṃ vyasanam api tu sarveṣām evāsmākaṃ kin tūpāyan na paśyāmaḥ kumārasya pratimuktaye | yenaiva viṣaṇṇāmanasas tiṣṭhāma iti | divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati | bhavantaḥ parijñāta eva yuṣmābhir ayaṃ kumāro yathātyantaṃ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ sattvavatsalaḥ | cittam apy ayam īdṛśe 'kārye na samartha utpādayituṃ prāg evācarituṃ | tataḥ kumārasya pravicāraṇārthaṃ yatna ārabhyatāṃ | yadi kumāraḥ pravicāryate niyatam asmād vyasanāt parimucyate | yūyañ ca sādhavaḥ sarvajanasādhāraṇās tad yuṣmākaṃ vijñāpayatāṃ na kaścid doṣo dṛśyate | nānyatra mayy anukampā darśitā bhavati | sādhutvāt guṇānurāgitvañ ca prakāśitaṃ bhavati | yat kāruṇyacittaṃ paryupasthāpya gatvā rājā vijñapyatāṃ | tanmantriṇo vā kadācic ca te 'rtharucitvāt suyuktam api yuṣmadvacanam anyathā na manayanti | ahañ ca putraviyogenātyantaṃ vyathitaḥ | tataḥ sarvasvam api madīyaṃ dattvā tathā prasādaḥ karaṇīyo yathā kumāraḥ pravicāryata iti |
body.translated_text: [37] Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, though stricken by the grief and suffering of separation from his son, took hold of his courage, and with palms joined together, addressed the citizens: 'Sirs, citizens! Listen — how is it fitting for you to ignore this calamity that has befallen me? How is it that, as if in a wilderness without any inquiry, right in the middle of the city, before your very eyes, my prince, though endowed with manifest virtues, is being led to execution? How can you stand by with so little concern? How is it that no thought is given to a remedy? How do you not make effort for the prince's release?' They replied: 'Caravan leader, such is this prince, endowed with virtues — this calamity belongs to you alone, but it concerns all of us as well. However, we see no means for the prince's release. That is why we stand here with despondent minds.' The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> said: 'Sirs, this prince is fully known to you — how he is supremely compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, and tender toward beings. He is unable to produce even a thought for such a wrongful deed, let alone carry it out. Therefore, let effort be undertaken for a thorough examination of the prince. If the prince is examined, he will certainly be freed from this calamity. And you are good people, common to all — there is no fault seen in your making a petition. Nor would compassion be shown for me alone elsewhere; rather, your goodness and devotion to virtue would be made manifest. Having aroused a heart of compassion, go and petition the king, or his ministers. Perhaps, out of their fondness for wealth, they will not dismiss your well-reasoned words. I too am utterly distressed by separation from my son. Therefore, giving away even all my possessions, let such an appeal be made that the prince is given a thorough examination.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 87,1 - 89,3
[38] prajñāto 'sau sārthavāhaḥ kṛtamitraś ca | teṣu vacanāt kumāraguṇānurāgāc cābhyupagataṃ tataḥ taiḥ pravīṇā vyavahāriṇaḥ paurikā rājakulaṃ preṣitā uktāś ca | sa ced adya kumāraḥ punar nipuṇataraṃ pravicāryate vayam api rājñaḥ suvarṇalakṣam anuprayacchāma iti | tatas te paurikā vyavahāriṇaḥ karaṇamaṇḍapaṅgatāḥ pracaṇḍena cāmātyena dūrata eva dṛṣṭā uktāś ca bhavantaḥ kim āgamanaprayojanam iti | tair ākhyātaṃ rājagṛhanivāsinaś ca paurā evaṃ vijñapayanty ayaṃ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro 'tyarthaṃ rūpaudāryasampadā yuktatvān mahājanavallabhaś ced asya viyogād rājagṛhanivāsino janakasya mahatī pīḍā | dharmābhiratatvād vinayādiguṇopetatvāc cāsya na kaścid enam aparādham abhiśraddadhāti | tad vayaṃ suvarṇalakṣam anuprayacchāmaḥ | divākaraś ca sārthavāhaḥ sarvasvam asmadvijñaptyā suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ pratinivartya punar nipuṇataraṃ pravicāryatām evaṃ kṛte cāsmākaṃ vijñāptisākalyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati | rājñaś ca koṣaḥ samvarddhito bhavati |
body.translated_text: [38] That caravan leader was well-known and had many friends. At their request, and out of their affection for the prince's virtues, they agreed. Thereupon, experienced and skilled citizen-merchants were sent to the royal court, and they were told: 'If today the prince is examined more thoroughly once again, we too shall give the king a <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of gold.' Then those citizen-merchants and officials, having entered the hall of justice, were seen from afar by the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, who said to them: 'Sirs, what is the purpose of your coming?' They informed him, saying: 'The citizens dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> petition thus — this prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, because he is supremely endowed with the splendor of beauty and form, is beloved of the great multitude. From his separation, his father, the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, suffers great affliction. Because of his devotion to <s>Dharma</s> and his being endowed with virtues such as modesty, no one believes any wrongdoing of his. Therefore, we shall give a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold. And the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> offers all his possessions at our request. Let the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> be brought back and examined more thoroughly once again. If this is done, our petition will have been fully carried out, and the king's treasury will be enriched.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 89,3 - 91,5
[39] pracaṇḍo 'mātyaḥ śrutvā ruṣitaḥ kathayati | bhavantaḥ kim atra na vicāritaṃ yad bhūyo vicāryate yac ca kathayata rājakośa eṣa saṃvarddhito bhavatīti | tata kiṃ vayam anyāyopāttair dravyai rājakośaṃ samvarddhayiṣyāmaḥ | na ca yuṣmābhī rājño 'bhiprāyo 'vabuddhaḥ | sarvathā yūyam avaśyaṃ vaiśālakānāṃ prayogeṇāsya rājño 'narthaṅ karttukāmā yenaivam upāyenāsya rājño 'varṇaṃ niścārayitum icchatha | anyāyakāry eva rājā yad evam avicāryaṃ janapadaṃ vināśayatīti | tena te nirbhartsitāḥ | sa tān nirbhartsayitvā catvāro 'sya kṛtāntapuruṣasadṛśāḥ santi manuṣyā atiraudrakarmāṇaḥ satatābhyāsavaśān nirghṛṇīkṛtasantānā niṣkaruṇās tān āhūya kathayati | gacchata śīghraṃ vadhyaghātakān adhitiṣṭhata | asmādvacanācca vaktavyā śīghram enaṃ nagarān niṣkāsya yathā sandiṣṭena vidhinā praghātayata | na ca yuṣmābhir māṃ muktvā rājānam vānayasya kasyacid vacanenāyaṃ moktavyaḥ | evaṃ hi kurvatāṃ śreyo 'nyathāhaṃ bhavatām mahāmarāryādābandaṅ karomīti | evaṃ svāminn iti te rājapuruṣās tasya pratiśrutya khaḍgapāṇayaḥ saṃprasthitās |
body.translated_text: [39] The minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, upon hearing this, became angry and said: 'Sirs, has this not already been examined, that it should be examined again? And as for your saying that the king's treasury would be enriched — what of it? Shall we enrich the royal treasury with unlawfully obtained wealth? Nor have you understood the king's intention. Surely you, at the instigation of the <s>Vaiśālikas</s>, wish to cause harm to this king, seeking by such means to spread ill repute about the king — [saying] that the king acts unjustly in destroying the realm without proper inquiry!' Thus he rebuked them. Having rebuked them, [he summoned] his four men resembling the messengers of death — men of extremely cruel deeds, who through constant practice had become merciless in their dispositions, devoid of compassion. Calling them, he said: 'Go quickly and take charge of the executioners. And on my authority, tell them to expel him from the city at once and have him executed according to the prescribed method. And without my permission, or the king's, he is not to be released at anyone else's word. If you do this, it will be well; otherwise I shall impose upon you the great punishment of confinement.' 'Yes, my lord!' — those royal servants, having agreed, set out with swords in hand.

body.text:
Sva Roy 91,5 - 93,4
[40] te vadhyaghātakā vyākṣepaśatāni kurvāṇāḥ śainaḥ śainaḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv anuśrāvayantaḥ paribhrāmayanto 'ho vata kumārasya kecit mocayitāro bhaviṣyanty apy evaṃ vayam īdṛśam akāryaṃ na kurma iti | te rājapuruṣā nikṛṣṭakhaḍgapāṇayas samprāptā tais teṣām vadhyaghātakānāṃ yathā sandiṣṭam ākhyātaṃ | uktāś ca yady enaṃ śīghraṃ nagarān niṣkrāmya yathā sandiṣṭena vidhinā na praghātayata | vayaṃ yuṣmān sāmpratam eva praghātayāma iti | te tān atisekanikṛṣṭān khaḍgavyagraṣṭān yamapuruṣān ivālokya saṃtrastās tato maraṇabhayabhītāś cintayituṃ pravṛttāḥ hā kaṣṭaṃ na kenacit kumārasya paritrāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ | sāṃpratam asmābhir eva praghātayitavyo bhaviṣyatīti | bāṣpāmbupariplutekṣaṇais tai rājapuruṣair adhiṣṭhitāḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ nagarān niṣkrāmayitum ārabdhāḥ |
body.translated_text: [40] Those executioners, making hundreds of diversions, slowly, slowly, parading the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> through the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections, kept proclaiming: 'Alas, perhaps some rescuers of the prince will appear, and thus we shall not have to perform such a terrible deed!' Those royal soldiers arrived with drawn swords in hand, and they conveyed the orders as instructed to the executioners, saying: 'If you do not quickly take him out of the city and have him executed according to the prescribed method, we shall execute you right now!' Those [executioners], upon seeing those extremely fierce men with swords drawn, like the servants of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death), became terrified. Then, frightened by the fear of death, they began to think: 'Alas, how terrible! No one has come to rescue the prince. Now we ourselves shall have to execute him.' With eyes flooded with tears, supervised by those royal soldiers, they began to lead <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> out of the city.

body.text:
Sva Roy 93,4 - 96,5
[41] tañ ca nagarān niṣkāsyamānam ālokyānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi ekaraveṇoccair vikroṣṭum ārabdhāni hā kaṣṭam eṣa | divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ sarvasvena viyujyate | eṣa divākarasya sārthavāhasya mātṛkāvaṅśaś chidyate | eṣa divākarasya sārthavāhasya kulapradīpo antardhāpyate | eṣa divākarasya sārthavāhasya kulanandano 'ntadrghāpyate | eṣa divākarasya sārthavāhasya kulacūḍāmaṇirapahriyate | eṣa divākarasya sārthavāhasya cakṣur nirudhyate | etad divākarasya sārthavāhasya kulavibhūṣaṇam apahriyate | etad divākarasya sārthavāhasya hṛdayam utapāṭyate | amī divākarasya sārthavāhasya mūrtimantaḥ prāṇā apahriyante | hā kaṣṭaṃ kathaṃ nāma kumāro 'ṭavyām evaṃ paribhrāmya niṣkāsito na kenacid asya paritrāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ | eṣa sāmprataṃ rājagṛhān nagarāc candramā mṛtyurāhuṇā grasyate | eṣa rājagṛhanagaranabhastaladivākaro 'staṅgacchati | etad rājagṛhanagaranivāsināṃ paurāṇāṃ netrāmṛtam adarśanapathe vyavasthāpyate | etad rājagṛhanagaranivāsināṃ paurāṇāṃ prītinibandhanaṃ vilupyate | etad rājanagṛhanagaranivāsināṃ paurāṇāṃ vibhūṣaṇam apahriyate | eṣa rājagṛhanagaranivāsināṃ paurāṇāṃ cūḍāmaṇir apahriyate | eṣa rājagṛhanagaranivāsināṃ paurāṇāṃ hṛdayavallabho vināśāya nīyate | kam idānīṃ rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurā animiṣam avalokayiṣyanti | kam idānīṃ dṛṣṭvā prītimanaso bhaviṣyantīti nirāśībhūtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [41] And seeing him being led out of the city, many hundreds of thousands of living beings began to cry out loudly with a single voice: 'Alas, how terrible! The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being deprived of his all! The maternal lineage of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being cut off! The lamp of the family of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being extinguished! The joy of the family of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being destroyed! The crest-jewel of the family of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being stolen! The eye of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being obstructed! The ornament of the family of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being taken away! The heart of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being torn out! The living breath, in bodily form, of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> is being stolen! Alas, how terrible — how is it that the prince, having been paraded through the wilderness thus, is led out, and no one has come to his rescue! Now, from the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, this moon is being swallowed by the death-<s>Rāhu</s>! This sun of the sky of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is setting! This nectar of the eyes of the citizens dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is being placed beyond sight! This bond of joy of the citizens dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is being torn away! This ornament of the citizens dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is being taken away! This crest-jewel of the citizens dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is being seized! This heart's beloved of the citizens dwelling in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is being led to destruction! Whom now shall the citizens of <s>Rājagṛha</s> gaze upon without blinking? Upon seeing whom shall they now become joyful in heart?' Thus they became hopeless.

body.text:
Sva Roy 96,5 - 99,2
[42] pracaṇḍasyāmātyasyānyatayamena puruṣeṇāgatya niveditaṃ | niḥkāsitaḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro rājagṛhān nagarād iti | sa śrutvā prītimanāḥ samvṛttaḥ | tatas te paurikā vyavahāriṇas tac chrutvā nirāśībhūtās tair āgatya teṣāṃ paurāṇām etat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇāveditaṃ | tac chrutvā te 'pi paurā nirāśībhūtāḥ | samudvignāḥ parasparam ūcuḥ | bhavanto 'pi kalirājena tādṛśaḥ pitā dhārmiko dharmarājā jīvitād vyavaropitaḥ | idānīm ārabdha evaṃvidhān api prakhyātaguṇān mahājanavallabhān puruṣaviśeṣān asaṃdṛśyān praghātayituṃ | aho nairghṛṇyam aho guṇājñatā | aho 'viśeṣajñatā mantriṇāṃ yo nāmaivam atyantarūpaudāryasampannatvāc ca vinītatvāc ca pūjām arhati sa eva guṇavān puruṣaviśeṣaḥ katham avicārya badhāya parityajyate | athavā kāla evāyam īdṛśaḥ samupasthito yad asanto vivarddhante | evaṃ guṇayuktasya janasyaivaṃvidho viyogo bhaviṣyatīti | kālopakarṣya daurātmyam udbhāvayanto divākarasya sārthavāhasya etat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇākhyātavantaḥ |
body.translated_text: [42] A man sent by the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> came and reported: 'The prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> has been expelled from the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.' Upon hearing this, he became delighted. Then those citizen-merchants, upon hearing this, became hopeless. They came and reported this matter in detail to the citizens. Upon hearing this, those citizens too became hopeless. Agitated, they said to one another: 'Sirs, by this king of the <s>Kali</s> age — even such a father, righteous, a <s>dharma-rāja</s> (king of righteousness), has been deprived of his life! Now he has begun to have even such men of renowned virtues, beloved of the great multitude, extraordinary men, executed out of sight! Oh, what cruelty! Oh, what ignorance of virtue! Oh, what lack of discrimination among the ministers — that indeed such a virtuous and extraordinary man, who, because of his supreme endowment with the splendor of beauty and form and his modesty, deserves to be honored, is without inquiry abandoned to execution! But perhaps such a time has arrived when the wicked flourish, and for a person endowed with such virtues, such a separation will occur!' Denouncing the wickedness as produced by the deterioration of the times, they related this matter in detail to the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 99,2 - 101,102
[43] tac chrutvā vihatāśo divākaraḥ sārthavāhas tīvra śokaduḥkhābhyāhato mūrcchito bhūmau patitaḥ | tato jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇo viṣaṇṇamanā nirānandaḥ sāṃprataṃ putrako me praghātyata iti | uccair vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [43] Upon hearing this, the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, bereft of hope, stricken by intense grief and suffering, fainted and fell to the ground. Then, having regained his breath through sprinkling of water, despondent in mind, devoid of joy, [thinking] 'Now my dear son has been executed!' — he began to cry out loudly:

body.text: locanānanda hā putra hā me kulavibhūṣaṇa |

children.translated_text: Of wretched-fated me, O dear one, you are being led away with none to cry for you! [1]

children.text: vimuhyate me hṛdayaṃ bhramanti ca diśo 'dhunā |
children.translated_text: My heart is bewildered, and the directions spin about now;
scorched by the fire of separation from you, alas, my mind is burning! [2]
For one who is wise, modest, and devoted to compassion —

children.text: hā kathaṃ dāruṇaṃ tāta tava vyasanam āgataṃ |3|
children.translated_text: alas, how has such a terrible calamity come upon you, dear one? [3]
Having attained the incomparable joy born of your birth, O son,
O good son, through separation from you, I have fallen again into the fire of grief! [4]
Merciless and lacking discrimination — oh, these ministers of the king!

children.text: yair evaṃ vinayopetas tvaṃ putra na vicāritaḥ |5|
children.translated_text: By whom you, so endowed with modesty, O son, were not given a [proper] examination! [5]
Oh, what cruelty has been displayed by that king,
by whom, without examination, you have today been abandoned, O dear son! [6]

children.text: viśeṣo dhik sādhujano nūnam astaṅgato hṛdi |
children.translated_text: Shame! Surely the recognition of good people has set in the heart;

children.text: guṇavān api yat putra nirākrandaḥ praghātyase |7|
children.translated_text: that you, though endowed with virtues, O son, are being executed with none to cry for you! [7]

children.text: tat kiṃ viproṣitāḥ sarvā nagarasyāsya devatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Have then all the deities of this city gone abroad,

children.text: ghātyamānam upekṣante yad evaṃ guṇinaṃ janaṃ |8|
children.translated_text: that they ignore such a virtuous person being slain? [8]

children.text: sendrāḥ salokapālāś ca devā ye ca maharddhikāḥ |
children.translated_text: The gods together with <s>Indra</s>, together with the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>), and those of great supernatural power —

children.text: anukampām upādāya te me rakṣantu putrakaṃ |9|
children.translated_text: may they, taking up compassion, protect my little son! [9]
Those great-souled sages (<s>munis</s>) of accomplished vows who exist now —

children.text: te 'nukampāṃ puraskṛtya parirakṣantu me sutam iti |10|
children.translated_text: may they, placing compassion foremost, protect my son!' [10]

body.translated_text: O delight of [my] eyes! Alas, my son! Alas, my family's ornament!

body.text:
Sva Roy 102,1 - 105,4
[44] tasya buddhir utpannā kim artham ahaṃ viṣīdāmi yan nv ahaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakalajagad ekabāndhavaṃ mahākāruṇikaṃ samunasmareyaṃ sa hi bhagavān anāthānān nāthaḥ | atrāṇānāṃ trāṇaṃ | aśaraṇānāṃ śaraṇaṃ | aparāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaṃ | tathā hi tena bhagavatā kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasambādhaprāptā bahavaḥ sattvās tebhyas tebhyo mahābhayebhyaḥ parimocitā | tathā mahāsamudram adhyagatā vaṇijo makarasya bhayasantrastāḥ samanusmaraṇamātreṇaiva tasmān maraṇabhayāt paritrātāḥ | tathā naika puruṣaghātakenaikarabhasenodyataśastreṇāṅgulīmālena ghātyamānā tajjananī tasmāj jīvitopacchedabhayāt paritrātā | tathā ca pūrvajanmavairānubanndhasāmarthyād anekaprāṇiśatasahastropaghātatham abhiprajvālitakrūrahutāśanasya mānuṣamāṃsarasāsvādalobhāt śravallālāvalelihāna_jihvā_vikaṭadīrghatīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇamukhasya yakṣasyāhārārtham upanāmitas tadvadvanasamīpastho hastaka āṭavakas tasmān maraṇabhayāt paritrātā || samarthaḥ sa bhagavān me putram asmāt saṅkaṭāt parimocayituṃ | yan nv ahaṃ tam eva bhagavantaṃ mahākaruṇikaṃ parmavatsalasvabhāvaṃ samanusmareyam iti | samīpastham anyatam upāsakaṃ pṛṣṭavān idānīṃ bhagavān kutra viharatīti | tato 'sav upāsako bhagavantam anusmṛtya bāṣpoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭham uvāca | sārthavāhaḥ
yaḥ sārthavāho lokasya yo loke sukhadāyakaḥ |

children.translated_text: He, the great Teacher, the sole kinsman of all the world, has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>. |1|
He who was the lamp of the lampless, the refuge, the support—

children.text: nirvṛtaḥ sa jino loke dīpaḥ snehakṣayād iti |2|
children.translated_text: that <s>Jina</s> (Victor) has been extinguished in the world, like a lamp when the oil is exhausted. |2|

body.translated_text: This thought arose in him: 'Why do I despair? What if I were to recall the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the sole kinsman of all the world, the greatly compassionate one? For that Blessed One is the protector of the unprotected, the refuge of the refugeless, the shelter of the shelterless, the support of the unsupported. For by that Blessed One, many beings who had fallen into distress, difficulty, and peril were liberated from those various great dangers. Thus, merchants who had gone upon the great ocean, terrified by fear of the sea monster (<s>makara</s>), were rescued from that mortal danger by merely recalling [his name]. Thus, when <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, the slayer of many men, with weapon raised in a single rush, was about to kill his own mother, she was rescued from that danger to her life. And likewise, <s>Hastaka Āṭavaka</s>, who dwelt near the forest, was brought as food to a <s>yakṣa</s> whose terrible fire had been kindled to destroy hundreds of thousands of beings through the force of enmity carried from former births, who craved the taste of human flesh, whose tongue licked forth streams of saliva, whose mouth was horrifying with hideous, long, sharp fangs—he too was rescued from that mortal danger. That Blessed One is capable of liberating my son from this peril. What if I were to recall that very Blessed One, the greatly compassionate one, whose nature is supreme tenderness?' He asked a nearby lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>): 'Where does the Blessed One now dwell?' Then that <s>upāsaka</s>, recalling the Blessed One, spoke with a voice choked and stuttering with tears: 'O caravan leader! He who was the caravan leader of the world, who was the giver of happiness in the world—'

body.text:
Sva Roy 105,4 - 111,2
[45] tac chrutvā divākaraḥ sārthavāho bhagavadviyogād dviguṇīkṛtaśokaśalyābhyāhato mūrcchito bhūmau nipapāta | tato jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇa utthāya yasyāṃ diśi bhagavān parinirvṛtas tadabhimukho uccair vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ |
hā dharmarāja sarvajña doṣārigaṇasūdana |

children.translated_text: Having abandoned the unprotected people, O Lord of the World, where have you gone? |1|
Alas, O mighty one of renowned conduct, sole kinsman of all beings,
detached from all bonds, teacher of the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>! |2|
Alas, how indeed will this world, its eyes veiled by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),
bereft of you as its protector, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>? |3|
When you, who were heroic in compassion for others, have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: anāthaḥ khalv ayaṃ lokaḥ kaṃ nāthaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati |4|
children.translated_text: this world, truly unprotected, to what protector will it resort? |4|

children.text: ye ca te dharmato jātā vineyajanaputrakāḥ |
children.translated_text: And those who were born from the <s>Dharma</s>, the children of those to be guided—

children.text: tvayā vihīnās te sarve kariṣyanti kam āśrayaṃ |5|
children.translated_text: bereft of you, upon whom will they all depend? |5|
Having made fruitful the hopes of many, O destroyer of suffering,

children.text: vihatāśaṃ janaṃ kṛtvā kām āśāṃ tvaṃ gato mune |6|
children.translated_text: having shattered the hopes of the people, to what hope have you gone, O <s>Muni</s>? |6|
If the citizens should gather, eager to hear your words,

children.text: ko nu vakṣyati saddharmam adhunā nirvṛte tvayi |7|
children.translated_text: who indeed will speak the true <s>Dharma</s> now that you have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>? |7|

children.text: hā hato 'yam anya loko lokaḥ sāmarakinnaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, destroyed is this other world, the world with its gods and <s>kinnara</s>s,
separated from a protector so difficult to find, namely you, O <s>Muni</s>! |8|
How indeed will living beings, longing for the <s>Dharma</s>,
lovers of the teaching, fare, having heard of the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of you, their sole protector? |9|
Depending on you, the compassionate one, whose sole essence is compassion, the steadfast one—

children.text: ye guṇāḥ samavāpyante kas tan bhūyo na 'bhidhāsyati |10|
children.translated_text: the virtues that were attained—who will proclaim them again? |10|
How is it that, having generated great compassion for the sake of the three worlds,
you, O knower of the truth of compassion, have resorted to equanimity? |11|
Alas! The ship of <s>Dharma</s>, rich in the jewels of virtues, accumulated over <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>kalpa</s>s,
having reached the abyss of death, has been wrecked! |12|
Alas, that this world, blinded by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), deprived of the <s>Buddha</s> as its guide,
in the wilderness of birth, will arrive at a lost refuge! |13|
Truly, a great decline of the worlds has come upon them,

body.translated_text: Hearing this, the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, struck by the doubled arrow of grief from separation from the Blessed One, fainted and fell to the ground. Then, revived by a sprinkling of water, he rose and, facing the direction in which the Blessed One had attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, began to cry out loudly: 'Alas, <s>Dharma</s>-king, omniscient one, destroyer of the host of faults and enemies!'

body.text: buddharatnena mahatā viyuktānām ihādhunā |14|
body.translated_text: now that they are separated from the great jewel of the <s>Buddha</s>! |14|

body.text: tvayā bhikṣugaṇaṃ śūnyaṃ ṛṣabheneva gogaṇaṃ |

children.text: kathaṃ na viduṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛdayan na vidīryate |15|
children.translated_text: how, seeing [this], do the hearts of the wise not burst? |15|
With heads bowed in devotion, whose [feet] will the gods
henceforth bear upon their heads—the dust placed upon the tips of [whose] feet? |16|
Impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>) has truly come equally to all beings, cruel [that it is],

children.text: yayā tvayy api nāmādya pakṣapāto na darśitaḥ |17|
children.translated_text: since even toward you, today, it has shown no partiality! |17|
The Teacher, the greatly compassionate king of physicians, who cured the diseases of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>)
with the medicine of the Eightfold Path (<s>aṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), has been felled! |18|
Alas, how cruelly and swiftly has the Lord of the World attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>—
the unsurpassed giver of sight to the blinded world! |19|

children.text: nirvṛte tvayi ko me 'dya putraratnam anāgasaṃ |
children.translated_text: Now that you have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, who today will come here
and suddenly rescue my son, the blameless jewel, who is being slain? |20|

children.text: trātari tvayy anāthānāṃ gate tu paramāṅ gatim |
children.translated_text: When you, the rescuer of the unprotected, have gone to the supreme destination,

children.text: hā jātaḥ sāṃpratam ahaṃ nirāśaḥ sutajīvite |21|
children.translated_text: alas, I have now become hopeless about my son's life! |21|

children.text: adya me tat suvihitaṃ yat tvayoktaṃ mahātmane |
children.translated_text: Today that [truth] is well demonstrated for me, which was spoken by you, O great soul—

children.text: sarvaiḥ priyair vinābhāvo bhavatīty uttamaṃ vaca iti |22|
children.translated_text: the supreme utterance: 'Separation from all that is dear comes to pass.' |22|

body.translated_text: Without you, the community of <s>bhikṣu</s>s is empty, like a herd of cows without the bull;

body.text:
Sva Roy 111,2 - 115,2
[46] sa evam bahuvidha paridevya tam upāsakam uvāca | bhoḥ kaścin mahāśrāvako 'pi tāvat tasya bhagavato 'vaśiṣyate | kasya bhagavān śāsanam anuparīkṣya parinirvṛta iti | tatas tenopāsakenoktaṃ sārthavāha śrūyate bhagavān sthaviramahākāśyapasya śāsanam anuparīkṣya parinirvṛtaḥ | sthaviramahākāśyapo 'pi bhagavadājñayaiva sthavirānandasya śāsanam anuparīndya parinirvṛtaḥ | sa idānīṃ sthavirānanando mahātmā śāsanadhūrdharaḥ | sa idānīṃ tathāgata iva kāruṇyāt tāṃs tān grāmanagaranigamapallīpattanādīn gatvā vineyaṃ janānugrahaṃ karoti | tathānavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlāvaropaṇaṅ karoti | samucitakuśalasantatīnāṃ paripācanaṅ karoti | paripakvakuśalamūlasantatīnāṃ parimocayati | tathā kleśavyādhigrastānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmadeśanābhaiṣajyapradānena vicikitsaṃ karoti suvaidyavat | kleśāndhakārāvaṣṭabdhānāṃ sattvānāṃ saddharmdeśanāraśminikareṇa kleśāndhakāraṃ vidhamayati sūryavat | vacanakarasamūhena vaineyakumudavanaprabodhanaṃ karoti candravat | vaineyakoṭṭarājasahastrāṇi saddharmadeśanayā samanuśāsti cakravarttivat | svaprajñapratibhānanādena kutīrthyamṛgagaṇavidrāvaṇaṅ karoti siṃhavat | samupadeśavaineyasārthanistāraṇaṃ karoti daiśikavat | saddharmapāṇyāvatāraṇaṃ karoti sārthavāhavat | kuśalabījaprarohaṇaṃ karoti mahāmeghavat | hitāhitopadeśaṃ karoti mātāpitṛvat | adāntān sattvān damayaty amuktān mocayaty anāśvastān āśvasayaty aparinirvṛtān parinirvāpayati | tathā kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasamvādhaprāptān sattvān mahābhayebhyo mocayati | saṃkṣepāt sa mahātmā buddhakāryaṅ karoti | tam eva samanusmara | samarthaḥ sa te 'dya sutam asmāt saṅkaṭāt parimocayatum iti |
body.translated_text: Having lamented thus in many ways, he said to that <s>upāsaka</s>: 'Sir, does at least some great disciple (<s>śrāvaka</s>) of that Blessed One remain? Under whose care did the Blessed One attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, entrusting the teaching?' Then that <s>upāsaka</s> said: 'Caravan leader, it is heard that the Blessed One attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> entrusting the teaching to the Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>. The Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> too, by the Blessed One's own command, entrusting the teaching to the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Now that great soul, the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, is the upholder of the teaching. He now, like the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, out of compassion goes to various villages, cities, market towns, hamlets, and ports, and bestows benefit upon the people to be guided. Thus, for beings in whom roots of virtue have not been planted, he plants roots of virtue. For those whose streams of virtue have been cultivated, he brings them to maturity. For those whose streams of roots of virtue have matured, he liberates them. Thus, for beings afflicted by the diseases of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), he provides treatment by giving the medicine of <s>Dharma</s> teaching, like a skilled physician. For beings enveloped in the darkness of the afflictions, he dispels the darkness of the afflictions with the rays of true <s>Dharma</s> teaching, like the sun. With the host of speech-gems, he awakens the lotus groves of those to be guided, like the moon. He instructs thousands of <s>koṭṭarāja</s>s of those to be guided with true <s>Dharma</s> teaching, like a universal monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>). With the roar of his own wisdom and eloquence, he scatters the herds of deer that are the heretical teachers (<s>kutīrthya</s>), like a lion. He leads the caravans of those to be guided by his instruction across [the desert], like a guide. He leads them to the port of the true <s>Dharma</s>, like a caravan leader. He causes the seeds of virtue to sprout, like a great cloud. He instructs in what is beneficial and harmful, like a father and mother. He tames the untamed beings, liberates the unliberated, comforts the uncomforted, and brings to <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Thus, he rescues beings who have fallen into distress, difficulty, and peril from their great dangers. In short, that great soul carries out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>. Recall him. He is able today to liberate your son from this peril.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 115,2 - 118,4
[47] tac chrutvā divākaraḥ sārthavāho gatapratyāgataprāṇa iva sasaṃbhramas tam upāsakam uvāca | kutredānīṃ sa ānando viharatīti | tenoktaṃ sārthavāha śrutaṃ mayā sthavirānanda etarhi vaiśālyām viharaty āmrapālīvana iti | atha divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ sahasaivotthāya jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena vaiśālī tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya sutaviyogaśokaduḥkhābhyāhato bāṣpormitaraṅgāpūryamāṇavadanakamalaḥ sāśruparyākulekṣaṇas tīvreṇāśayena sthavirānandam āyācituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Hearing this, the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, as if his breath had left and returned, agitated, said to the <s>upāsaka</s>: 'Where does that <s>Ānanda</s> now dwell?' He replied: 'Caravan leader, I have heard that the Elder <s>Ānanda</s> is presently dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the <s>Āmrapālī</s> grove.' Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, rising at once, placing his knees on the ground, joining his palms toward <s>Vaiśālī</s>, stricken by the grief of separation from his son, his lotus-like face flooded with waves of tears, his eyes turbid with weeping, with intense devotion, began to supplicate the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: yadi tvaṃ paramācārya sattvāśayaviduttamaḥ |

children.translated_text: knowing [their] dispositions and latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), hear this entreaty: |1|

children.text: nirvṛto bhagavān buddhaḥ śiṣyāś cāsya maharddhikāḥ |
children.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Buddha</s> has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and his disciples of great miraculous power [have too];

children.text: avaśiṣṭas tvam eko hi teṣāṃ śāsanavardhanaḥ |2|
children.translated_text: you alone remain, the sustainer of their teaching. |2|
You have become the comfort of this world, you are its support;
now you must look upon the task that is for the welfare of all beings. |3|

children.text: tad adyaivaṃvidhe nāthe tiṣṭhaty ārakṣake tvayi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when such a protector, a guardian, namely you, still remains,
how can our son be slain thus without anyone crying out? |4|

children.text: na bhaved yadi sattvārtho na tiṣṭheyur bhavadvidhāḥ |
children.translated_text: If there were no concern for beings' welfare, those like you would not remain;

children.text: ghātyamānaṃ janaṃ śrāddham evaṃ katham upekṣase |5|
children.translated_text: how then do you look on indifferently while faithful people are being slain? |5|

children.text: sattvārthañ cec charīraṃ hi tvaṃ dhārayasi suvrata |
children.translated_text: If indeed you maintain your body for the welfare of beings, O one of excellent vows (<s>suvrata</s>),

children.text: tat kṛpāṃ sammukhīkṛtya samanvāhara me sutaṃ |6|
children.translated_text: then, bringing compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) to the forefront, attend to my son! |6|
Deprived of all recourse, without protection, without support,
sunk in the mire of grief—deliver me together with my wife! |7|

children.text: kam vā vijñapayāmy anyaṃ ko 'nyo 'py evaṃ jagaddhite |
children.translated_text: Whom else shall I beseech? Who else is thus [devoted] to the welfare of the world,

children.text: nirdiṣṭaḥ śākyamuninā yathā tvam adhunā prabho |8|
children.translated_text: appointed by <s>Śākyamuni</s> as you are now, O lord? |8|

children.text: tvadṛte putrakasyānyas trātā nāsti vibho yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since, apart from you, there is no other rescuer of [my] son, O mighty one,

children.text: tasmāt tvaritam āgamya putram me trātum arhasi |9|
children.translated_text: therefore, come swiftly and deign to rescue my son! |9|
Seized by the unbearable, evil enemy that is grief for my son,
joyless, together with my wife—O <s>Ānanda</s>, bring joy to me today! |10|
Thus.

body.translated_text: If you, O supreme teacher, the highest knower of the dispositions of beings,

body.text:
Sva Roy 118,4 - 121,122
[48] athaitasminn antare sthavirānandaḥ karuṇayāpūryyamāṇaś cintayaṃs trirātrestridivasasya śrāvakacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokayati | ko hīyate ko varddhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṅkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ sambādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ | ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāptāraḥ | kam aham apāyamārgād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ | kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyāṃ | kam āryadhanavirahitaṃ āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam ity adrākṣīt sthavirānandaḥ sthaviraśāradvatīsutasamena cakṣuṣā suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāramupacitakuśalamūlasambhāraṃ kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasambādhaprāptaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā punas tatrastha eva ṛddhyā gajabhujasadṛśam bāhum abhiprasārya sahasaiva rājānam ajātaśatrum upariprāsādatalagatam atipramattavihāriṇam acchaṭāśabdena prabodhya vyāpinā svareṇovāca | mahārāja na śobhanaṃ te kṛtaṃ yata suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ svayam eva na vicāritas tathādyaiṣa na sāṃpratam atrāpy anapakārī rājagṛhān niṣkāśya mahāśmaśānaṃ nīyate praghātayituṃ | nivārayety athaitat sthavirānandavacanam upaśrutya rājā sasambhramaṃ tvaritam abhinamya sthaviranandam uparidhavalagṛhastha utthāya mahatā svareṇa caturdiśam uktaṃ bhoḥ śrūyatāṃ yo mahāśmāśānaṃ tvarita mabhigamyāsmadvacanāt suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ ghātyamānaṃ pratimocayati tasyāhaṃ suvarṇapeṭakamanu prayacchāmi pañca ca grāmavarāṇi| mahājanavallabho 'sau kumāraḥ| tad rājño vacanam upaśrutya prāṇisahasrāṇi pradhāvitāni ||
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, filled with compassion, reflecting, surveyed the world with the eye of a disciple (<s>śrāvaka</s>) [that sees] three nights and three days: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into peril? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into difficulty, peril, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>)? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who has arrived at the lower realms? Whom might I lift from the path of the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of sensual desire (<s>kāma</s>), might I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, bereft of the noble treasures, might I establish in the sovereignty of the noble treasures?' The Elder <s>Ānanda</s> saw, with an eye equal to that of the Elder <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> [<s>Śāriputra</s>], Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, who had accumulated a store of roots of virtue, and who had fallen into difficulty, peril, and distress. Then, remaining right there, by his miraculous power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), extending an arm like an elephant's trunk, he suddenly awakened King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, who was on the upper terrace of the palace, dwelling in extreme heedlessness, with a snapping sound, and spoke in a pervading voice: 'Great King, what you have done is not fitting, for Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> himself was not investigated, and now this one, who is moreover innocent, is being led from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the great charnel ground to be executed. Prevent it!' Then, hearing these words of the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, the king, agitated and in haste, bowing to the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, rising from the upper white mansion, proclaimed in a great voice in all four directions: 'Hear! Whoever goes quickly to the great charnel ground and, by my command, rescues Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> who is being slain—to him I shall grant a basket of gold and five choice villages! That prince is beloved of the people!' Hearing the king's words, thousands of people rushed forth.

body.text:
Sva Roy 122,1 - 123,4
[49] athaitasminn antare vadhyaghātakās tai rājapuruṣair adhiṣṭhitāḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram ādāya mahāśmaśānam anuprāptāḥ | kāśisundarī dārikā svakair jñātibhir nīlapītalokahitāvadātair vastraiḥ samalaṅkṛtāyāṃ śivikāyām āropya mahāśmaśānam abhinirhṛtā tasyā jñātayas tām ekasmin pradeśe sthāpayitvā kāṣṭhāni samudānīya citām uparacayitum ārabdhāḥ | taiś ca vadhyaghātakair uktāḥ | etāvad eṣā yuṣmābhiś citāyām āropayitavyā muhūrtaṃ tāvad udīkṣadhvaṃ | yāvad vayaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ śūle protaṃ kṛtvā praghātayāmo yat kāraṇam eṣa suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro 'nayā kāśisundaryā dārikayā saha ekāṃ citām āropya dhyāpayitavya ity uktvā śūlaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitum ārabdhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the executioners, directed by those royal servants, took Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> and reached the great charnel ground. The courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, placed by her own kinsmen in a palanquin adorned with blue, yellow, and white garments [befitting one departing the world], was carried out to the great charnel ground. Her kinsmen, having placed her in one spot, began to bring firewood and build a funeral pyre. And those executioners said: 'She is to be placed by you upon the pyre in due time. Wait a moment while we impale Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> on a stake and execute him. The reason is that this Prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> is to be placed on one pyre together with this courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s> and burned.' Having said this, they began to set the stake in the ground.

body.text:
Sva Roy 123,2 - 125,3
 [50] atha suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ śūlaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya mānam ālokya mātaram anusmṛtya tīvramanyudravīkṛtasantāno 'śrūṇi prapātayitum ārabdhaḥ | sāṃprataṃ mātur madviyogaṃ śrutvā kā 'vasthā bhaviṣyati | yā hi nāma pūrvaṃ yāmārddhamātram api mām apaśyantī parāpīḍāpraveditavatī sā mayādyaikaputreṇa viyuktā kathaṃ prāṇān dhārayiṣyati | hā kaṣṭam īdṛśo 'py aham evam adhanyo yan mām āgamya mātā madviyogaduḥkhaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti | tatas tair vadhyaghātakaiḥ tat śūlaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nikhātaṃ paraparāṅ ca saṅjalpaṅ kartum ārabdhaḥ | ko 'smākaṃ kumāraṃ śūle samāropayati | tatra caikaiko 'pi vyājaṃ kartum ārabdho yūyam āropayata | mama śirorujātyartham bādhate | mama pṛṣṭhaśūlam mama pārśvaśūlam iti na teṣāṃ kaścid utsahate sma tad akāryaṅ kartuṃ ||
body.translated_text: [50] Then the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, after the stake was erected on the ground, looking up at the sky and remembering his mother, his heart melted by intense grief, began to shed tears: 'What will be my mother's condition now when she hears of my separation? She who previously, if she did not see me for even half a watch, would be stricken with distress—how will she, separated today from me, her only son, sustain her life? Alas, how unfortunate I am, that because of me my mother will experience the suffering of separation from me!' Then the executioners planted that stake in the ground and began to deliberate among themselves: 'Who among us will mount the prince on the stake?' Each one of them began to make excuses: 'You do it—my head aches terribly!' 'I have back pain!' 'I have side pain!' None of them dared to perform that dreadful deed.

body.text:
Sva Roy 125,3 - 127,128
[51] tataḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāras teṣāṃ sañjarupaṃ śrutvā śūlañ ca pṛthivyāṃ nikhātam udvīkṣya hā sāmpratam ahaṃ na bhaviṣyāmīti | saṃsāra doṣodvigno mokṣamārggābhilāṣī nirānandamātmānamavagamya param abhayaviṣāda vihvalekṣaṇo vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | hā kaṣṭam idānīṃ mayā sudurllabhaṃ saddharmamahotsavaṃ manuṣyatvam āsādyākṛtārthe naiva marttavyam bhaviṣyatīti | hā punar api saṃsāre saṃsariṣyāmi | punar api mayā saṃsāracārake vastavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | punaḥ saṃsārāṭavyāṃ paribhramitavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | punaḥ saṃsāramahāgahanaṃ praveṣṭavyam bhaviṣyati | punaḥ saṃsāramahāprapāte patitavyam bhaviṣyati | punaḥ saṃsāramahājambālamadhye sthātavyam bhaviṣyati | punar mayā sañjīvanakālasūtrasaṃghātarauravamahārauravapratāpanāvīcyādiṣu narakeṣūpapattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | punar api mayā gajagavayamahiṣaśaśaśarabhamṛgarurucamarabiḍālacitrāsu yoniṣūpapattavyam bhaviṣyati | punar api mayā satataṃ kṣuttṛṣṇādimahadduḥkhadaurmanasyaparīteṣu nirnaṣṭapānabhojanaśabdeṣu mūtrapurīṣakheṭasiṃhāṇakādyāhāreṣu galagaṇḍakādiṣu preteṣūpapattavyam bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: [51] Then the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, hearing their deliberation and looking up at the stake planted in the ground, thought: 'Alas, now I shall cease to be!' Distressed by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), longing for the path of liberation, perceiving himself to be without joy, with eyes overwhelmed by supreme fear and despair, he began to cry out: 'Alas, how terrible! Having obtained human birth, so hard to obtain, the great festival of the true <s>Dharma</s>, I shall die with my purpose unfulfilled! Alas, I shall transmigrate again in <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to dwell in the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to wander in the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to enter the great thicket of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to fall into the great precipice of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to stand in the midst of the great swamp of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Again I shall have to be reborn in the hells of <s>Sañjīvana</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, and others! Again I shall have to be reborn in the wombs of elephants, yaks, buffaloes, hares, deer of various kinds, camels, cats, and other creatures! Again I shall have to be reborn among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) with goiters and such, constantly surrounded by the great sufferings of hunger and thirst and other miseries, where the word for food and drink has vanished, feeding on urine, feces, phlegm, mucus, and such!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 128,1 - 130,1
[52] śrūyate ca kadācit karhicit tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā loka utpadyante | tad yathodumbare puṣpaṃ kadācit karhicit tathāgatapraveditasya dharmavinayasya lokeṣu darśanārthaṃ prajñāyate | durllabhā kṣaṇasampad durllabham manuṣyatvam āryāyatane pratyājātir indrayair vikalatā 'jaḍatā 'neḍamūkatā 'hastasamvārtikatā pratibalatā subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇām artham ājñātuṃ | ahañ cātra viratito 'dya na bhaviṣyāmi | tad idam aṣṭākṣaṇavinirmuktam me manuṣyatvaṃ viphalī bhaviṣyati | tata kim idānīṅ karomi | kiṃ bhagavān mahākāruṇiko buddhas tiṣṭhati yaṃ samanusmārāmi yo mām āsyām avasthāyām anātham atrāṇam aśaraṇaṃ aparāyaṇaṃ nirālokaṃ kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasambādhaprāptaṃ mahākāruṇikatvād āgatya paritrāsyate | sa ca bhagavān mama bhāgyāparādhena laghu laghu eva parinirvṛtaḥ | tat kim idānīm asyām avasthāyāṃ samanusmarāmi | ko me tathāgata iva kāruṇyād āgatya paritrāṇaṅ kariṣyatīti | nirāśībhūtaḥ kampitum ārabdhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [52] 'And it is heard that only at rare intervals do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> arise in the world—just as the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> tree appears only rarely, so the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen in the worlds. Rare is the conjunction of favorable conditions; rare is human birth; rebirth in the realm of the noble ones; the integrity of one's faculties; freedom from dullness; not being deaf-mute; not being born in a place where one cannot practice; the ability to understand the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken <s>dharmas</s>. And I, separated from all this, shall today cease to be! This my human birth, freed from the eight unfavorable conditions, shall be rendered fruitless. What then shall I do now? Does the Blessed One, the greatly compassionate <s>Buddha</s>, still abide, whom I may remember, who out of great compassion would come and rescue me—helpless, unprotected, without refuge, without recourse, without light, fallen into dire distress? But that Blessed One, due to the fault of my fortune, quickly, all too quickly, attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. What then can I remember in this condition? Who will come out of compassion, like the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and rescue me?' Having lost all hope, he began to tremble.

body.text:
Sva Roy 130,1 - 133,134
[53] tasya buddhir utpannā sthavirānando mahātmā tiṣṭhati | taṃ samanusmarāmi | so 'pi mahātmā śrūyate sarvasattvahitāvahitacittasantānaḥ | tasya bhagavatā sthavirmahākāśyapena ca sakalaṃ śāsanam anuparīnditaṃ | tenādhunāvalokyāvalokya sarvasattvahitaṃ karaṇīyaṃ mahārddhikaś cāsau mahānubhāvaḥ samarthaś ca sthavirānando mām asmād vyasanāt paritrātuṃ tam eva samanusmarāmīti viditvā vāṣpāmbupariplutekṣaṇaḥ | saṃsārabhayodvignaḥ | paramasamvegaprāptas tīvreṇāśayena sthavirānandam āyācituṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [53] An idea arose in him: 'The great-souled elder <s>Ānanda</s> still abides. Him I shall remember. That great soul too is heard to have a mental continuum devoted to the welfare of all beings. To him the entire teaching has been entrusted by the Blessed One and by the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>. Therefore, observing and looking after the welfare of all beings, that elder <s>Ānanda</s>, who is of great supernatural power and great might, is capable of rescuing me from this calamity. Him alone shall I remember.' Knowing this, with eyes flooded with tears, distressed by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, having reached the utmost urgency, he began to supplicate the elder <s>Ānanda</s> with intense aspiration:

body.text: saṃsārabhayabhītasya nirānandasya me sataḥ |

children.text: sthavirānanda vijñaptiṃ tvam idānīṃ śrotum arhasi |1|
children.translated_text: O elder <s>Ānanda</s>, you should now deign to hear my petition. [1]
The Omniscient One, compassionate by nature, having laid down the burden of benefiting beings,

children.text: ayi nirvṛtim āyātaḥ kāśyape tu mahātmani |2|
children.translated_text: Alas, has gone to <s>nirvṛti</s> (final rest); and likewise the great-souled <s>Kāśyapa</s>. [2]
That elder <s>Kāśyapa</s> too, having fulfilled his purpose, has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: tvayy eva bhāraṃ nikṣipya jagato 'sya vibhūtaye |3|
children.translated_text: Having placed the burden upon you alone, for the welfare of this world. [3]
Now that the perfectly enlightened one, the kinsman of the world, has gone to <s>nirvṛti</s>,
And the illustrious <s>Kāśyapa</s>, devoted to the welfare of all beings— [4]
You are the protector of the unprotected, the giver of fearlessness to the frightened,
The resting ground for the weary, the refuge of those who seek refuge. [5]
The duty of the teacher must be performed by you; you are the sole kinsman of the world;

children.text: agrayas tvaṃ buddhaśiṣyāṇāṃ tvañ ca śāsanadhūrddharaḥ |6|
children.translated_text: You are the foremost among the <s>Buddha</s>'s disciples; you are the bearer of the teaching's yoke. [6]

children.text: tvam adya duḥkhapātālād yadi māṃ noddhariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: If you will not lift me today from the abyss of suffering,

children.text: hato 'smi yasmād dheto 'nyaṃ nāthaṃ nānavaimi sāṃprataṃ |7|
children.translated_text: I am slain, for I know no other protector at present. [7]

children.text: na bibhemi tathā mṛtyor jātasya maraṇaṃ dhruvaṃ |
children.translated_text: I do not so much fear death—for one who is born, death is certain;
You who know the way of escape from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>— [8]
Having obtained this rare moment, freed from the eight unfavorable conditions,

children.text: akṛtārthena martavyam iti me mahatī vyathā |9|
children.translated_text: That I should die with my purpose unfulfilled—this is my great anguish. [9]
Rare indeed is the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the all-seeing ones;

children.text: tvām āgamya yathā nīti vandhyatām me tathā kuru |10|
children.translated_text: Through reliance on you, as is proper, make my life not fruitless. [10]
Your unwavering compassion extends to all living beings;
Therefore it is not fitting to abandon me, who longs for the path of liberation. [11]
If you, O greatly fortunate one, are devoted to the welfare of all beings,
Look upon me, who has fallen into dire distress! [12]

children.text: tad evam aparitrāṇaṃ vīkṣya divyena cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: Seeing me thus unprotected, with your divine eye,

children.text: tvam adya kṣipram āgamya māṃ paritrātum arhasī ty |13|
children.translated_text: You should today come swiftly and rescue me.' [13]

body.translated_text: 'For me, who am terrified by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who am without joy,

body.text:
Sva Roy 134,1 - 137,5
[54] athāsminn antare sthavirānando mahātmā sakalajagadarthasampādanāvabaddhaparikaraḥ kāruṇyāc cānena tathānantasattvaceṣṭāvalokanāhitacittasantānaparamaduḥkhādivyena cakṣuṣā suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram asyām avasthāyāṃ varttamānam ālokya karuṇayā sañcodyamānacittavṛttirdivyenāvabhāsena bhuvanamaṇḍalam avabhāsya pañcārhacchataparivāraḥ sahasaiva ṛddhyā nabhastalam sandhyābhrapaṭalair iva gaganatalam āpūrayan sakalabhuvanalakṣmīpuñja iva dedīpyamānavigrahaḥ śmaśānābhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ | adrākṣīd rājā 'jātaśatrur uparidhavalagṛhasyāvasthitaḥ | sthavirānandaṃ mahatābhikṣusaṃghena sārddham arddhacandrākāropagūḍham upari vihāyasā ṛddhyā sandhyābhrapaṭalair iva gaganatalam alaṅkṛtya mahāśmaśāṇābhimukham āgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyābhavan niyataṃ sthavirānandaḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram uddiśyāgatas tañ cāgamya mahad āścaryādbhutan dharmaṃ deśayitukāmo bhaviṣyatīti | gacchāmy aham mahāśmaśānam iti | tataś ca sahasaiva sthavirānandaṃ saparivāraṃ namaskṛtya śaraṇapṛṣṭhāt tvaritatvaritam avatīrya padabhyām eva naika prāṇiśatasahasraparivāro mahāśmaśānaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | asmiṃś cānantare vadhyaghātakās tai rājapuruṣair udyatā śastrais tarjitāḥ kim artham eva vilambadhvaṃ śīghram enaṃ kumāraṃ śūle samāropayateti | tatas te vaghyaghātakāḥ saṃtrastāḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ śūle samāropayāmaḥ | ity uktvā kṣeptum ārabdhā | suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ saṃsāradoṣodvignacetā nirāśībhūto vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | hā kaṣṭam āryānandenāhaṃ parityakto yan nāma samanvākṛtya na paritrāta ity ||
body.translated_text: [54] At that moment, the great-souled elder <s>Ānanda</s>, girded for accomplishing the purposes of the entire world, and out of compassion, with his divine eye—his mental continuum devoted to observing the actions of infinite beings, deeply pained—saw the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> in this condition. With his mind impelled by compassion, illuminating the entire world with divine radiance, accompanied by a retinue of five hundred <s>Arhats</s>, he suddenly set forth through the sky by supernatural power, filling the firmament like evening clouds in the sky, his body blazing like a mass of splendor of all the worlds, heading toward the cremation ground. King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, standing on the upper terrace of the white palace, saw the elder <s>Ānanda</s> coming with the great assembly of monks, enclosed in a half-moon formation, traveling above through the sky by supernatural power, adorning the firmament like evening clouds, heading toward the great cremation ground. Seeing this, he thought: 'Surely the elder <s>Ānanda</s> has come on account of the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, and having come, he will wish to teach a great, wonderful, and marvelous <s>Dharma</s>. I shall go to the great cremation ground.' Then, immediately paying homage to the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and his retinue, he quickly descended from the palace roof and set forth on foot, accompanied by many hundreds of thousands of beings, to the great cremation ground. At this very time, the executioners were being urged by those king's men with raised weapons: 'Why do you delay? Quickly mount this prince on the stake!' Then those executioners, terrified, said: 'Let us mount the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> on the stake!' And they began to throw him up. The prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, his mind distressed by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, having lost all hope, began to cry out: 'Alas, how terrible! The noble <s>Ānanda</s> has abandoned me, for he has not come to rescue me despite my remembering him!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 137,3 - 141,3
[55] athāsminn antare sthavirānando mahātmā dūrata evāgacchan vyāpinā svareṇa diśaḥ sarvvāḥ samāpūrayan suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ samāśvāsayann uvāca | mā bhair vatsa yuṣmadvidhānam eva vineyānām arthe imam āśīviṣaprakhyaṃ kāyam aham dhārayāmīti tad vatsa mā bhair ahaṃ tvām adyāsmāt saṃṅkaṭāt parimocayiṣyāmi adya bhagavato buddhasya manorathaṃ paripūrayāmi | adya yat tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena sthaviramahākāśyapena ca śāsanam api vinyas taṃ tat saphalī kariṣyāmi | adya tathāgraśrāvakamahātmyam udbhāvayiṣyāmi | adya te manorathaṃ paripūrayāmi | adya tavedam maraṇabhayaṃ saṃsārikañ ca bhayam apanayāmi | adya vicikitsākathaṃ kathāśalyam utpāṭayāmi | adya te kudarśanapaṭalāvaṣṭabdhe netre jñānāñjanaśalākayā śodhyāmi | adya te krodhāgniṃ nāśayāmi | adya tvāṃ vigatarāgatvenācchādāyāmi | adya te kuśalabījaṃ prarohayāmi | adya tvāṃ saṃsārapaṅkād uddharāmi | adya tvāṃ duḥkhasamudrāt uttārayāmi | adya tvāṃ saṃsārakāntāraparyantam upanayāmi || adya te kleśabandhanāni cchinadmi | adya te nivaraṇakapāṭapaṭalaṃ bhinadmi | adya te haṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathā tvam anantakoṭiniyutaśatasahasradurllabhataram aśeṣakleśopakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ prāpsyasi |
body.translated_text: [55] At that moment, the great-souled elder <s>Ānanda</s>, coming from afar, filling all the directions with his all-pervading voice, consoling the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, said: 'Fear not, my child! It is for the sake of trainable beings such as you that I maintain this body, comparable to a venomous serpent. So fear not, my child—today I shall free you from this distress! Today I shall fulfill the heart's wish of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>! Today I shall make fruitful that teaching which was entrusted by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, the Knower and Seer, and by the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>! Today I shall manifest the greatness of the foremost disciples! Today I shall fulfill your heart's desire! Today I shall remove your fear of death and your fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Today I shall pull out the thorn of doubt and perplexity! Today I shall cleanse your eyes, obscured by the film of wrong views, with the collyrium-stick of knowledge! Today I shall extinguish the fire of your anger! Today I shall clothe you with freedom from attachment! Today I shall cause your wholesome seeds to sprout! Today I shall lift you from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Today I shall bring you across the ocean of suffering! Today I shall lead you to the end of the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>! Today I shall cut your bonds of affliction! Today I shall break open the door-panels of your hindrances! Today I shall act in such a way that you shall attain <s>Arhatship</s> (the state of a worthy one)—more difficult to obtain than countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions—through the complete abandonment of all afflictions and secondary afflictions.'

body.text: adya kleśāndhanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ dhakṣyase jñānavahninā |

children.translated_text: Today you shall become one of certain mind, free from fever. [1]

children.text: adya tvaṃ vatsa sahasā janmavṛkṣañ cirāyituṃ |
children.translated_text: Today, my child, you shall swiftly cut down the tree of birth, long-standing,
With the great thunderbolt of knowledge—hard to cut though it be—you shall sever it completely. [2]
The ocean of existence, with its whirlpools of the intoxication of passion, with its waves of pride—

children.text: vīrya plavaṃ samāruhya tvam adya pratariṣyasi |3|
children.translated_text: Mounting the raft of effort, today you shall cross over. [3]
The mountain of suffering, with its passes of birth, its clefts of old age, its caverns filled with death—
With the great thunderbolt of wisdom you shall shatter it. [4]

children.text: kalpakoṭisahasreṣu yan na labdhaṃ tvayā padaṃ |
children.translated_text: That state which you have not obtained in thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages)—

children.text: tad vatsa durlabhataraṃ prāpsyasy adya nirāsravam iti |5|
children.translated_text: That, my child, most rare, you shall attain today: the influx-free state.' [5]

body.translated_text: 'Today you shall burn the entire mass of affliction-darkness with the fire of knowledge;

body.text:
Sva Roy 141,3 - 144,145
[56] athaitat sthavirānandād upaśruta suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro gatapratyāgataprāṇa ivāśvasitaḥ saṃhṛṣitatanuruho gaganatalāsaktadṛṣṭiḥ sthavirānandāvarjitaikamanaso 'bhavat | tatas tai rājapuruṣais te vadhyaghātakā uktāḥ | bhavanta ete bhikṣavo gaganatalam avagāhyāgacchanti | kāruṇikā ete kadācid āgatya vighnaṃ kurvanti | tacchīghram enaṃ kumāraṃ śūle samāropayata | mā vo rājaśāsanātikramān mahān anartho bhaviṣyatīti | tatas te vadhyaghātakāḥ putradārasvajanabandhujīvitavināśabhayabhītāḥ suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram utkṣipya śūle pratiṣṭhāpayitum ārabdhāḥ | tataḥ sthavirānandena sahasaiva tathādhiṣṭhitaṃ yathā tasya śūlasyopari candramaṇḍalapratisparddhi vistīrṇakarṇiakam mahāpramāṇaṃ padmaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ | tasya ca padmasyopari karṇikāyāṃ suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ praryaṅkeṇa niṣannaḥ tañ ca padmakarṇikāyām upari paryaṅkena niṣannam udvīkṣya gaganatalagatair anekair devatāniyutaśatasahasrair hāhākāro muktaḥ |
body.translated_text: [56] Then, having heard this from the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, as if life had gone and returned again, was reassured, his body-hairs standing on end, his gaze fixed on the sky, his mind captivated by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> alone. Then those king's men said to the executioners: 'Sirs, these monks are coming through the sky. They are compassionate—they might come and create an obstacle. Therefore, quickly mount the prince on the stake, lest great misfortune befall you for transgressing the royal order.' Then those executioners, frightened by the threat of destruction to their sons, wives, kinsmen, and relatives, lifted the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> and began to set him upon the stake. Then the elder <s>Ānanda</s> instantly performed a supernatural feat such that upon the top of that stake there appeared a great lotus of vast size, with a broad pericarp rivaling the orb of the moon. And upon the pericarp of that lotus, the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> sat cross-legged. Seeing him seated cross-legged upon the lotus pericarp, many millions of hundreds of thousands of gods in the sky raised a cry of wonder:

body.text: aho śāsanamamāhātmyaṃ sarvajñā(jñasyā)dbhutaṃ hi yata |

children.translated_text: Even a disciple performs such a miraculous feat of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! [1]
By the noble <s>Ānanda</s> today, the greatness has been made manifest aloud,
Performing, just like the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One) himself, something truly supremely wondrous! [2]
When the sun of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) has set, dispelling all the darkness of calamity,
Oh, this glorious sun of the elder <s>Ānanda</s> has risen! [3]
Adorned with the rays of the majesty of his own wisdom and virtues,
By the moon that is the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, the sky-vault of the world [is illuminated]. [4]
The world, shrouded in darkness due to the absence of the light of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One),
Is now properly illuminated by the lamp that is the noble <s>Ānanda</s>. [5]
When the jewel that is the <s>Buddha</s>, endowed with all inconceivable virtues, had disappeared,
The illustrious noble <s>Ānanda</s>, the crest-jewel of the world, has arisen. [6]

body.translated_text: 'Oh, how wondrous is the greatness of the teaching of the Omniscient One!

body.text:
Sva Roy 145,1 - 146,3
[57] atha sthavirānandaḥ śaradamalaśāṅkamaṇḍalātirekadyutiḥ sandhyābbhrapaṭalāvaruddha iva bhāskaraḥ sakalabhuvanalakṣmīpuñja iva dedīpyamānamūrttiḥ svatejasā sūryaprabhān nirbhartsayaṃś pañcārhacchataparivāraḥ samanuprāpto gagatalastha eva suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram āmantrayām āsa |
body.translated_text: [57] Then the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, whose radiance surpassed the spotless orb of the autumn moon, his form blazing like the sun obscured by an evening bank of clouds, like a mass of all the world's splendor, outshining the brilliance of the sun by his own radiance, accompanied by a retinue of five hundred <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones), arrived. While still in the sky, he addressed prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>:

body.text:
vatsa
kadācit karhicit loke utpadyante tathāgatāḥ |

children.translated_text: Teachers of gods and men, possessing the eye [of wisdom], gone beyond conflict. [1]
They who illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> that dispels all suffering—
Suffering, the arising of suffering, and the transcendence of suffering,

body.translated_text:
'My child—
At some time, rarely in the world, <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-gone Ones) arise,

body.text: āryāṣṭāṅgikaṃ mārggaṃ kṣemaṃ nirvāṇagāminaṃ(nam) |2|
body.translated_text: The noble eightfold path, the safe way leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. [2]

body.text: asmindharme deśyamāne sarvaduḥkhavinodane |

children.text: jñānena hatvā hy ajñānaṃ nāgacchanti punarbhavam ity |3|
children.translated_text: Having destroyed ignorance by wisdom, they do not return to further existence.' [3]

body.translated_text: When this <s>Dharma</s> that dispels all suffering is being taught,

body.text:
Sva Roy 146,3 - 148,149
[58] athāsya vacanasya samanantaram eva suvarṇavarṇena kumāreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāmadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphala sākṣāt kṛtaṃ | atha suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ sasyasampanna iva karṣakaḥ | śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaś cakravartirājyapratilambhād iva paramaprītiprāmodyajātaḥ | tatrastha eva kṛtakarapuṭaḥ sthavirānandaṃ pratiṣṭotum ārabdhaḥ |
namas te sthavirānanda namas te sthavirottama |

children.translated_text: Homage to you, O great sage, banner-bearer among the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)! [1]

children.text: aho te karuṇā sphītā aho kāruṇyam uttamaṃ |
children.translated_text: Oh, how abundant is your compassion! Oh, how supreme is this mercy,
By which I have been liberated from this great peril! [2]

children.text: lokanātha iti sthāne śabdas te visṛto bhuvi |
children.translated_text: 'Protector of the world'—fittingly has this name been proclaimed for you on earth,

children.text: bhayārtto yad anātho 'haṃ tvayā nāthena mocitaḥ |3|
children.translated_text: Since I, fearful and helpless, have been freed by you, the protector. [3]
To refresh the world scorched by the nature of suffering, you,
The moon among sages, have risen with cool rays of loving-kindness and compassion. [4]

children.text: tat kṛtaṃ na ca me mātrā na pitrā nāpi bāndhavaiḥ |
children.translated_text: That which was not done for me by my mother, nor by my father, nor by my relatives—

children.text: kalyāṇamitram āgamya tvām ahaṃ yad avāptavān |5|
children.translated_text: Having found you as my spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), I have obtained [that]. [5]
All the doors to lower rebirths are shut; the gate of liberation is opened;
All the oceans [of suffering] are dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over. [6]
<s>Saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), without beginning, middle, or end, fraught with the fear of affliction—

children.text: dhiyā samena guṇitaḥ paryante sthāpitas tvayā |7|
children.translated_text: Measured by wisdom and insight, has been brought to its end by you. [7]
The thorn of [wrong] views, lodged since beginningless time, has been extracted;

children.text: bhiṣagvaram iha prāpya sukhajāto 'smi nirjvara iti |8|
children.translated_text: Having found here the supreme physician, I have become well, free from fever, and filled with joy.' [8]

body.translated_text:
[58] Then, immediately upon hearing these words, prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of a real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Then prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, like a merchant who has obtained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won the battle, was filled with supreme joy and delight as if he had obtained the sovereignty of a universal monarch. Standing right there, with palms joined, he began to praise the elder <s>Ānanda</s>:
'Homage to you, elder <s>Ānanda</s>! Homage to you, foremost of elders!

body.text:
Sva Roy 149,1 - 150,4
[59] tato devatābhiḥ sthavirānandasya mānasam avalokya tatkṣaṇād eva mahāśmaśānam apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ candanavāripariṣiktaṃ surabhidhūpadhūpitaṃ samucchritadhvajapatākātoraṇam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpam ativicitrasurabhikusumāvakīrṇaṃ atiramaṇīyaṃ devānām iva nandanodyānaṃ tatra ca sthavirānandasyārthe nānāratnavinyāsavicitritabhaktiprakāraracitaṃ divyaṃ sarvasauvarṇaṃ sapādapīṭhaṃ mahat siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptaṃ teṣām api pañcānām arhacchatānām arthe divyāny āsanāni prajñaptāni | tataḥ sthavirānando gagatalād avatīrya siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | tāny api pañcārhacchatāny avatīrya prajñapteṣv āsaneṣu niṣaṇṇāni ||
body.translated_text: [59] Then the deities, discerning the mind of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, at that very instant made the great cremation ground free of stones, gravel, and thorns, sprinkled it with sandalwood water, perfumed it with fragrant incense, [adorned it] with raised banners, flags, and arched gateways, hung with festoons of silk garlands, strewn with exceedingly beautiful and fragrant flowers, as delightful as the <s>Nandana</s> garden of the gods. There, for the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, a great, divine, all-golden lion throne with a footstool was prepared, decorated with inlays of various gems in artful patterns. For those five hundred <s>arhats</s> as well, divine seats were prepared. Then the elder <s>Ānanda</s> descended from the sky and sat upon the lion throne. Those five hundred <s>arhats</s> too descended and sat upon the prepared seats.

body.text:
Sva Roy 150,4 - 153,3
[60] rājā cājātaśatrur anekaprāṇiśatasahasraparivāraḥ samanuprāpto yāvat paśyati tām vibhūtiṃ suvarṇavarṇañ ca kumāraṃ candramaṇḍalapratisparddhinaṃ padmasyopari karṇikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ ghanapaṭalanirmuktam iva śaratakālapūrṇacandraṃ suvarṇayūpam iva śriyā jvalantam udvīkṣya paramavismayāvarttitacittasantatiḥ | samuddaṇḍaromakūpaḥ paramapraharṣormmitaraṅgāpūryamāṇavadanakamalaḥ paramaprasādavegāvarjitacittasantatiḥ | sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirānandasya pādayoḥ patitaḥ tataś ca mukhatuṇḍakena caraṇāv anuparimārjyotthāyobhe jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kṛtakarapuṭaḥ sthavirānandam udvīkṣamāṇa uvāca |
body.translated_text: [60] King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of beings, arrived. He then beheld that splendor, and prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, rivaling the orb of the moon, seated upon the pericarp of a lotus—like the full moon of autumn released from a bank of clouds, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post. Looking up, his stream of thought overcome with supreme wonder, his hair standing on end, his lotus-face flooded with waves of supreme delight, his stream of thought carried away by a rush of supreme devotion, he fell at the feet of the elder <s>Ānanda</s> with his whole body. Then, wiping the feet with the tip of his face, rising up, placing both kneecaps on the ground, with palms joined, gazing up at the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, he said:

body.text: namas te paramācārya yenādyaivaṃ prakurvatā |

children.translated_text: Have rescued this people, and I myself have been delivered. [1]

children.text: na samanvāhṛtaś cet syād ahañ cāyañ ca te janaḥ |
children.translated_text: Had you not given thought [to this], both I and this people of yours
Would have been destroyed by the thunderbolt of the cry of 'Shame upon you!' O sage. [2]

children.text: yaditvan na bhaves trātā samāsattva hito muniḥ |
children.translated_text: If you, O sage, devoted to the welfare of beings, had not been the savior,

children.text: aham adyaiva dagdhaḥ syāṃ paścāt tāpadavāgnimā |3|
children.translated_text: I would have been burned this very day by the fire of remorse thereafter. [3]

children.text: aho jñānamahatvan te karuṇā ceyam uttamā |
children.translated_text: Oh, the greatness of your wisdom! And this compassion is supreme!

children.text: adbhutañ cāritaṃ cedam aho samyak prakāśitaṃ |4|
children.translated_text: This conduct is marvelous! Oh, how rightly it has been made manifest! [4]
Having seen this supremely wondrous miracle of yours, O sinless one,

children.text: praśāntim paramāṃ yāto manye naivaṃ tathāgataḥ |5|
children.translated_text: I have attained supreme peace—I think even the <s>Tathāgata</s> [could do] no more than this. [5]

children.text: kṛcchraprāptasya lokasya tvan nāthas tvaṃ parāyaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: For the world in distress, you are the protector, you are the refuge,
You are the benefactor of all beings, tender like the Blessed One himself. [6]

children.text: bhagavantaṃ samālokya yā me prītir abhūt purā |
children.translated_text: The delight that I formerly had upon beholding the Blessed One—

children.text: sa evādya tvāṃ samālokya jinaśāsanadhūrdharam iti |7|
children.translated_text: That same [delight arises] today upon beholding you, the bearer of the yoke of the <s>Jina's</s> teaching.' [7]

body.translated_text: 'Homage to you, supreme teacher, who by acting thus today,

body.text:
Sva Roy 153,3 - 156,5
[61] atha sa rājā sthavirānandanam evam abhistutya samutthāya ca paramapraharṣapūrṇamanās tvaritatvaritaṃ śūlasamīpam upagamya tato hastau prasārya suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ priyaputram iva naṣṭopalabdhaṃ pareṇa premṇā svayam eva tasmāt padmāsanād avatārya gāḍhaṃ pariṣvajya muhur muhaḥ śirasi paricumbate sma | harṣāśruparyākulekṣaṇaś ca suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāram animiṣam abhivīkṣamāṇa uvāca |
body.translated_text: [61] Then the king, having thus praised the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and risen up, his mind filled with supreme delight, went swiftly to the stake. From there, stretching out his hands, he himself took prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> down from that lotus seat, as if he were a beloved son recovered after being lost, and with exceeding affection embraced him tightly and kissed him on the head again and again. With eyes brimming with tears of joy, gazing at prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> without blinking, he said:

body.text: rājyalābhād iva purā na sā prītir abhūn mama

children.text: muktaṃ tvāṃ saṅkaṭād asmād dṛṣṭvā yā varddhate 'dhunā |1|
children.translated_text: As now grows upon seeing you freed from this peril. [1]
This lotus-face of yours, stealing the radiance of the full moon, with eyes like petals of the blue lotus—

children.text: mukhābujam idaṃ putra diṣṭyā paśyāmi te 'dhunā |2|
children.translated_text: By good fortune, O son, I see it now! [2]
Adorned with the endowments of refined complexion, grace, and virtuous qualities,
Possessed of all limbs in perfection—by good fortune I see your form! [3]
By what merciless, evil-souled person was wickedness proclaimed,

children.text: vadhāyāsi parityakto yena tvaṃ vallabho nṛṇāṃ |4|
children.translated_text: That you, beloved of all people, were condemned to death? [4]
Your conduct is endowed with discipline; your speech brings delight to the ear;

children.text: rūpam atyadbhutañ cedaṃ vada kasya na vallabhaṃ |5|
children.translated_text: This form is supremely wondrous—tell me, to whom would it not be dear? [5]

children.text: guṇeṣu kasya pradveṣaḥ ko doṣānuguṇaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Who would have hatred toward [such] virtues? Who is always attached to faults?
Whose heart is hard as adamant? Who is devoid of discernment? [6]
Surely his heart is made of stone, devoid of feeling,

children.text: vyāhṛtaṃ hṛdayaṃ tasya tvaṃ putraka na vallabhaḥ |7|
children.translated_text: That person's heart is broken, to whom you, my child, are not dear. [7]

children.text: pradīptam vajram ārabdhaṃ prakṣeptum mama mastake |
children.translated_text: A blazing thunderbolt was about to be hurled upon my head,

children.text: kaṇṭhe vā niśitaṃ śastraṃ śaktiṃ vakṣyasi vā dhṛḍhāṃ |8|
children.translated_text: Or a sharp weapon at my throat—or will you speak of a powerful spear? [8]

children.text: prapātayitum ārabdhaḥ kena me hy ayaśo 'śaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: By whom was the thunderbolt of infamy about to be cast upon me?

body.translated_text: 'Not even when I first obtained the kingdom did I have such joy

body.text: vadho yenābhyanujñātas tava sarvajanapriya |9|
body.translated_text: By whom was the execution of you, dear to all people, authorized? [9]

body.text: hā kena dāruṇañ vācā karmedaṃ tava kāritaṃ |

children.text: ko me vairānubaddhaḥ syāt kasyāhaṃ na priyo bhaveta |10|
children.translated_text: Who could be my sworn enemy? To whom could I not be dear? [10]

children.text: mṛtyunāliṅgitaḥ ko 'sau prāṇāḥ kasya na vallabhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Who is that one embraced by death? To whom are his own life-breaths not dear?

children.text: yena te vadha ājñaptaḥ śīghram ākhyātum arhasīti |11|
children.translated_text: He who ordered your execution—you should tell me quickly!' [11]

body.translated_text: Alas, by whom was this cruel deed ordered to be done to you with [mere] words?

body.text:
Sva Roy 156,5 - 158,159
[62] atha suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraś cintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | sa ced asya rājña evaṃ kathayāmi pracaṇḍenāmātyena mamedaṃ karma kāritam iti | caṇḍoyaṃ rājā sthānam etad vidyate | yataḥ sāṃpratam eva pracaṇḍam amātyaṃ praghātayati | tat katham atra pratipattavyaṃ || atha vākkarmasvakatāvalambayitavyā | dhruvañ ca mayā pūrvveṣu janmāntareṣu pāpakam akuśalaṃ karma kṛtaṃ yasyāyaṃ vipāko na ca pūrvakarmavipākaṃ muktvā evam anāgaso vadhāya parityajyata iti niścayam upagamya rājānam uvāca |
body.translated_text: [62] Then prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> began to reflect: 'If I tell this king that the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> had this deed done to me—this king is wrathful; this possibility exists: he might execute the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> right now. How then should I act here? One should rather rely upon the principle that deeds are one's own (<s>karmasvakāta</s>). Surely I performed sinful, unwholesome <s>karma</s> (action) in previous births, and this is its ripening. Without the ripening of former <s>karma</s>, one who is innocent is not condemned to death.'
