Having arrived at this conclusion, he addressed the king:

body.text: mayaivaṃ tat kṛtaṃ karma pāpakaṃ pūrvajanmasu |

children.translated_text: Whose ripening of this kind, O king, has come to pass. [1]

children.text: tad aniṣṭañ ca nāmādya svakānām eva karmaṇāṃ |
children.translated_text: Since today I am experiencing the unpleasant

children.text: vipākaṃ paribhuñjāno py ādekṣyāmi kam nv ahaṃ |2|
children.translated_text: Ripening of my own deeds, whom indeed shall I blame? [2]'

body.translated_text: 'It was I myself who performed that sinful <s>karma</s> (action) in previous births,

body.text: ity uktvā sthavirānandasamīpam upagamya sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirānandasya pādayor nipatitaḥ | sthavirānandena cokto vatsa eṣā kāśisundarī dārikā viṣavegenāvaṣṭabdhā tad uttiṣṭhaināṃ satyādhiṣṭhānena svasthī kuru mahājanakāyaś ca pratyāyya iti |
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he approached the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and fell at his feet with his whole body. The elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'My child, this girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> has been seized by the force of poison. Therefore, rise and restore her to health through a declaration of truth (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), and thereby convince the great multitude.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 159,1 - 162,3
[63] atha suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ sthavirānandasya pratiśrutya sarvasattvādhyāśayapravṛttena cetasā satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ | yena me satyena satyavacanenāsyāḥ kāśisundaryā dārikāyā antike mana sūkṣmo 'pi kleśo notpanno rāgo vā dveṣo vā moho vā vihiṃsā vānyatam anyatamo vā caitasika upakleśo 'nena satyena satyavacanena cāsyāḥ śarīraviṣamvilayam upagacchatv ity athaitasmin satyādhiṣṭhānasamanantaram eva kāśisundarīdārikāyāḥ śarīrād viṣaṃ vilayam upagataṃ svasthībhūtaśarīrā ca suptaprabuddhā ivotthitā | tāṃ svasthībhūtaśarīrām utthitām ālokya tena mahājanakāyenānekaiś ca devatāśatasahastrair ekaravenoccair nādo muktaḥ | aho āścaryam aho kumārasyāśayaviśuddhatā | maharddhiko 'yaṃ kumāro mahānubhāvo yatredānīṃ satyādhiṣṭhānabalād iyam anena kāśisundarī dārikā samutthāpitā priyeṇa jīvitenācchāditeti | tataḥ kāśisundarī dārikā samantān nirīkṣitum ārabdhā yāvat paśyati mahāśmaśāne sthavirānandaṃ mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena sārddham arddhacandrākāropagūḍhaṃ | nānāratnapradyotite divye mahati siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaṃ rājāmaṃ ajātaśatrum anekaprāṇiśatasahasraparivāram ātmānañ ca nīlapītalohitāvadātāyāṃ śivikāyām āropitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sambhrāntā cintayituṃ pravṛttā | kim ayaṃ svapnam āho svic cittavibhramaḥ | atha vā kenacid etan māyākarmavidarśitaṃ bhavatīti | yāvat tasyā jñātibhir etad vistareṇa samākhyātaṃ | uktā ca sarvathā yad etat tava jīvitaṃ tat sarvaṃ sthavirānandam āgamyeti
body.translated_text: [63] Then prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, having accepted [the instruction of] the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, with a mind directed toward the aspirations of all beings, began to make a declaration of truth (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>): 'By this truth and truthful word of mine—that toward this girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> not even the subtlest defilement arose in my mind, neither attachment (<s>rāga</s>), nor aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), nor delusion (<s>moha</s>), nor desire to harm (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), nor any other mental secondary defilement (<s>upakleśa</s>)—by this truth and truthful word, may the poison disappear from her body!' Then, immediately upon this declaration of truth, the poison disappeared from the body of the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>. Her body restored to health, she arose as if awakened from sleep. Seeing her risen with body restored to health, that great multitude and many hundreds of thousands of deities uttered a loud cry in a single roar: 'Oh, how wondrous! Oh, the purity of the prince's intention! This prince is of great supernatural power and great might, since now by the power of his declaration of truth he has revived this girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, covering her with the gift of dear life!' Then the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> began to look around in all directions. She saw the elder <s>Ānanda</s> at the great cremation ground, surrounded by a great community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) in a semicircular formation, seated on a great divine lion throne blazing with various gems, and King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of beings, and herself placed upon a palanquin of blue, yellow, red, and white. And seeing this, bewildered, she began to reflect: 'Is this a dream, or is it a disturbance of the mind? Or has this been displayed by someone through magical illusion?' Then her relatives explained to her the whole matter in detail, and said: 'In every way, your life—all of it—is due to the elder <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 162,3 - 167,5
[64] tac chrutvā kāśisundarī dārikā sthavirānande samupajātabahumānā paraṃ prasādaṃ pravedayitum ārabdhā | atha kāśisundarī dārikā udyānaṃ samanusmṛtya pracaṇḍañ cāmātyaṃ udvignamanasā maraṇabhayaviṣādavihvalekṣaṇāvasthān tām eva parāṃ pravedayantī strībhāvam anuśocitum ārabdhā | aho strītvaṃ nāmātijaghanyataraṃ sarvaduṣkhāspadabhūtaṃ | yad āgamy āham imām avasthām anuprāpteti samvignamānasā tvaritam utthāyaikañ ca vastram ādāya sthavirānandasamīpam upagamya tad ekaṃ vastraṃ sthavirānandāya niryātya pādayor nipatya tīvrena prasādavegena sthavirānandaguṇānusmaraṇapūrvvakaṃ satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kartum ārabdhā || yena satyena satyavacanena tvaṃ videhamune | sarveṣāṃ buddhaśiṣyāṇām agraprāpto 'tiśreṣṭho viśiṣṭaḥ pravara uttaro 'nuttaraḥ śrāvakanāgaḥ | śrāvakasiṃhaḥ | śrāvakaṛṣabhaḥ | śrāvakajāneyaḥ | śrāvakapadmaḥ | śrāvakakumadaḥ | śrāvakapuṇḍarīkaṃ | śrāvakasārathiḥ | śrāvakasārthavāhaḥ | śrāvakacandraḥ | śrāvakabhāskaraḥ | śrāvakaratnaṃ | śrāvakacūḍāmaṇiḥ | śāsanakarṇadhāraḥ | śāsanadhūrddharaḥ | arhan kṣīṇāstravaḥ | kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyo 'pahṛtabhāro 'nuprāptasvakārthaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacitto maharddhiko mahānubhāvo mahādakṣiṇīyo 'nena satyena satyavacanenādyaiva me strīndriyam antarddhātu puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhavatu | athaitat satyādhiṣṭhānasamanantaram eva tasyāḥ strīndriyam antarhitaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ | puruṣo babhūva atirupo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko vicitravastrālaṅkṛtaśarīro gaganatalāc cāsyā divyanvicitraṃ manoramaṃ vastravaryam patitum ārabdhaṃ | apīdānīṃ vastravaryeṇa patatā tathā gaganamaṇḍalaṃ saṃcchannaṃ yadā tasmin muhurte tasmin mahāśmaśāne sūryaraśmayo na prajñāyante sma | tatas tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ sthavirānandasyaguṇamāhātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaganatalagatair anekair devatākoṭiniyutaśatasahastrair hāhākāro muktaḥ | aho āścaryam aho 'tyadbhutaṃ | aho sthavirānandasya guṇamāhātmyaṃ | aho udāratā | aho suviśuddhaṃ dakṣiṇīyaṃ kṣetraṃ yatra hi nāmaikavastrapradānamātreṇa praṇidhānasamanantaram eva kāśisundarīdārikāyāḥ strīndriyam antarhitaṃ | puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtamiyañ cedṛśī vibhūtir iti | tatas tābhir devatābhiḥ prasannamanaskābhir divyaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ pātitaṃ | divyāni na vādyāni ca parāhatāni ||
body.translated_text: [64] Having heard this, the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, with great reverence arisen toward the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, began to experience supreme devotion. Then the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, remembering the garden and the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, with an agitated mind and eyes overwhelmed by the despair of fear of death, expressing that very supreme feeling, began to lament the state of womanhood: 'Alas, womanhood is truly the most wretched, the ground of all sufferings! Because of it I have reached this condition!' With an agitated mind, she quickly rose up and, taking a single garment, approached the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, offered that one garment to the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, fell at his feet, and with an intense surge of devotion, preceded by the remembrance of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtues, began to make a solemn declaration of truth: 'By the truth, by this truthful word—you, O sage of <s>Videha</s>, who among all the disciples of the <s>Buddha</s> have attained the foremost position, most excellent, distinguished, supreme, superior, unsurpassed; elephant among disciples, lion among disciples, bull among disciples, thoroughbred among disciples, lotus among disciples, white water lily among disciples, white lotus among disciples, charioteer among disciples, caravan leader among disciples, moon among disciples, sun among disciples, jewel among disciples, crest-jewel among disciples; helmsman of the teaching, bearer of the teaching's yoke; an <s>Arhat</s>, one whose influxes are destroyed, who has done what was to be done, who has accomplished the task, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, whose bonds of existence are completely destroyed, who is perfectly liberated in mind through right knowledge, of great supernatural power, of great might, a great field of merit—by this truth, by this truthful word, may my female faculty disappear this very day and may the male faculty arise!' And immediately following that solemn declaration of truth, her female faculty disappeared and the male faculty arose. He became a man—exceedingly handsome, beautiful, charming, his body adorned with various garments. And from the sky, divine, variegated, delightful, excellent garments began to fall upon him. Indeed, the sky was so covered by the falling excellent garments that at that moment, in that great cremation ground, the rays of the sun were no longer visible. Then, seeing that most wondrous greatness of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtues, which captivated gods and humans, many millions of hundreds of thousands of gods in the sky raised a cry of wonder: 'Oh, how marvelous! Oh, how most wondrous! Oh, the greatness of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtues! Oh, what nobility! Oh, what a supremely pure field of merit, where indeed by the mere offering of a single garment, immediately following the vow, the female faculty of the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> has disappeared and the male faculty has arisen—such is this miraculous power!' Then those gods, with joyful minds, rained down divine flowers, and divine musical instruments were played.

body.text:
Sva Roy 167,5 - 170,3
[65] tataḥ kāśisundaraḥ puruṣaḥ sthavirānandaguṇamāhātmyasāmarthyād abhimanoharam ātmano yathābhilaṣitaṃ sadyo vipākaphalam udvīkṣya paramavismayāvarjitacittasantatiḥ paramaprītiprāmodyajātapraharṣaromāñ cakarkasīkṛtamūrttir utthāyajānumaṇḍaladvayam upanikṣipya bhūmau kṛtakarapuṭaḥ sthavirānandam abhiṣṭotum ārabdhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [65] Then <s>Kāśisundara</s>, now a man, seeing directly the wondrous, heart-captivating fruit of ripening exactly as he had wished, produced by the power of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtuous greatness, with his mental continuum captivated by supreme wonder, his body bristling with the hairs of supreme joy and delight, rose up, placed both knees on the ground, joined his palms, and began to praise the elder <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: namas te durlabhācintya suviśuddhaguṇaiś cita |

children.text: yenādyaivam anāthusya dattam ye jīvitaṃ tvayā |1|
children.translated_text: By whom today, to one who was helpless, life has been granted. [1]

children.text: yadi tvan na bhaves trātā viśuddhajñānalocanaḥ |
children.translated_text: If you had not been the savior, with eyes of pure knowledge,

children.text: kathaṃ prāṇavaśiṣṭaṃ syāṃ tvam me prāṇaprado mune |2|
children.translated_text: How could I have remained alive? You are the giver of my life, O sage. [2]
Oh, the greatness of your virtues! Oh, your desire for the welfare of beings!

children.text: yad evaṃ saṅkaṭād ghorāt paritrātas tvayā janaḥ |3|
children.translated_text: That from such a terrible distress a person has been rescued by you. [3]
Oh, your worthiness as a field of merit—supremely pure and supremely rare—
Where even the offering of a single garment yields such immense value! [4]
Having offered a single garment to you, O great sage,

children.text: yathābhilaṣitaṃ prāptam adya phalam idaṃ śubhaṃ |5|
children.translated_text: I have obtained today this auspicious fruit, just as I wished. [5]

children.text: ādhāram iva yan manye doṣāṇām mahatām api |
children.translated_text: That which I considered the very foundation of great faults—

children.text: tat strītvaṃ tyaktam adyaiva puṃstvaṃ cādhigataṃ mayā |6|
children.translated_text: That womanhood has been abandoned this very day, and manhood has been attained by me. [6]
And this divine-like form, adorned with divine ornaments,
And from the sky fall garments of the finest quality, supremely captivating! [7]

children.text: evaṃ guṇini sukṣetre ye vai kārān na kurvate |
children.translated_text: Those who do not make offerings to such a virtuous and excellent field of merit—

children.text: adhanyā vañcitās te mohādyaiḥ kleśaśatrubhir iti |8|
children.translated_text: Those unfortunate ones are deceived by the enemies of affliction, beginning with delusion.' [8]

body.translated_text: 'Homage to you, O inconceivable one, difficult to encounter, adorned with supremely pure virtues,

body.text:
Sva Roy 170,3 - 171,3
[66] sa eva sthavirānandam abhiṣṭutya karmaphalapratyakṣadarśī cintayām āsa | na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad aham iṣṭāniṣṭakarmaphalapratyakṣadarśī punar apy āgāram adhyāvaseyam iti || sa sthavirānandasya pādayor nipatyovāca || labheyāham ārya svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvañ careyam ahaṃ sthavirasyāntike brahmacaryam iti | sa sthavirānandena pravrājitas tathā ca samanuśiṣṭo yathā yāvat sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ |
body.translated_text: [66] Having praised the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, he, seeing directly the fruits of <s>karma</s>, reflected: 'It would not be fitting for me, who has directly seen the fruits of desirable and undesirable <s>karma</s>, to return again to the household life.' He fell at the feet of the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and said: 'May I, noble one, obtain the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), the full ordination (<s>upasampadā</s>), and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the elder.' He was ordained by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and was so instructed that before long, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 171,3 - 176,3
[67]athāsminn antare divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ sapatnīko 'pi putraviyogaśokaduḥkhābhyāhato rājagṛhasya nagarasya madhye śṛṅgāṭakasya pṛthivyām utthāyotthāyātmānaṃ pātayati | punaḥ punaḥ pṛthivyām āvartanaparivartanaṃ karoti | ubhābhyāṃ pāṇībhyām ātmānaṃ tāḍayati | hā putra hā putreti cārttasvaraṃ virauti sma | aśrauṣīd divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ sthavirānandena gaganatalenāgatya suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ paritrāto mahāśmaśāne āścaryā bhūtāni vartanta iti | śrutvā ca punaḥ sapatniko 'py amṛtā cābhiṣekābhisikta iva paramānanditamanāś cakravarttirājyābhiṣekābhiṣikta iva paramaprītiprāmodyajātaḥ sahasaivotthāya tvaritagatipracārayā rājagṛhān nagarān nirggatya mahāśmaśānam anuprāpto yāvat paśyati suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ rāhugrastavinirmuktaṃ śaratakālapūrṇacandraṃ sthavirānandasamīpe niṣaṇṇaṃ tāñ ca sthavirānandaguṇasāmarthyajanitāṃ vibhūtiṃ tatas tasya tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthavirānande samupajātabahumānaḥ paramaprasādavegāvarjitacittasantānaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirānandasya pādayoḥ patitaḥ | utthāya cobhe jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyām upanikṣipya harṣād aśrūrmibhir āpūryamāṇavadanakamalaḥ | kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ sthavirānandamabhiṣṭotum ārabdhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [67] Meanwhile, the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, together with his wife, stricken by the grief and suffering of separation from their son, in the middle of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at a crossroads, was rising up and throwing himself upon the ground again and again, rolling back and forth on the earth, striking himself with both hands, and wailing in a pitiful voice: 'Oh my son! Oh my son!' The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> heard that the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> had been rescued by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> who had come through the sky, and that marvels were occurring at the great cremation ground. Upon hearing this, together with his wife, as if anointed with the consecration of immortality, with a mind filled with supreme bliss, as if consecrated with the consecration of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), filled with supreme joy and delight, he immediately rose up and, moving with swift pace, left the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and arrived at the great cremation ground. There he saw the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, like the full moon of autumn freed from the grip of <s>Rāhu</s>, seated near the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, and that miraculous power born of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtuous might. Then, seeing that most wondrous marvel which captivated gods and humans, with great reverence arisen toward the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, his mental continuum captivated by the force of supreme devotion, he fell at the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s feet with his entire body. Rising up and placing both knees on the ground, his lotus-face filled with waves of tears of joy, with palms joined, he began to praise the elder <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: aho tvayā mahābhāga māhātmyaṃ samprakāśitaṃ |

children.text: yan mahāsaṅkaṭād ghorāt paritrātas tvayā janaḥ |1|
children.translated_text: That from a terrible, great distress a person has been rescued by you! [1]
Oh, the greatness of compassion! Oh, the excellence of knowledge!
By you, who are like the Omniscient One himself, the pure ones have been made manifest! [2]
Thus this son of ours, from the great ocean of calamity,
Has been properly lifted out by you through the power of compassion and knowledge. [3]

children.text: yadi vāyaṃ tvayādyaiva na samanvāhṛto bhavet |
children.translated_text: If he had not been looked after by you today,

children.text: nimagno duḥkhajambāle sapatnīko hy ahañ ciraṃ |4|
children.translated_text: Together with my wife, I would have been long submerged in the mire of grief. [4]
Through reliance on you from today, O son of the greatly compassionate one,
I have crossed over the ocean of grief for my son and have emerged from the forest of grief. [5]
Freed from the bonds made of grief, released from the prison of grief,
Fallen from the iron cage of grief, liberated from the cage of grief! [6]

children.text: na lagnaḥ śokapaṅke 'dya na kṣataḥ śokakaṇṭakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Today I am not stuck in the mud of grief, not wounded by the thorns of grief,

children.text: na daṣṭaḥ śokasarpeṇa na viddhaḥ śokasāyakaiḥ |7|
children.translated_text: Not bitten by the serpent of grief, not pierced by the arrows of grief! [7]

children.text: na cchinaḥ śokanistriṅśair na prāptaḥ śokaśatrubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Not cut by the swords of grief, not overtaken by the enemies of grief,

children.text: na grastaḥ śokamakarair na dagdhaḥ śokavahninā |8|
children.translated_text: Not seized by the sea-monsters of grief, not burned by the fire of grief! [8]
By your doing this today, this great multitude has been illumined;
Their eyes have been opened and their minds have been delighted. [9]

children.text: ānanda iti nāmedam aho svanvarthatāṅ gataṃ |
children.translated_text: Oh, the name <s>Ānanda</s> (Joy) has truly become true to its meaning,

children.text: yenaivaṃ kurvatā trāṇaṃ paramānanditā vayam iti |10|
children.translated_text: For by your performing this rescue, we have been supremely gladdened!' [10]

body.translated_text: 'Oh, by you, O greatly fortunate one, the greatness has been made manifest,

body.text:
Sva Roy 176,3 - 177,4
[68] atha divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ sthavirānandam abhiṣṭutyotthāya ca suvarṇavarṇasya kumārasya samīpam upagamya sapatnīko 'pi sahagāḍhaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya muhurmuhuḥ pariṣvajate sma | praharṣajāto 'śruparyākulekṣaṇaś ca suvarṇavarṇaṃ kumāraṃ animiṣena samavalokayann uvāca |
body.translated_text: [68] Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, having praised the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, rose up and approached the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>. Together with his wife, he tightly embraced him around the neck, embracing him again and again. With eyes filled with tears of joy, gazing at the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> without blinking, he said:

body.text: śaratpūrṇendubimbaśrīkāntidyutiharambvapuḥ |

children.text: manorathaśatair labdhaṃ diṣṭyā paśyāmi te punaḥ |1|
children.translated_text: Obtained through a hundred wishes—by good fortune I see your face again! [1]
With eyes that are tender, dark, wide, and edged with crimson,

children.text: sthavirānandam āgamya punaḥ paśyāmi te mukham iti |2|
children.translated_text: Through the coming of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, I see your face again.' [2]

body.translated_text: 'Your body has the beauty, splendor, and radiance of the full autumn moon;

body.text:
Sva Roy 177,4 - 181,4
[69] atha suvarṇavarṇaḥ kumāraḥ saṃsāradoṣodvignacetā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya sthavirānandasya pādayor nipatyovāca | sthavira labheyāhaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvañ careyam ahaṃ svākhyātadharmavinaye brahmacaryam iti | sa sthavirānandena pravrājitas tathā ca samanuśiṣṭo yathānena tasminn eva muhūrte sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ prāptaṃ | so 'rhattvaprāptaḥ pūrvaikāṃ janmaparamparām avalokitum ārabdho yāvat paśyaty ātmānam atīva puṇyamaheśākhyaṃ tasyaitad abhavat | kṣuṇo 'haṃ sa cen mayā vijñātum abhaviṣyad ity aham eva puṇyamaheśākhya iti | mayā yāvad āptaṃ dānāni dattāni puṇyāni kṛtāny abhaviṣyan | tad idānīm api sattvānāṃ puṇyeṣu gauravotpādanārthaṃ svaṃ puṇyamahātmyaṃ prakāśayeyam iti | tatas tena tāni vastrāṇi svaśarīrād avatāritāni tatsamanantaram eva cāparāṇi tādṛśāny eva prādurbhūtāni | punaḥ punar avatārayitum ārabdhas tathaiva cāsya punaḥ punaḥ prādurbhavanti | tenāvatāryāvatārya sthavirānandasya purastān mahān vastrarāśiḥ kṛtaḥ | tañ ca teṣām api mahārhāṇām vastrāṇāṃ rāśim abhinavoditadivākarakiraṇvicchuritam iva jāmbunadasuvarṇarāśiṃ kanakāyamānam udvīkṣya sa mahājanakāyaḥ paramavismayāvarjitacittasantatir uvāca | aho āścaryam aho 'dbhutam aho puṇyānāṃ māhātmyam aho sukṛtāni puṇyāni anena mahātmanā | yatra hi nāmaivam avyavacchinnam avatārayato 'pi caiṣām atimahārhāṇāṃ paryantam api nādhigamyata iti | tatas tena mātāpitros tāni vastrāṇi niryātitāni tābhyām api sthavirānandapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgham ādiṃ kṛtvā yāvān asau janakāyo mahāśmaśānaṃ sannipatitaḥ | tatra ca ekaikaḥ prāṇīvastrayugalenācchāditaḥ | suvarṇavarṇasya tu bhikṣoḥ puṇyānubhāvenāsau vastrarāśir naiva kṣīyate |
body.translated_text: [69] Then the prince <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, his mind distressed by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, having obtained permission from his parents, fell at the feet of the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and said: 'Elder, may I obtain the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), the full ordination (<s>upasampadā</s>), and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s> in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' He was ordained by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and was so instructed that at that very moment, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, he attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he began to survey his former succession of births. He saw himself as none other than <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit), and he thought: 'What a loss! If I had known that I myself was <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s>, then as long as I was able, I would have given gifts and performed acts of merit!' 'Even now, for the sake of generating reverence for merit in beings, I should make manifest my own greatness of merit.' Then he removed those garments from his own body, and immediately other garments of the very same kind appeared. He began to remove them again and again, and likewise they kept appearing again and again. Having removed them one after another, he piled up a great heap of garments before the elder <s>Ānanda</s>. Gazing up at that heap of priceless garments, gleaming like a heap of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold glittering with the rays of the newly risen sun, that great multitude, with mental continua captivated by supreme wonder, said: 'Oh, how marvelous! Oh, how wondrous! Oh, the greatness of merit! Oh, what well-done merits this great soul has! For although he removes them continuously, even the limit of these supremely valuable garments cannot be reached!' Then he offered those garments to his parents. And they in turn, beginning with the elder <s>Ānanda</s> at the head of the community of monks and extending to the entire multitude of people that had assembled at the great cremation ground, clothed each living being with a pair of garments. Yet, through the power of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>'s merit, that heap of garments was not at all diminished.

body.text:
Sva Roy 181,4 - 184,185
[70] tataḥ suvarṇavarṇo bhikṣur upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya ṛddhyā rājagṛhan nagaraṃ gatvā madhye śṛṅgāṭakasya suvarṇavarṇānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ svaśarīrād ava(6)tāryāvatārya mahāpramāṇaṃ rāśiṃ kṛtvā svareṇa rājagṛhan nagaram āpūrayann uvāca | bhavanto mayaitāni vastrāṇi parityaktāni yasya vo yāvadbhiḥ prayojanaṃ sa tāvanti pratigṛhṇātv iti | śrutvā tatkṣaṇād evānekāni prāṇiśatasahastrāṇi sannipātitāni | yāvat paśyanti nagaramadhye śṛṅgāṭakasya teṣāṃ suvarṇapītānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ atimahāpramāṇaṃ rāśiṃ aruṇkiraṇaparāmṛṣṭam iva jāmbūnadasuvarṇarāśim iva milimilāyamānam āyuṣmāntaṃ ca suvarṇavarṇam uttaptakāñcanagiriśṛṅgam iva paramayā śriyā jvalantaṃ gaganatalagatam udvīkṣya sa mahājanakāyaḥ paramavismayāvarjitacittasantatiḥ paramapraharṣormitaraṅgāpūryamāṇavadanakamalaś cintayām āsa aho āścaryam aho 'dbhutaṃ tat kiṃ punar anena mahātmanā kṛtaṃ bhaved yenāyam evaṃ maharddhiko mahānubhāvo yadi ca vayaṃ jānīmo vayam api tat kuryāmahe yena vayam apy evaṃ maharddhikāṃ syāma iti | samutpannābhilāṣāḥ sandehadolāruḍhāś ca parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | teṣām etad abhavad eṣa eva mahātmā maharddhiko mahānubhāvaḥ siddhavrato divyajñānasamanvāgataś ca etam eva paripṛcchāma iti | tato 'sau janakāyaḥ paramavismayotphullalocanaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo gaganatalāsaktadṛṣṭir āyuṣmantaṃ suvarṇavarṇam ekaraveṇa praṇamyovāca |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, rising up into the sky by supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), went to the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and in the middle of the crossroads, removing from his own body golden-colored garments one after another, made a great heap, and filling the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> with his voice, he said: 'Good people, these garments have been relinquished by me. Whoever among you has need of any amount, let him take that much.' Upon hearing this, at that very instant hundreds of thousands of beings assembled. They saw in the middle of the city crossroads that exceedingly great heap of golden-yellow garments, shimmering like a heap of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold touched by the rays of dawn. And looking up at the Venerable <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> situated in the sky, blazing with supreme glory like the peak of a mountain of refined gold, that great multitude, their mental continuum captivated by supreme wonder, their lotus-like faces flooded with waves of supreme joy, thought: 'Oh, how marvelous! Oh, how wondrous! What deed was done by this great soul that he has such great supernatural power and might? If we knew, we too would do it, so that we too might possess such great supernatural power.' With desire aroused, mounted on the swing of doubt, they began to confer among themselves. This thought arose in them: 'This very great soul, of great supernatural power and might, has fulfilled his vows and is endowed with divine knowledge. Let us ask him.' Then that multitude, their eyes wide open with supreme wonder, with joined palms, their gaze fixed on the sky, bowing to the Venerable <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> with one voice, said:

body.text: upetas tvaṃ mahābhāga divyena jñānacakṣuṣā |

children.text: yenaivaṃ tvaṃ maheśākhyas tvaṃ samākhyātum arhasi |1|
children.translated_text: by which you are called 'Great Lord'—you should deign to explain. |1|

children.text: yena prāpnoti sampattim iha loke paratra ca |
children.translated_text: By which one attains prosperity in this world and the next,

children.text: bhogānāñ ca guṇānāñ ca tān svayaṃ khyātum arhasī ti |2|
children.translated_text: and [the prosperity] of enjoyments and virtues—please declare those yourself.' |2|

body.translated_text: 'You are endowed, O greatly fortunate one, with the divine eye of knowledge;

body.text:
Sva Roy 185,2 - 196,3
[71] tatas tān sa mahāsattvaḥ karuṇākṣiptamānasaḥ |

children.translated_text: gladdening [them] with a great voice, filling the directions with his sound: |1|

children.text: amum evārtham uddiśya mayedaṃ darśitaṃ hi vaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'With reference to this very matter, I have shown this to you;
I shall tell you in due order—hear these words of mine: |2|

children.text: puṇyair āpnoti sampattim iha loke paratra ca |
children.translated_text: By merit (<s>puṇya</s>) one attains prosperity in this world and the next,

children.text: bhogānāñ ca guṇānāñ ca puṇyaiś cāham maharddhikaḥ |3|
children.translated_text: and of enjoyments and virtues; and by merit I have great supernatural power. |3|

children.text: yadi vo na priyaṃ duḥkhaṃ priyāś ca sukhasampadaḥ |
children.translated_text: If suffering is not dear to you, and if the attainments of happiness are dear,

children.text: kṣipraṃ kurudhvaṃ puṇyāni sukhaṃ puṇyasya sañcayaḥ |4|
children.translated_text: quickly perform meritorious deeds—the accumulation of merit is happiness. |4|

children.text: yā kācit sukhasampattir iha loke paratra ca |
children.translated_text: Whatever attainment of happiness there is, in this world and the next,

children.text: prāpyate nivṛttiś cāpi puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |5|
children.translated_text: and cessation [of suffering] too—that is the fruit of merit alone. |5|

children.text: dhaninaḥ śreṣṭhino viprāḥ sārthavāhādayaś ca yān |
children.translated_text: The rich, the merchants, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, the caravan leaders, and others—

children.text: bhuñjate vipulān bhogān puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |6|
children.translated_text: the abundant enjoyments they enjoy—that is the fruit of merit alone. |6|
Delightful wives, servants, sons, friends, and other prosperities—

children.text: yad bhavanti manuṣyāṇāṃ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |7|
children.translated_text: that these exist for humans—that is the fruit of merit alone. |7|
The attainment of beauty and charm that captivates hearts and eyes—

children.text: labdhvā yad rājante martyāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |8|
children.translated_text: that mortals shine having obtained it—that is the fruit of merit alone. |8|
An unbreakable retinue, inexhaustible wealth of generosity—

children.text: labhante khalu yan martyāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |9|
children.translated_text: that mortals indeed obtain these—that is the fruit of merit alone. |9|
Remembrance of past lives, good fortune, learning, persuasive speech—

children.text: prāpnuvanti manuṣyā yat puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |10|
children.translated_text: that humans attain these—that is the fruit of merit alone. |10|
Extensive wealth of enjoyments, always accompanied by kinsmen—

children.text: yan martyā muñjate hṛṣṭāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |11|
children.translated_text: that mortals enjoy [these] with joy—that is the fruit of merit alone. |11|
That humans have innumerable wealth and prosperity,

children.text: niḥsapatnāḥ sthirāś caiva puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |12|
children.translated_text: unrivaled and stable—that is the fruit of merit alone. |12|

children.text: yad uttarakurau dvīpe hy amamā aparigrahāḥ
children.translated_text: That on the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, without the notion of 'mine,' without possessions,

children.text: manuṣyā niyatāyuṣkāḥ puṇyānām eva eva tat phalaṃ |13|
children.translated_text: humans have a fixed lifespan—that is the fruit of merit alone. |13|
That [they eat] rice that grows as grain, unsown, of great value—

children.text: manuṣyā bhuñjate tatra puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |14|
children.translated_text: that humans enjoy it there—that is the fruit of merit alone. |14|
Wishing-garments, variegated, and ornaments that are there—

children.text: ācchādayanti manujāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |15|
children.translated_text: that men clothe themselves [with these]—that is the fruit of merit alone. |15|

children.text: yat tad uttarakurau dvīpe manuṣyās tad anantaraṃ |
children.translated_text: That on the island of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, humans, immediately after [death],

children.text: cyutā devā bhaviṣyanti puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |16|
children.translated_text: will become gods when they pass away—that is the fruit of merit alone. |16|
That the <s>Nāga</s>s, like sons of gods, enjoy divine prosperity

children.text: pātāle bhuñjate divyāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |17|
children.translated_text: of ambrosia-food and the like in the netherworld (<s>pātāla</s>)—that is the fruit of merit alone. |17|
That by the power of splendor, etc., having attained royal sovereignty like that of gods,

children.text: manujendrā virājante puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |18|
children.translated_text: human kings shine forth—that is the fruit of merit alone. |18|
That kings of the earth, having attained universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartitvam</s>) by their power,
shine like <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods—that is the fruit of merit alone. |19|
The entire [sovereignty over] all humans, the prosperity of the seven jewels and the like—

children.text: buṅkte yac cakravartī ca puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |20|
children.translated_text: that the <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) enjoys—that is the fruit of merit alone. |20|

children.text: tridaśendra samāṃ lakṣmīṃ prāpya yat paribhuṅkte |
children.translated_text: That having attained fortune equal to that of the lord of the thirty [gods],

children.text: vemacitrādayo daityāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |21|
children.translated_text: <s>Vemacitra</s> and other <s>Daitya</s>s (titans) enjoy it—that is the fruit of merit alone. |21|
The four world-guardians (<s>Lokapāla</s>s)—<s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) and others—

children.text: bhuñjate muditāś citrāṃ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |22|
children.translated_text: enjoy their wondrous splendor with delight—that is the fruit of merit alone. |22|
That the gods enjoy the splendor of <s>Nandana</s> and other garden-parks

children.text: yat sārddhaṃ devakanyābhiḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |23|
children.translated_text: together with celestial maidens—that is the fruit of merit alone. |23|
The wondrous prosperity of divine kingship and the like—that the lord of the thirty [gods]

children.text: yat sadā mudito bhuṅkte puṇyānām eva tatphalam |24|
children.translated_text: (<s>Tridaśādhipa</s>) always enjoys with delight—that is the fruit of merit alone. |24|
That they enjoy divine pleasures as desired—

children.text: vimānavāsino devāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |25|
children.translated_text: the gods who dwell in celestial palaces—that is the fruit of merit alone. |25|
That certain gods surpass other gods in ten respects—

children.text: devebhyo 'py adhikā devā puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |26|
children.translated_text: lifespan, color, strength, and the like—that is the fruit of merit alone. |26|
The supreme, wondrous, divine wealth of enjoyments at the summit of the desire realm (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>)—

children.text: kāmadhātvīśvaro bhuṅkte puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |27|
children.translated_text: that the lord of the desire realm enjoys—that is the fruit of merit alone. |27|
Desired pleasures among gods and humans

children.text: labhante yad ayatnena puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |28|
children.translated_text: that are obtained effortlessly—that is the fruit of merit alone. |28|
That <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, meditators in the realms of <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: prāpnuvanty uttamaṃ saukhyaṃ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |29|
children.translated_text: attain supreme bliss—that is the fruit of merit alone. |29|

children.text: dhyāyino dhyānajaṃ yac ca tṛṣṇākṣayasukhañ ca yat |
children.translated_text: The bliss born of meditation for the meditators, and the happiness of the destruction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>)—

children.text: prāpnuvanti sukhaṃ śāntiṃ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |30|
children.translated_text: that they attain such happiness and peace—that is the fruit of merit alone. |30|
That the disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>s) of the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s> become endowed with fierce virtues,

children.text: maharddhikā mahātmānaḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |31|
children.translated_text: of great supernatural power, great souls—that is the fruit of merit alone. |31|
That great souls, after the passage of hundreds of <s>kalpa</s>s (cosmic ages),

children.text: bodhiṃ pratyekasambuddhāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |32|
children.translated_text: attain enlightenment as <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s (solitary awakened ones)—that is the fruit of merit alone. |32|
That they become perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>s, adorned

children.text: bhavanti samyaksambuddhāḥ puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |33|
children.translated_text: with immeasurable, incomparable virtues—that is the fruit of merit alone. |33|
Women graced with beauty and youth, ornaments of families along with men—

children.text: striyaḥ puṇyair avāpyante puṇyānām eva tat phalaṃ |34|
children.translated_text: are obtained through merit—that is the fruit of merit alone. |34|

children.text: puṇyair avāpyate svargaḥ puṇyasya apsarasaḥ phalaṃ |
children.translated_text: Through merit, heaven is attained; <s>Apsaras</s>es (celestial nymphs) are the fruit of merit;
through merit, all desired fulfillments of wishes are obtained. |35|

children.text: puṇyair avāpyate tīkṣṇā tathā ca vimalā matiḥ |
children.translated_text: Through merit, a sharp and also a pure intellect is obtained;

children.text: puṇyair āyatanaiḥ śraddhāḥ puṇyaiḥ paṭutarā smṛtiḥ |36|
children.translated_text: through merit, faith through the sense faculties; through merit, a keener memory. |36|
Through merit: amiability, eloquence, a beautiful voice, and fame;
all auspicious splendors of virtue are obtained through merit. |37|

children.text: na tad asti sukhaṃ loke yat puṇyair nādhigamyate |
children.translated_text: There is no happiness in the world that is not attained through merit;
therefore, by those who desire happiness, the accumulation of merit must always be performed. |38|

children.text: svalpaṃ puṇyaṃ mayā kṛtvā vipaśyini tathāgate |
children.translated_text: Having performed a small merit in the time of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>,
I obtained the desired fruit, exceedingly abundant. |39|
In the six classes of gods, sovereignty, lordship, and supremacy—
for thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s of births, I enjoyed happiness. |40|
Immeasurable, unrivaled, and supreme among humans likewise—
as a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) and the like, I have enjoyed wealth and prosperity. |41|
By the greatness of that merit, wherever I was reborn,
there and there I became one called 'Great Lord,' endowed with happiness. |42|
Beautiful, endowed with virtues, with a face fragrant like a lotus,
dear and of persuasive speech, delightful, accompanied by gods. |43|
Even now, of that very merit, [behold] this desired
prosperity of virtues such as beauty—see this, which delights the mind! |44|
I was born in a great family, of great wealth, of great enjoyments,
my body draped in garments of golden hue. |45|
From my entire body emanate fragrances resembling sandalwood;

children.text: gandho nīlotpalasyaiva tathā vāti mukhāc ca me |46|
children.translated_text: and from my mouth too wafts the fragrance of a blue lotus. |46|
Whatever I desire of wealth in garments, jewels, and the like—

children.text: tac ca saṃṅkalpamātreṇa mama sarvaṃ samṛdhyati |47|
children.translated_text: all that is fulfilled for me by mere wish alone. |47|

children.text: pravrajyā ca mayā labdhā sākyasiṃhasya śāsane |
children.translated_text: And I have obtained ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) in the teaching of the Lion of the <s>Śākya</s>s;

children.text: arhatvañ ca mayā prāptaṃ śītībhūto 'smi nirvṛtaḥ |48|
children.translated_text: and I have attained <s>Arhatship</s>—I am cooled, I am at peace. |48|

children.text: iyam me paścimā jātir mmama nāsti punarbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is my final birth; for me there is no further existence;
I shall not come again; I shall dwell without any support. |49|
The extensive ripening-fruit of that karma by which I was propelled—

children.text: tasya nāvaimi paryantam adyāpy evaṃvidho 'pi san |50|
children.translated_text: I cannot perceive its limit, even now being of such a nature. |50|

body.translated_text: Then that great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), his mind impelled by compassion,

body.text:
Sva Roy 196,3 - 197,3
[72] tadatyadbhutam aparimitam acintyaṃ ca tasya sakāśāt puṇyamāhātmyaṃ śrutvānekaiḥ prāṇikoṭiniyutaśatasahastraiḥ paramaprasādavegāvarjitacittasantatibhir bhagavacchāsanasatkāraparāṅmikhair api yathecchaṃ dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā praṇidhānāni kṛtāni | athāyuṣmān suvarṇavarṇāsya mahājanakāyasyaivam aneka prakāraṃ puṇyeṣu gauravotpādanārthañ ca puṇyamāhātmyaṃ prakāśya
body.translated_text: Then, having heard from him the exceedingly wonderful, immeasurable, and inconceivable greatness of merit, many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of beings, their mental continuum captivated by a surge of supreme faith, turned toward honoring the teaching of the Blessed One, gave gifts as they wished, performed meritorious deeds, and made aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). Then the Venerable <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, having thus revealed the greatness of merit in many ways for the purpose of generating reverence toward merit in that great multitude,

body.text:
Sva Roy 197,3 - 199,5
[73] tata evopari vihāyasā sadyo mahāśmaśānam āgatya sthavirānandapramukham bhikṣusaṃgham anuparipāṭikayā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | rājñā cājātaśatruṇā śrutaṃ yathā kila pracaṇḍenāmātyenerṣyāprakṛtenodyāne kāśisundaryā dārikāyā ayañ cāyañ cānarthaḥ kṛtaḥ | suvarṇavarṇasyābhyākhyānaṃ dattvā niraparādha eva vadhāya parityakta iti | śrutvā ca punas tīvrakrodhaparyākulekṣaṇo bhṛtyān āmantrayate bhavantaḥ | kathan nāmānena durātmanaivaṃ vyavaharttavyaṃ savarthā parityakto me pracaṇḍo 'mātya iti | pracaṇḍaś cāmātyas tatraiva sannipatito 'bhūt | atha pracaṇḍo 'mātya etad rājño vacanam upaśrutya maraṇabhayaviṣādavihavalekṣaṇaḥ pravepamānaḥ sarvāṅgāvayavaḥ sahasaivotthāya niṣpalāyitum ārabdho mahājanapradviṣṭo 'sau tasyopary anekāni praṇiśatasahasrāṇi pradhāvitāni samantāc ca parivārya mahājanakāyena gṛhīto gṛhītvā ca kharacapeṭapārṣṇiprahārādibhis taṃ tāḍayitum ārabdhāḥ | sa tāḍyamānaḥ pragāḍhaduḥkhavedanābhyāhato vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ āryānanda paritrāsyasva mām anātham atrāṇam aśaraṇam aparāyaṇaṃ nirālokaṃ priyeṇa jīvitenācchādayeti ||
body.translated_text: then immediately went through the sky to the great charnel ground. Having saluted the assembly of <s>bhikṣu</s>s headed by the Elder <s>Ānanda</s> in due order, he sat down in one place. King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> heard that the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, jealous by nature, had committed this and that outrage against the courtesan <s>Kāśisundarī</s> in the garden, and having made a false accusation against <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, had handed over the innocent one to execution. Hearing this, with eyes agitated by intense anger, he summoned his attendants: 'Sirs! How could this evil-minded one act in such a manner? My minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> is dismissed from all positions!' And Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> had arrived at that very assembly. Then Minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, hearing these words of the king, his eyes bewildered by the distress of mortal fear, trembling in all his limbs, suddenly rose and began to flee. Detested by the great multitude, many hundreds of thousands of beings rushed upon him, surrounded him on all sides, and the great crowd seized him. Having seized him, they began to beat him with sharp slaps, kicks, and other blows. Being beaten, struck by deep painful sensations, he began to cry out: 'Noble <s>Ānanda</s>, rescue me! I am unprotected, without defense, without shelter, without support, without light—cover me with dear life!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 200,1 - 203,204
[74] sthavirānandena cāsau mahājanakāyo 'bhihito bhavanto mainaṃ praghātayatāhaṃ rājānam ajātaśatrum anusaṃjñāpayiṣyāmīti | tatas tena mahājanakāyenāsau sthavirānandavacanam upaśrutya pratimuktaḥ sthavirānandaś ca rājānaṃ nirīkṣitum ārabdhaḥ | rājovāca | kim ājñāpayasīti | sthavirānandenoktaṃ | mahārāja muñcainam iti 200,5-201,1 rājovāca | samayato muñcāmi yadi svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya sthavirānandasyaṃ yāvajjīvam upasthānaṃ karotīti | sthavirānandenoktam evam astv iti | sa ca tena janakāyena nirdayaṃ tāḍitaḥ | pragāḍhaduḥkhavedanābhyāhato murcchitas tiṣṭhati | sthavirānandena cāyuṣmān suvarṇavarṇo 'bhihitaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānena pracaṇḍasyāmātyasya śarīrād duḥkhavedanāṃ prastambhayeti | athāyuṣmān suvarṇavarṇaḥ sarvasattvahitādhyāśayapravṛttena cetasā satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ | yena satyena satyavacanenāsya pracaṇḍasyāmātyasyaivam atyantāpakāriṇo 'py antike mama sūkṣmo 'py āghāto notpannaḥ | tena satyena satyavacanenāsya śarīrād duḥkhavedanā pratipraśrabhyatām iti | satyādhiṣṭhānasamanantaram eva pracaṇḍasyāmātyasya śarīrād duḥkhavedanā pravigatā svasthībhūtaśarīraś ca samutthāya bhagavacchāsane samupajātabahumānaḥ sthavirānandasamīpam upagamya pādayor nipatyovāca | labheyāhaṃ sthavirānanda svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvañ careyam ahaṃ sthavirānandasyāntike brahmacaryam iti | sa sthavirānandena pravrājitas tathā ca svam anuśiṣṭo yathā tena tasminn eva muhūrte sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ prāptaṃ | so 'rhatvaprāpto gaganatalam abhyudgamya vicitraiḥ prātihāryam mahājanamanānsi prahlādayan gaganatalād avatīrya sthavirānandapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ anuparipāṭikayā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: [74] And the elder <s>Ānanda</s> addressed that great multitude: 'Sirs, do not execute him! I shall persuade King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>.' Then that great multitude, upon hearing the words of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, released him. And the elder <s>Ānanda</s> began to look at the king. The king said: 'What do you command?' The elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Great King, release this man.' The king said: 'I shall release him on one condition — if, having gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, he serves the elder <s>Ānanda</s> for life.' The elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'So be it.' He had been mercilessly beaten by that crowd. Stricken by intense painful sensations, he lay there unconscious. The elder <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the venerable <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>: 'By a truth-act (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>), cause the painful sensation to subside from the body of the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, with a mind engaged in the intention of benefiting all beings, began to perform a truth-act: 'By this truth, by this truthful utterance — although this minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> has done me extreme harm, not even the slightest resentment has arisen in me toward him. By this truth, by this truthful utterance, may the painful sensation subside from his body!' Immediately upon that truth-act, the painful sensation departed from the minister <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>'s body. Having recovered and risen with his body restored to health, with great reverence arisen toward the teaching of the Blessed One, he approached the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, fell at his feet, and said: 'May I, elder <s>Ānanda</s>, obtain ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>! May I practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>!' He was ordained by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and so instructed that at that very moment, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, he attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he rose into the sky and, performing various miracles, gladdened the minds of the great multitude. Descending from the sky, he saluted the assembly of monks headed by the elder <s>Ānanda</s> in due order and sat down to one side.

body.text:
Sva Roy 204,1 - 205,5
[75] tatas tad atyadbhutaṃ sthavirānandasya mahātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā parat sthavirānande 'tyartham abhiprasannā | tatas tāṃ parṣadaṃ tathābhiprasannmanaskām ālokya sthavirānandena tathā vidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrais mahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ | kaiścit srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptaṃ | yāvad arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ | kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni | kaiścid yāvadbuddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbharā vyavasthitā divākareṇa ca sārthavāhena sapatnīkena satyāni dṛṣṭāni | anekaiś ca devatāśatasahastrais tatas tābhir devatābhiḥ prasannamanasmabhiḥ divyaṃ vastravaryaṃ pātitaṃ | divyāni ca vādyāni parāhatāni divyaiś cotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndārakādyair jānumātreṇocchrena sarvaṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ vicitraiḥ puṣpair avakīrṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: [75] Then, having witnessed that most wondrous greatness of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, the entire assembly became supremely devoted to the elder <s>Ānanda</s>. Then, seeing that assembly with minds so well-disposed, the elder <s>Ānanda</s> delivered such a <s>Dharma</s> teaching that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great distinction. Some attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti-phala</s>), up to some who directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Some generated the aspiration for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening, and some were established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>. The caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> together with his wife saw the truths (<s>satyāni</s>). And many hundreds of thousands of deities — those deities, with gladdened minds, caused divine garments of the finest quality to rain down. Divine musical instruments were played, and with divine <s>utpala</s>, lotus, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>māndāraka</s>, and other flowers, knee-deep in height, the entire great cremation ground was strewn with varied blossoms.

body.text:
Sva Roy 205,5 - 208,5
[76] atha rājā 'jātaśatrus tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprasādāvarjitacittasantāna udānam udānayām āsa | aho āścaryam aho 'tyadbhutaṃ aho āryānandena svaguṇamāhātmyaṃ prakāśitaṃ aho tathāgataśāsanamāhātmyam udbhāvitaṃ aho yat tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena sthaviramahākāśyapena cāsya śāsanaṃ vinayas taṃ tat saphalīkṛtaṃ || aho tathāgatāditya 'staṅgate āryānandabhāskareṇa svaguṇakiraṇajālair udyotitā diśaḥ | aho tathāgataśaśiny anityatāsurendrarāhuṇā graste āryānandacandreṇa svam atimayūkhavisarair vaineyakumudavanāni prabodhitāni | aho tathāgataviyogatīkṣṇaduḥkhārkakiraṇasantapitaḥ sthavirānanda_mahāmeghena svavacanāmṛtavaryeṇa prahlādito lokaḥ | aho tathāgatasya manorathāḥ samyakparipūritāḥ | aho tathāgataśāsanakarṇadhāratvaṃ prakāśitaṃ | aho tathāgataśasanadhūrddharatvaṃ prakāṭīkṛtaṃ | aho agraḥ śrāvakaḥ śabdaḥ saphalīkṛtaḥ | anenaivātyadbhutena svaguṇamāhātmyaṃ sāmarthyād antasattvahitasampādanena sarvajñaguṇamāhātmyaṃ prativivṛtaṃ | aho darśitānena mahātmanā tasya bhagavato mahākāruṇikasya pratyupakārabuddhir ity ||
body.translated_text: [76] Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having witnessed that most wondrous miracle capable of converting both gods and humans, with the stream of his mind captured by supreme devotion, uttered an exclamation: 'Oh, how wonderful! Oh, how supremely marvelous! Oh, the greatness of the noble <s>Ānanda</s>'s own virtues has been made manifest! Oh, the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching has been displayed! Oh, that which was entrusted — the teaching and discipline — by that Blessed One, the Knower and Seer, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, and by the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, has today been made fruitful! Oh, when the sun of the <s>Tathāgata</s> has set, the directions have been illuminated by the effulgence of the rays of the noble <s>Ānanda</s>'s own virtues! Oh, when the moon of the <s>Tathāgata</s> has been seized by the <s>Rāhu</s> of <s>Indra</s>'s impermanence, the lotus-groves of trainable beings have been awakened by the overflowing beams of the moon of the noble <s>Ānanda</s>! Oh, the world, scorched by the fierce and painful rays of separation from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, has been refreshed by the great cloud of the elder <s>Ānanda</s> with the supreme nectar of his words! Oh, the aspirations of the <s>Tathāgata</s> have been perfectly fulfilled! Oh, the role of helmsman of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching has been made manifest! Oh, the bearing of the yoke of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching has been made clear! Oh, the designation of foremost disciple has been made fruitful! By this most wondrous display, the greatness of his own virtues — through the power of accomplishing the welfare of beings at all times — has revealed the greatness of the qualities of the Omniscient One! Oh, this great soul has demonstrated the spirit of gratitude toward that greatly compassionate Blessed One!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 208,5 - 211,5
[77] atha rājā sthavirānandena praśādavegāvarjitacittasantatiḥ | sthavirānandasamīpam upagamya sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirānandasya pādayor nipatitaḥ | utthāya ubhe jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyām upanikṣipya prasādaromāñcakarkaśīkṛtamūrtiḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ sthavirānandam abhiṣṭotum ārabdhāḥ |
body.translated_text: [77] Then the king, with the stream of his mind captured by the force of devotion to the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, approached the elder <s>Ānanda</s> and prostrated with his entire body at the feet of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>. Rising, placing both knees upon the ground, his body bristling with the hair-raising thrill of devotion, with palms joined together, he began to praise the elder <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: namas te puruṣaśreṣṭha namas te śrutaśāgarāḥ |

children.translated_text: Homage to you, O wondrous and inconceivable bearer of the yoke of the <s>Jina</s>'s teaching! [1]
The greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching has indeed been perfectly manifested,

children.text: acintyam adbhutaṃ te 'dya kurvatā jagate hitaṃ |2|
children.translated_text: by you who today perform what is inconceivable and wondrous for the welfare of the world! [2]

children.text: yat tad bhagavatā cāryakāśyapena ca dhīmatā |
children.translated_text: That which the Blessed One and the wise noble <s>Kāśyapa</s>

children.text: śāsanaṃ tvayi vinyastaṃ tad adya saphalīkṛtaṃ |3|
children.translated_text: entrusted — the teaching placed in your care — has today been made fruitful. [3]
This most wondrous and inconceivable great [deed], performed for the welfare of beings,
has today reflected in you the greatness of the qualities of the Omniscient One. [4]

children.text: kiñ citraṃ yadi sambuddhaḥ sarvārthaṃ kṛtavāṃs tathā |
children.translated_text: What wonder if the perfectly enlightened one accomplished all purposes thus?

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca mahākaruṇiko hy asau |5|
children.translated_text: For he was omniscient, all-seeing, and greatly compassionate. [5]

children.text: idañ citrataraṃ manye śrāvakeṇa satā tvayā |
children.translated_text: This I consider even more wonderful — that by you, a true disciple,
with the [same] great compassion, such a great deed for the welfare of beings has been accomplished. [6]

children.text: aho sulabdhalābho 'haṃ māgadhaś ca jano hy ayaṃ |
children.translated_text: Oh, how fortunate am I, and this people of <s>Magadha</s> too,

children.text: yeṣām evaṃ pramattānāṃ tvaṃ hitāvahitaḥ sadā |7|
children.translated_text: for whom, though we are heedless, you are always devoted to bringing benefit! [7]
Rightly has the <s>Tathāgata</s> placed this teaching in your care,
by whom today, just as by the <s>Sugata</s> himself, something truly supremely wondrous has been done! [8]
Then, amazed at the greatness of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>'s virtues,
remembering the perfectly enlightened one, he made obeisance, saying: [9]
Homage to you, O great hero, O perfectly enlightened one, O supreme among bipeds!

children.text: yasya te śrāvako 'py evaṃ sadā sattvahitodyataḥ |10|
children.translated_text: Whose disciple too is thus always devoted to the welfare of beings! [10]
The greatness [of the teaching] has been proclaimed aloud and perfectly by the <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: aśūnyam iva manyāmas tvayaināṃ janatāṃ yatheti |11|
children.translated_text: we consider this world as if not empty, since you [remain] with these people.' [11]

body.translated_text: Homage to you, O best of men! Homage to you, O ocean of learning!

body.text:
Sva Roy 211,5 - 213,214
[78] tato rājā sthavirānandaṃ papraccha sthavira kiṃ divākareṇa sārthavāhena sapatnīkena karma kṛtaṃ | yasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ sasaṃvṛttaḥ | bhagavacchāsane ca satyadarśanaḥ kṛtaḥ | kāśisundareṇa pracaṇḍena ca bhikṣuṇā kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yenāḍhyo mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāto bhagavacchāsane ca pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ | suvarṇavarṇena ca bhikṣuṇā kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ | yasya karmaṇo vipāke nādya mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ | evamabhirupo darśanīyaḥ | prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopeta uttaptasuvarṇavarṇayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ | sarvajanamanonayanaharaḥ suvarṇavarṇair vastrair avaguṇṭhitavigrahaḥ | kāyāc cāsya candanagandho vāti | mukhāc ca nīlotpalagandho janmani cāsya vastravaryaṃ karṇikārakusumavaryaṃ ca patitaṃ | tāni ca vastrāṇi suvarṇavarṇāni evam atyārtha maharddhiko mahānubhāvo bhagavacchāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti |
body.translated_text: [78] Then the king asked the elder <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Elder, what <s>karma</s> was performed by the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s> together with his wife, by the ripening of which <s>karma</s> he became wealthy, of great riches, of great resources? And [by what <s>karma</s>] was he brought to the seeing of the truths in the teaching of the Blessed One? By the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Kāśisundarī</s> and the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, what <s>karma</s> was performed by which [she/he] was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great resources, and having gone forth in the teaching of the Blessed One, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the complete abandonment of all afflictions? And by the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, what <s>karma</s> was performed, by the ripening of which he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great resources, so handsome, beautiful, charming, endowed with all limbs and secondary limbs, possessed of a beauty of complexion like refined gold, captivating the minds and eyes of all people, his body wrapped in golden-yellow garments? And from his body emanates the fragrance of sandalwood, and from his mouth the fragrance of blue lotus, and at his birth a rain of finest garments and finest <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers fell, and those garments were golden in color — thus supremely endowed with great supernatural power and great might, having gone forth in the teaching of the Blessed One, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?'

body.text:
Sva Roy 214,1-3
[79] sthavirānandaḥ kathayati | mahārājā ebhir eva pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu |
karmāṇi kṛtāni yāvat phalanti khalu dehināṃ ||
body.translated_text: [79] The elder <s>Ānanda</s> replied: 'Great King, by these very ones, previously in other births, <s>karmas</s> were performed, which indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 214,3 - 215
[80] bhūtapūrvaṃ mahārāja ita ekanavate kalpe bhagavāṃ vipaśyī nāma tathāgato loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasamampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniḥsṛtya viharati bandhumatīyake dāve |
body.translated_text: [80] 'Long ago, Great King, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) from now, a Blessed One named <s>Vipaśyī</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One), a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a charioteer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He had gone forth from the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> and was dwelling in the <s>Bandhumatīyaka</s> grove.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 215,1 - 216,1
[81] tena khalu samayena bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ karṇo nāma sārthavāhaḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇapratisparddhī bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ agrakulikas tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītaṃ | sa tayā sārddhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā samvṛtā yāvat karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ pañcavaṇikaśataparivāro mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [81] 'At that time, in the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, there lived a caravan leader named <s>Karṇa</s>, who was wealthy, of great riches, of great resources, with vast and extensive possessions, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches, the foremost householder in the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing. Together with her he enjoyed pleasures, delighted, and made merry. As he enjoyed, delighted, and made merry, his wife became pregnant. Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, accompanied by a retinue of five hundred merchants, descended into the great ocean.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 216,1 - 218,2
[82] sa ca garbho yathā vṛddhisu gacchati | tathā karṇasya sārthavāhasya yad āvārīgataṃ kṣetragataṃ deśāntaragataṃ vārthajātaṃ tatra kiñcid agninā dagdhaṃ kiñcic caurair apahṛtaṃ kiñcit pauruṣeyā gṛhītvā niḥpalānāḥ | yāvat sārthavāhapatnī paripūrṇe kāle prasūtā dārako jātaḥ kṛṣṇacchavir atyantavirūpo 'ṣṭādaśabhir avalakṣaṇair dūṣitagātras tasya kāyān mukhāc ca tādṛśo 'tyantaviraso gandhaḥ pravātum ārabdho yaṃ ghrātvā tadgṛhasthāḥ parijanāḥ paraṃ vaimukhyam upagatāḥ | tasya dārakasya jātamātrasya tasmin gṛhe 'gniḥ prādurbhūto yena tad gṛhaṃ niravaśeṣañ ca svāpateyaṃ dagdhaṃ | sārthavāhapatnī kathañcid dārakam ādāya tasmād gṛhān nirgatā | yadā ca so 'gnis tad gṛhaṃ niravaśeṣañ ca svāpateyaṃ dagdhvā svayam eva nirvāṇaḥ | tadā sārthavāhapatnī tatrārddhabhagne khaṇḍāvavarake praviśya paṭārddhaṃ pṛthivyāṃ prasārya dārakaṃ śāyitvā dīrgham uṣṇañ ca niḥśvasya karṇaṃ sārthavāham anusmṛtya rodituṃ pravṛttā | hā kaṣṭam īdṛśo me viparyayaḥ samupasthita iti |
body.translated_text: [82] 'And as that embryo grew, so did the fortunes of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> — whatever was in his warehouses, in his fields, in other regions, his various merchandise — some of it was burned by fire, some stolen by thieves, some seized by officials who then fled. In due time, the caravan leader's wife gave birth. A boy was born — of dark complexion, extremely ugly, with his body marred by eighteen inauspicious marks. And from his body and mouth there began to emanate such an extremely unpleasant odor that the household servants, upon smelling it, became utterly averse. At the very moment of that boy's birth, a fire broke out in that house, by which the house and all the property were completely burned. The caravan leader's wife, somehow taking the boy, escaped from that house. When that fire, having completely burned the house and all the property, extinguished itself, the caravan leader's wife entered a half-ruined, dilapidated shelter, spread half a cloth on the ground, laid the boy down, and heaving a long, hot sigh, remembering the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, began to weep: "Alas, how terrible — such a reversal of fortune has befallen me!"'

body.text:
Sva Roy 218,2 - 219,4
[83] karṇasya sārthavāhasya ye dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyās te tāṃ vipattiṃ dṛṣṭvā yāmo mā vayam api vinaṅkṣyāma iti bhītāḥ karṇasya sārthavāhasya patnīm apahāya niḥpalānāḥ | tatraikā preṣyadārikā saṃlakṣayati | mayā karṇasya sārthavāhasya gṛhe naikaprakārā sampad anubhūtā | na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad aham asyām avasthāyāṃ sārthavāhapatnīm anātham ekākinīṃ cchorayitvā niḥpalāyeyam iti | saivaikā sārthavāhapatnyāḥ pārśve 'vasthitā | tasyāś ca sārthavāhapatnyāḥ sarvan tat svāpateyam agninā dagdham ekadaivasikam api bhoktavyan nāsti |
body.translated_text: [83] 'The slaves, servants, laborers, and workers of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, seeing that calamity and thinking, "Let us go before we too perish!" — frightened, they abandoned the wife of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> and fled. There, one maidservant reflected: "I have experienced manifold prosperity in the house of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>. It would not be fitting for me to abandon the caravan leader's wife — unprotected, alone — and flee in this condition." She alone remained at the side of the caravan leader's wife. And for that caravan leader's wife, all her property having been burned by fire, there was not even a single day's food to eat.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 219,4 - 221,3
[84] tataḥ sā preṣyadārikā kakarṇasya sārthavāhasya ye suhṛtsambandhibāndhavās teṣāṃ sakāśaṅ gatvā kathayati bhavantaḥ | karṇasya sārthavāhasya patnyā idṛśy avasthā varttate | yogodvahanaṃ kuruteti | yata eva te tasyā yogodvahanaṃ kartum ārabdhās tata evaiteṣām api kuleṣv anarthaśatāni prādurbhūtāni | tair upalakṣitam ayaṅ karṇasya sārthavāhasya putro 'tyantaṃ na maṅgalo 'syāpuṇyasāmarthyāt karṇasya sārthavāhasya sarvo gṛhavibhavādivistaro vināśaṅ gatas tad yadi vayam apy asya yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyāmo 'smākam api gṛheṣu na cirād eveyam īdṛśy avasthā bhaviṣyati | tadyathā karṇasya sārthavāhasya | sarvathā na tasya yuktaṃ nāmāpi grahītum api tu taiḥ sā preṣyadārikābhihitā na bhūyas tvayāsmanniveśanāny upasaṃkramitavyānīti ||
body.translated_text: [84] Then that servant-girl went to the friends, relatives, and kinsmen of <s>Karṇa</s> the caravan leader and said: 'Good sirs, the wife of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> is in such a state. Please provide support for her.' But from the very moment they began to provide support for her, hundreds of misfortunes arose in their households as well. They realized: 'This son of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> is extremely inauspicious. By the power of his demerit, all the household wealth and possessions of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> have been destroyed. If we too provide support for him, before long this same condition will befall our households as well—just as it did the caravan leader <s>Karṇa's</s>. It is not proper even to utter his name.' And so they told the servant-girl: 'You must never again come to our dwellings.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 221,3 - 222,4
[85] sā tair nirbhatsitā cintayām āsa | idānīṃ sārthavāhapatnī sarveṇa sarvaniśakrandā jātā | katham atra pratipattavyam | athavā gṛhīto 'yaṃ mayā bhāraḥ sutarām evādhunā sārthavāhasya patnī paripālayitavyeti | tataḥ paragṛhāṇi gatvā bhṛtakayā karma kartum ārabdhā | tatra ca yan mūlyaṃ labhate tena sārthavāhapatnīm ātmānañ ca dārakañ ca poṣayitum ārabdhā | tasya ca dārakasya paramavirūpatvād virūpa iti nāma vyavasthāpitaṃ | daivāt sā preṣyadārikā pratidivasam apacīyamānaṃ mūlyaṃ pratilabhate | tatas te trayaḥ prāṇino 'ti kṛcchreṇa yāpayitum ārabdhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: [85] She, having been rebuffed by them, reflected: 'Now the caravan leader's wife has become utterly destitute. What should be done here? But I have taken up this burden; all the more so must I now protect the caravan leader's wife.' Then she began to go to others' houses and work as a hired laborer. And with whatever wages she earned, she began to support the caravan leader's wife, herself, and the child. Because of the child's extreme ugliness, the name <s>Virūpa</s> (Ugly) was established for him. By fate, the servant-girl received diminishing wages day by day. So those three beings began to subsist with extreme difficulty.

body.text:
Sva Roy 222,4 - 224,5
[86] sārthavāhapatnī saṃlakṣayati | ahaṃ hi sarvair dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaiḥ suhṛtsambandhibāndhavaiś ca parityaktā yata kiñcin mama jīvitaṃ sarvaṃ tadenāṃ preṣyadārikām āgamya | eṣā hi me mātṛkalpā snehena | tat kiyantaṃ kālam ekākinī karma kurvāṇā sā parikhedaṃ gamiṣyati | yāvac ca mūlyaṃ labhate | tāvatā na śakyate yāpayituṃ | tad aham api svakarmāparādham anubhavāmy aham api bhṛtikayā karma karomīti vicintya tayā preṣyadārikayā saha paragṛhāṇi gatvā bhṛtikayā karma kartum ārabdhā sā paramasukumārā kṣudduḥkhādiparipīḍitā ca karma kurvāṇā muhur muhur moham upagacchati | tataś ca parikhinnā dīrgham uṣṇañ ca niḥśvasya karṇaṃ sārthavāham anusmṛtya rodituṃ pravṛttā | hā kaṣṭam īdṛśo me viparyayaḥ samupasthito yan nāma sakalanagarotkṛṣṭā śrīsampadam anubhūyedānīm ihaiva janmani sakalanagara-uttamā bhūtvā paragṛheṣu bhṛtikayā karma kurvāṇā mahad duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pratyanubhavāmīti |
body.translated_text: [86] The caravan leader's wife reflected: 'I have been abandoned by all servants, slave-women, laborers, attendants, friends, relatives, and kinsmen. Whatever life remains to me, it is all due to this servant-girl. She is like a mother to me in her affection. For how long can she, working alone, avoid exhaustion? And the wages she earns are not enough for us to subsist on. So I too shall experience the consequences of my own past deeds; I too shall work for wages.' Having thus reflected, she went with the servant-girl to others' houses and began to work for wages. She, being extremely delicate, tormented by hunger, pain, and other sufferings, fell into a swoon again and again while working. Then, exhausted, sighing long and hot, remembering the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, she began to weep: 'Alas, what misery! Such a reversal of fortune has befallen me—that I, who was the most eminent in the entire city and enjoyed the splendor of wealth, now in this very lifetime, having been the most exalted in the whole city, am working for wages in others' houses and experiencing great suffering and misery!'

body.text:
Sva Roy 224,5 - 227,228
[87] tāñ ca tathā duḥkhaparipīḍitāṃ rudantīm ālokya sā preṣyadārikā rodituṃ pradattā | hā kaṣṭam ihaiva janmani sārthavāhapatnī kāśiśūkṣmātivicitrām varadhāraṇī vividhasurabhigandhakusumamālāvibhūṣitagātrī | naikasugandhadravyayojitamukhavāsakāvāsitakapolā apsarasa iva nandanavanodyānagatā | annapānavastrālaṅkārādibhir dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavādīn yathārhaṃ samvibhajya_ idānīm ihaiva janmani uddhṛtaśiraskā malapaṭaladigdhagātrī kṣudduḥkhādiduḥkhena pariśuṣkasarvagātrāvayavā saṭitasāṭakātyantamalinena khaṇḍacoṭakena yūkāśataniketabhūtena pracchāditakaṭipradeśā sakalanagarādhamā bhūtvā paragṛheṣu bhṛtikayā karma kurvāṇā mahad duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pratyanubhavaty aho bhāgyaviparyayaḥ | aho cañcalā bhogasampadaḥ | aho karmaṇāṃ vaicitryam ity āha ca |
body.translated_text: [87] Seeing her thus tormented by suffering and weeping, the servant-girl too began to cry: 'Alas, what misery! In this very lifetime the caravan leader's wife—who [formerly wore] garments of fine <s>Kāśi</s> silk, exceedingly beautiful, adorned with various fragrant flower garlands on her body, her cheeks perfumed with many kinds of fragrant mouth-freshening preparations, like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> garden, distributing food, drink, garments, ornaments, and other things appropriately to servants, slave-women, laborers, attendants, friends, relatives, and kinsmen—now in this very lifetime, with disheveled hair, her body smeared with layers of dirt, all her limbs withered by the suffering of hunger and other pains, her hip-region covered with a torn and extremely filthy rag that has become a dwelling for hundreds of lice, having become the lowest in the entire city, working for wages in others' houses, experiences great suffering and misery. Oh, what a reversal of fortune! Oh, how unstable are riches! Oh, the diversity of <s>karma</s> (deeds)!' And she spoke:

body.text: paṭaṃśukādīn prāvṛtya sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitā |

children.text: apsarā iva yā pūrvam idaṃ rathyāmukhaṅ gatā |1|
children.translated_text: Went to the mouth of this street like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph)— [1]

children.text: tad evaṃ sāmprataṃ yātā saiva bhāgyaviparyayāt |
children.translated_text: That same one has now come to this, by reversal of fortune,
Her body stained with dirt, wearing a torn rag. [2]

children.text: devakanyeva yā pūrvaṃ puṃsāṃ netrāmṛtaṃ hy abhūt |
children.translated_text: She who formerly, like a divine maiden, was nectar to the eyes of men—

children.text: pretīṃ vā sāṃprataṃ dṛṣṭvā tām evodvijate manaḥ |3|
children.translated_text: Seeing her now, as if she were a <s>pretī</s> (female hungry ghost), the mind recoils in horror. [3]
She who formerly, by her wealth, was the foremost of the city—
That same one has today fallen to the most extreme destitution, [lower] even than the wretched. [4]
She who formerly enjoyed great prosperity with delight—

children.text: imām adya daśāṃ prāpya saiva śocati duḥkhinī |5|
children.translated_text: Having reached this condition now, that same one grieves in misery. [5]
Oh, the cruelty of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence)! Oh, the impermanence of prosperity!

children.text: yad evaṃ sukhitā bhūtvā duḥkhabhājanatāṅ gateti |6|
children.translated_text: That having been happy, she has come to be a vessel of suffering!' [6]

body.translated_text: 'She who formerly, wrapped in fine silk and other garments, adorned with all ornaments,

body.text:
Sva Roy 228,1 - 231,5
[88] tataḥ sārthavāhapatnī tayā preṣyadārikāyā saha anayānupūrvyā paragṛheṣu bhṛtikayā karma kartum ārabdhā | virūpasya ca kumārasyāpuṇyādhipatyena prātidivasam apacīyāmānaṃ mūlyaṃ labhate | yāvad apareṇa samayenā sūryāstaṃ divasaṃ karma kārayitvā na kiñcil labhyate | yāvat karma 'pi na kaścit kārayati | yāvat sārthavāhapatnī tatyā preṣyadārikayā saha sañjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhā | apīdānīṃ karmāpi na kaścit kārayati | sarvathā bhikṣām aṭāma iti | te mallakam ādāya bhikṣām aṭitum ārabdhā | yadā ca virūpaḥ kumāraḥ paryaṭituṃ samartho jātaḥ tadā tasya mātrābhihitaṃ putra tvam idānīṃ svayam eva bhikṣām aṭitvā bhuṅkṣveti | tayā tasya mallako dattaḥ | sa taṃ mallakam ādāya vīthīm avatīrṇaḥ | tañ cātikṛṣṇaṃ virasacchavim atyantavirūpam aṣṭādaśabhir avalakṣaṇair vidūṣitagātram avalokya loko 'tyantavimukho jāto 'dhomukhaḥ prakrāmati | sa yeṣāṃ gṛhadvāraṃ gacchati te tasya tad ativirasaṃ kāyād gandham āghrāya sahasaiva nāśāpuṭadvayaṃ pidhāya kāṣṭhapāṣāṇaśarkarādibhis tāḍayitvā niṣkāśayanti śīghram asmād gaccheti | sa jaṅgama iva nagaravistārajambāle yatra yatra gacchati tatra tatra kāṣṭhapāṣāṇaśarkarādibhis tāḍayitvā niṣkāśyate | saikabhiṣām apy alabdhvā kāṣṭhapāṣāṇaśarkarādibhis tāḍitas tena mallakena bhagnena krandamāno mātur antikam āgatya bhṛśataramanyumān bhūtvā vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | tataḥ sā taṃ dṛṣṭvodvignā urasi prahāraṃ dattvā kathayati |
body.translated_text: [88] Then the caravan leader's wife, together with the servant-girl, in this gradual descent, began to work for wages in others' houses. Due to the dominion of the demerit of prince <s>Virūpa</s>, she received diminishing wages day by day. Until one day, after working until sunset, she received nothing at all. Then no one would even give them work. Then the caravan leader's wife began to confer with the servant-girl: 'Now no one even gives us work. We shall beg for alms in every way.' Taking a bowl, they began to beg for alms. When prince <s>Virūpa</s> had become able to walk about, his mother told him: 'Son, from now on you yourself shall beg for alms and eat.' She gave him a bowl. He took that bowl and descended into the street. Seeing him—extremely dark-complexioned, of repulsive appearance, supremely ugly, his body disfigured by eighteen inauspicious marks—the people became utterly averse and walked away with downcast faces. Wherever he went to a house-door, the people there, smelling the extremely repulsive odor from his body, immediately closed both nostrils and, striking him with sticks, stones, gravel, and such, drove him out: 'Go away from here quickly!' Like a moving plague throughout the city's extent, wherever he went, he was struck with sticks, stones, gravel, and such, and driven away. Without obtaining even a single alms, struck by sticks, stones, and gravel, with his broken bowl, weeping, he came back to his mother and, filled with extreme rage, began to cry out. Then she, seeing him, with anguish, beating her chest, said:

body.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ kasya te putra aparāddhan tu kim bhavet |

children.text: kṛpām apāsya yenaivaṃ prahṛtaṃ tvayi duḥkhite |1|
children.translated_text: That casting aside compassion, they have thus struck you in your suffering? [1]'

body.translated_text: 'Alas, what misery! Against whom, O son, have you offended, and what could it be,

body.text: tato virūpaḥ kumāraḥ sasvaraḥ prarudann uvāca |
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Virūpa</s>, weeping aloud, said:

body.text: yeṣāṃ yeṣāṃ gṛhadvāram ahaṃ gacchāmi yācituṃ |

children.text: te te kaṭhallapāṣāṇaiḥ kāṣṭhādyais tāḍayanti mām iti |2|
children.translated_text: They all strike me with thorns, stones, sticks, and such.' [2]

body.translated_text: 'To whichever house-door I go to beg,

body.text:
Sva Roy 231,5 - 234,235
[89] tac chrutvā sārthavāhapatnī virūpaṃ kumāraṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya sasvaraṃ prarudantī provāca |
body.translated_text: [89] Hearing this, the caravan leader's wife embraced prince <s>Virūpa</s> at the neck and, weeping aloud, said:

body.text: nūnaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā ghoraṃ pāpaṃ putrānyajanmaṣu |

children.translated_text: For you, utterly helpless, are thus beaten by others. [1]

body.translated_text: 'Surely you committed terrible sins, O son, in other births,

body.text: dhik kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ |
body.translated_text: Fie, what misery, alas!

body.text: imam atyantavirasaṃ saukhyavivarjitaṃ |

children.text: dīnaṃ yācantam ālokya kṛpotpannā na cetasi |2|
children.translated_text: Pitiful and begging—does no compassion arise in your hearts? [2]

children.text: hā hatāsmi vinaṣṭāhaṃ kena te putra mallakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alas, I am ruined, I am destroyed! By whom, O son, has your bowl been broken—
The bowl of one whose body is broken, who lives by alms alone? [3]

children.text: pitrā mātrā vimuktasya muktasya ca gṛhāśramāt |
children.translated_text: Abandoned by father and mother, expelled from the household life—

children.text: kena putra dayāṃ hitvā tava bhagno 'dya mallakaḥ |4|
children.translated_text: By whom, O son, casting aside mercy, has your bowl been broken today? [4]
For one whose entire livelihood is destroyed, who is forsaken by friends and people—

children.text: mitran nātho guruś caiva bhagnas te kena mallakaḥ |5|
children.translated_text: Your friend, your protector, your teacher—by whom has your bowl been broken? [5]

children.text: hā putra kena vā vīryaṃ tvayi darśitam āture |
children.translated_text: Alas, O son, by whom has valor been displayed against you, who are afflicted,

children.text: dīne ca hā hato 'si putraka hataḥ pūrvakarmaṇā svena |6|
children.translated_text: And pitiful? Alas, you are destroyed, my child, destroyed by your own former <s>karma</s> (deeds)! [6]

children.text: hā putra mṛdu śūraḥ kaḥ kasya kṛpā nāvagāhatehṛdayaṃ |
children.translated_text: Alas, O son, who is a hero against the gentle? Whose compassion does not penetrate the heart?
Whose heart is [hard as] stone and rock? Tell me today! [7]

children.text: hā kathaṃ tvāṃ parāhantuṃ dīnaṃ mukhaśatair hataṃ |
children.translated_text: Alas, how does the mind of the world dare to strike you,
Who are pitiful, struck by a hundred blows, begging for alms, afflicted by suffering? [8]
Exhausted by hunger and thirst, deprived of all prosperity,

children.text: rogaduḥkhābhitaptaṃ hā hataṃ ko hantum udyataḥ |9|
children.translated_text: Tormented by disease and suffering—alas, who is prepared to strike one already stricken? [9]
Wretched, with a pitiful face, weeping, oppressed by hunger,

children.text: saṃśuṣkakaṇṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvādya kṛpā kena kṛtā na te |10|
