children.translated_text: With parched throat—seeing [you] today, who has not felt compassion for you? [10]
How were you struck, O son, by those intoxicated with the pride of birth?
By whom today, when you are overcome by pain and extremely suffering, has compassion been abandoned? [11]

children.text: hā tvayā yat kṣudhārtena bhikṣayā samupārjitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Alas, that which you, tormented by hunger, had obtained through begging—

children.text: stokam annaṃ tad apy adya śvabhiḥ kākaiś ca bhakṣitaṃ |12|
children.translated_text: Even that small amount of food has today been eaten by dogs and crows! [12]

children.text: hā putra mandabhāgyāham adhunā kiṃ karomi te |
children.translated_text: Alas, O son, I am of wretched fortune—what can I now do for you,
[Undone] by evil deeds committed before, by fate's unkind acts?' [13]

body.translated_text: Seeing this one, supremely wretched, devoid of all happiness,

body.text:
Sva Roy 235,1 - 244,2
[90] evaṃ sā 'nekaprakāram ātmananam anuśocantī tasyaiva khaṇḍāvavarakasyāgratas taṃ putraṃ virūpaṃ rudhiradhārāvaśiktāṅgaṃ pariṣvajyātibahusaṅkāraśarkarāmedhyasthāṇukaṇṭakānvitāyāṃ bhūmau niṣādya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ pāṇinā madayitum ārabdhāḥ | yāvat sā vīthīmadhyena gacchataḥ paśyaty anekān śreṣṭhiputrān sārthavāhaputrāṃś cānyāṃś cotsadān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn kāśikadukūlakoṭambakakauśeyasūkṣmātimahārhavicitravastraharṣakaṭakakeyūrāṅgadakuṇḍalahārārddhahāravicitrālaṅkārasamalaṅkṛtaśarīrān vividhavikacasurabhikusumakalāpavibhūṣitavigrahāṃs tāṃś cātmīyam anatikaṣṭām avasthām ālokya tañ ca virūpaṃ putraṃ tathātidīnavadanaṃ dīrgham uṣṇañ cābhiniśvasya sāśrekṣaṇātidīnair vacobhir uccaiṃ provāca |
body.translated_text: [90] Thus lamenting in many ways, she sat down before that very broken hovel, embracing her son <s>Virūpa</s>, his body drenched with streams of blood, on ground covered with heaps of rubbish, gravel, filth, stumps, and thorns, and slowly began to soothe him with her hand. Then she saw, passing through the middle of the street, many sons of wealthy merchants, sons of caravan leaders, and other eminent <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, their bodies adorned with garments of fine <s>Kāśi</s> silk, <s>dukūla</s> cloth, <s>koṭambaka</s> fabric, <s>kauśeya</s> silk, fine and exceedingly precious and variegated garments, bracelets, armlets, upper-arm ornaments, earrings, necklaces, half-necklaces, and various ornaments, their forms embellished with various blooming fragrant flower garlands. And seeing her own supremely miserable condition and that ugly son with his extremely pitiful face, sighing long and hot, with tearful eyes, in an extremely pitiful voice she spoke aloud:

body.text: sampannaikasatākīrṇe ratnaiḥ sāgarasannibhaiḥ |

children.text: kule suviprule bhūtvāpy anubhūya sukhaṃ paraṃ |1|
children.translated_text: And having enjoyed supreme happiness in a splendid lineage, [1]
We two have become sharers of misfortune, dwelling in a pile of refuse,
We two who, even with great difficulty, cannot obtain food when hungry. [2]
An ocean of grief, terrifying with waves of a net of suffering, filled with hundreds of fierce crocodiles of torment—

children.text: hā hā hatā veti vimuktanādaṃ dāridratoyaughanidhiṃ praviṣṭau |3|
children.translated_text: Alas, alas, 'I am ruined!'—uttering such cries, we have entered the flood-reservoir of poverty. [3]
Teeming with thousands of various crocodiles of calamity, unstable with terrifying waves of misfortune,
Fierce with the fear of great piercing disease—we have entered the river of poverty. [4]
Strewn with rocks of suffering and sharp diseases, its groves filled with the roaring of lions of torment,
Filled with hundreds of nesting-places of the birds of grief—we have arrived at the abode of the suffering of poverty. [5]

children.text: nūnaṃ purā sādhujane na dattaṃ dānaṃ pramādaskhalitāśayābhyāṃ |
children.translated_text: Surely in the past we two, with minds stumbling through heedlessness, did not give gifts to virtuous people,

children.text: dīnāv idānīm iha mandabhāgyau paśyāva yad dṛptamukhāni nityaṃ |6|
children.translated_text: For now, pitiful and of wretched fortune, we always behold proud faces. [6]

children.text: prāyeṇa yācanakāyācanakaṃ na dattaṃ klībesu bhāgyarahiteṣu vimohitābhyāṃ |
children.translated_text: We, deluded, did not give to the timid and fortune-forsaken who begged,

children.text: āvāsamātravikalāv api yena jātau klībau yato vyasanam ugrataraṃ prapannau |7|
children.translated_text: For we two have become destitute of even a place of shelter, timid, having fallen into the most severe calamity. [7]

children.text: nūnaṃ pṛthivyāṃ gurusammatān yān saṃprāpya satkṛtya vimānitās te |
children.translated_text: Surely we obtained [and then] disrespected those revered as elders on this earth,

children.text: yenādhunāvān tu vimānanīyau jātau janāsyādya vipattibhājau |8|
children.translated_text: For now we two have become worthy of disrespect by people, sharers of misfortune. [8]
Surely we struck many restrained ones in former births,
For these people now strike us with stones and clods. [9]
Surely the elders were formerly led to the path of abuse,
For this extreme, terrible contempt has arisen among people. [11]
We two did not give garments to guests in former births,

children.text: vastrāṇi yena vāsāṃsi na bhavanty adhunāvayoḥ |12|
children.translated_text: For now we two have no clothing. [12]
Many people were made to cry with sounds of weeping,

children.text: yena bandhuvihīnau hi ciraṃ rodiva duḥkhitau |13|
children.translated_text: For we two, bereft of kinsmen, weep in suffering for a long time. [13]
A bed covered with fine coverlets was not given in the past,
For we sleep on the ground strewn with gravel and stones. [14]

children.text: āsanāni vicitrāṇi na ca dattāni sādhuṣu |
children.translated_text: Various seats were not given to the virtuous,
For our seat is the earth, beset with many thorns. [15]

children.text: pūrvaṃ nopānahau dattau na ca yānaṃ sukhāvahaṃ |
children.translated_text: Previously, sandals were not given, nor a vehicle bringing comfort,
For we wander on ground covered with thorns.' [16]

children.text: āvāsamatsratayā khalu naiva dattaṃ prāyeṇa cārthini jane gṛhavāsamātraṃ |
children.translated_text: Out of attachment to one's own dwelling, indeed nothing was given, nor even mere shelter to the needy people;

children.text: ugrāṃśupaṅktiparirājitamadhyabhāgaṃ saṃkārakūṭam iha yena vayaṃ prapannāḥ |17|
children.translated_text: Therefore we have arrived at this rubbish heap, its middle portion scorched by rows of fierce sun-rays. |17|
Having first beheld those with dried throats and parched cheeks and faces, with minds longing for drink,

children.text: nūnan na dattām iti teṣu jālaṃ suśītaṃ yenādhunā vayam atīva viśuṣkavaktrāḥ |18|
children.translated_text: Surely cool water was not given to them — therefore now our mouths are exceedingly dry. |18|

children.text: naivá_annam athirni jane kṛpaṇe pradattanṃ na jñātayo na ca suhṛn na ca bandhuvargāḥ |
children.translated_text: Not even food was given to the wretched people; neither relatives, nor friends, nor kinsmen [were helped];

children.text: satkṛtya vānnavidhinā paribhojitāś ca teneha bhakṣyarahitau viparibhrāmavaḥ |19|
children.translated_text: Nor were they honored and fed according to proper rites of hospitality — therefore here we two wander devoid of food. |19|
Those skilled in understanding others' welfare were surely angered by [our actions] in previous lives in many ways;

children.text: yeneha sāmpratam api tu itare 'pi loke ākrośabhājanaparatvam upāgatāḥ smaḥ |20|
children.translated_text: Therefore now, even in this and the next world, we have become vessels of reproach. |20|
By us two, many people were surely, out of the intoxication of pride in birth,
Struck, though virtuous — therefore we are now born as donkeys. |21|
In the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), the medicine that removes fear of all diseases,

children.text: bhaiṣajyaṃ na purā dattaṃ yena rogābhi pīḍitau |22|
children.translated_text: Was not given [by us] before — therefore we are afflicted by diseases. |22|

children.text: na snāpitā pitṛvayasyajanā na mātā āpyapitā na guravo na ca dīnalokaḥ |
children.translated_text: Our father's companions were not bathed [in honor], nor was mother nourished, nor were teachers [served], nor the destitute [helped];

children.text: āsnānapānarahitau vidhinā prajātau yeneha duḥkhaśatabhāgyahatāv anāthau |23|
children.translated_text: Therefore by fate we are born devoid of bathing and drink, afflicted by hundreds of sorrows, orphans. |23|
Exhausted by hunger and thirst, deprived of food and clothing,
Tormented by the suffering of disease — who indeed will protect us two? |24|

children.text: kasya dāsau bhavāvo 'dya kasya vā paricārakau |
children.translated_text: Whose servants shall we become today? Or whose attendants?

children.text: yo no 'dya jīvitaṃ dadyād asmin loke sudurlabhaṃ |25|
children.translated_text: Who would give us life today, so hard to obtain in this world? |25|

children.text: aho duḥkhaṃ hi dāridrayam aho 'py akṛtapuṇyatā |
children.translated_text: Alas, how painful is poverty! Alas, the state of not having made merit!

children.text: evaṃ sphīte 'pi nagare nātho nāsti yathāvayor iti |26|
children.translated_text: Even in such a prosperous city, there is no protector for us two! |26|

body.translated_text: 'Having been born in a most distinguished family, overflowing with jewels like the ocean,

body.text: evam anyathā ca sā sārthavāhapatnī kṣudhāparigatahṛdayātmānam anuśocantī tiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: Thus and in other ways, the merchant's wife, her heart overcome by hunger, remained lamenting over herself.

body.text:
Sva Roy 244,3 - 246,4
[91] karṇaś ca sārthavāho mahāsamudrād bhagnayānapātraḥ kathañcit phalakam āsādya dārakasahāyo jalāt sthalam uttīryāyātaḥ | mahatā kṛcchreṇa bhikṣām aṭan bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm āgataḥ | sa tatra bahiḥ kṣetrake rātrim vāsam upagataḥ | tatra cānyatamo bhṛtakapuruṣaḥ kṣetrapālakas tenāsau pratyabhijñātaḥ | tasyaitad abhavad eṣa sārthavāho 'tikṣāmaśarīro vipannasarvasvan draviṇasañcayo dārakasahāyo 'bhyāgataḥ | tat katham asya gṛhapravṛttim ārocayiṣyāmy api tu svayam eva jñāsyatīti viditvā tena tasya hastaprakṣālanodakaṃ datvā māṣapūpavadvayam anupradattaṃ | tataḥ karṇena sārthavāhena ekaṃ māṣapūpakaṃ sthāpitaṃ | mā riktahastako gṛhaṃ pravekṣyāmīti viditvā dārakasya haste sthāpitaṃ | evaṃ tv arddhārddhikaṃ kṛtvānāhāraśarīreṇa tena dārakena sārddhaṃ bhakṣitam | athāparasmin divase karṇaḥ sārthavāhas taṃ māṣapūpakam ādāyātiparamarukṣakṣāmaśarīro 'timalinaikaśāṭakamātrasāro bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīṃ praviśya gṛhaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [91] And the merchant <s>Karṇa</s>, his vessel broken in the great ocean, somehow finding a plank, together with his son, crossed from water to land and arrived. With great difficulty, begging for alms, he came to the capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. There, he took lodging for the night outside in a small field. And there, a certain hired man, a field-guard, recognized him. He thought: 'This merchant has arrived with an extremely emaciated body, all his wealth and store of riches lost, accompanied only by his son. How then shall I inform him of the situation at his home? Rather, he will find out for himself.' Having realized this, he gave him water for washing the hands and offered two bean cakes. Then the merchant <s>Karṇa</s> set aside one bean cake. Thinking 'I shall not enter my house empty-handed,' he placed it in his son's hand. Thus, dividing it in half, with his body unfed, he ate together with his son. Then on the next day, the merchant <s>Karṇa</s>, taking that bean cake, with an extremely rough and emaciated body, clad in nothing but a single extremely dirty garment, entered the capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> and set out for his home.

body.text:
Sva Roy 246,4 - 247,2
[92] virūpo 'pi prabhātakāla eva kṣuttṛṣṇāparikṣāmavadanaḥ kim mayā mandabhāgyenātra tiṣṭhatā jīvatā vā prayojanaṃ | gacchāmy ātmānaṃ praghātayāmīti tām mātaram uvāca | amba gacchāmi paitṛkam udyānam ity uktvā tad udyānaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: [92] <s>Virūpa</s> too, at dawn, with face emaciated from hunger and thirst, [thought]: 'What is the use of my living or staying here, wretched as I am? I shall go and have myself killed.' He said to his mother: 'Mother, I am going to father's garden.' Having said this, he set out for that garden.

body.text:
Sva Roy 247,1 - 251,5
[93] karṇo 'pi sārthavāhaḥ svagṛhasamīpaṅ gato yāvat paśyati cirād dhavastaṃ śāntālayavarṇaṃ mṛttikāpuñjaśeṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ kim idam iti vicintya taṃ khaṇḍāvavarakaṃ pravṛṣṭo yāvat paśyati tāṃ bhāryāṃ tasmin khaṇḍāvavarake dāsyā sārddham avasthitām atikṣāma dīnavadanāṃ malinakhaṇḍacoṭakāvacchāditakaṭipradeśāṃ malapaṭaladagdhāṅgīṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ hā kim idam ity uktvā mūrcchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ śītena vāyunā saṃspṛṣṭaś cirāc ca cetanāṃ labdhvā tatyā bhāryayā sārddhaṃ kim idam ity uccair vikroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | tato bhāryāsakāśād upalabdhavṛttānto dīrgham uṣṇañ cābhiniśvasya kathayati | nūnam mayā dakṣiṇīyakṣetre na kārāḥ kṛtā yena me īdṛśī vipattis | tat kim idānīm ahām adhunā kariṣyāmi kaṃ śaraṇam anuvrajāmi | kasya mukhāvalokako bhaviṣyāmi | ko loke hīnadīnānukampakaḥ | kam āgamyāham idaṃ dāridramahāsamudram uttariṣyāmi kam āgamya vipattipaṅkaṃ prakṣālayiṣyāmi kam āgamyemām anantāṃ śokanadīm uttariṣyāmi | kam āgamyemam dāridraśatru parājeṣye kam āgamyemāṃ sarvaduḥkhamātṛkāṃ dāridralatām utpāṭayiṣyāmi kam āgamyemam dāridravṛkṣam unmūlayiṣyāmi | kam āgamyemam kṣuduḥkhadaṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ hāhākārabhairavamahārāvaṃ dāridramahārākṣasaṃ nirvāsayiṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ dāridramahāmallaṃ parājiṣye | kam āgamyemaṃ kṣuttṛṣṇādipradīptajvālaṃ dāridravarddhanaṃ nirvāpayiṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ viṣadāvaliptadāridramahāhastinaṃ damayiṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ anekaduḥkhaviṣamaviṣasvāsaṃ dāridramahāprannagaṃ nirviṣīṃ kariṣyāmi | kam āgamyāham imaṃ sarvasyāpahāriṇaṃ dāridramahāvīraṃ nivārayiṣyāmi | kam āgamyāham imaṃ sarvaduḥkhaduḥsvabhāvaṃ dāridranigaḍaṃ bhetsyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ dāridracārakam atikramiṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ dāridrakapāṭaṃ pāṭayiṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ dāridrāntakaṃ nirāsīkariṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ viṣādaughaṃ pratariṣyāmi | kam aham āgamyemaṃ dāridramahākāntaraṃ niṣtariṣyāmīty evam anekaprakārakaruṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair vikrośati sma |
body.translated_text: [93] And the merchant <s>Karṇa</s>, having gone near his own house, looked and saw it long-ruined, of the color of a desolate dwelling, with only heaps of earth remaining. And seeing this, thinking 'What is this?', he entered that ruined shelter. As he looked, he saw his wife in that ruined shelter, standing together with the maidservant, with extremely emaciated, pitiful face, her hip-region covered with a dirty, torn piece of cloth, her body scorched by layers of filth. And seeing this, saying 'Alas, what is this!', he fell to the ground in a faint. Touched by a cool breeze, after a long time regaining consciousness, he began to cry out loudly together with his wife: 'What is this?' Then, having learned the circumstances from his wife, drawing a long, hot sigh, he said: 'Surely I did not make offerings in a field worthy of gifts, and therefore such misfortune has befallen me. What then shall I do now? What shall I do? Whom shall I go to for refuge? Whose face shall I look to? Who in the world is compassionate toward the lowly and destitute? Going to whom shall I cross this great ocean of poverty? Going to whom shall I wash away the mud of misfortune? Going to whom shall I cross this endless river of sorrow? Going to whom shall I defeat this enemy of poverty? Going to whom shall I uproot this creeper of poverty, the mother of all suffering? Going to whom shall I cut down this tree of poverty at its root? Going to whom shall I banish this great demon of poverty, with terrible fangs and claws of the suffering of hunger, emitting a frightful great roar of lamentation? Going to whom shall I defeat this great wrestler of poverty? Going to whom shall I extinguish this fire of poverty ablaze with the flames of hunger, thirst, and the like? Going to whom shall I tame this great elephant of poverty smeared with poison? Going to whom shall I render this great serpent of poverty, with its many breaths of the poison of various sufferings, venomless? Going to whom shall I ward off this great hero of poverty who robs everything? Going to whom shall I break these fetters of poverty, whose nature is all suffering and misery? Going to whom shall I escape this prison-keeper of poverty? Going to whom shall I break open this door of poverty? Going to whom shall I destroy this slayer called poverty? Going to whom shall I cross this flood of despair? Going to whom shall I traverse this great wilderness of poverty?' — thus with many kinds of piteous, woeful, drawn-out syllables he cried out.

body.text:
Sva Roy 251,5 - 259,2
[94] atra cāntare nāsti kiñcid buddhānām bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātaṃ | dharmatāṃ khalu buddhānām bhagavatāṃ śaradaruṇakaranikaravisaraparikhacitaparikapilamaṇiguṇataruṇadivasakarasakalāmalakiśalayakalāpakuvalayamarakatendukomalāyudhavimalasaudāminīvalayaghṛtadhārābhiṣekasusamṛddhadhārānalajvālākalāpamaṅgalayūkhakiraṇabahalāmitatimiranikaravijarjarīkṛtajarāmaraṇabhavapañjarāṇām anekakuśalaśatasamādhānabalabhūtakumudaśaṅkhakudāmalatārahāratuṣāramṛṇālāmalakaridaśanasaṃkalitajāmbūnadācavikaṭakoṭakoṭisthitadaśaśatanayanaruciracāpavakrīkṛtavisṛtavimalakarabhāsurānantagaganaikaśatanayanaśaśāṅkadhavalamṛdusnigdhapradakṣiṇavyāmaprabhāmaṇinibiḍabhruvadvayodgīrṇorṇānāṃ virājitaprabuddhanavajalajasadṛśavadanānāṃ | tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ body.translated_text: [94] And in this interval, there is nothing unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, or unrecognized by the blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. For it is the <s>dharmatā</s> (inherent nature) of the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> — whose cages of birth, aging, and death have been shattered by the dense, boundless mass of darkness-destroying abundant rays of auspicious light consisting of streams of consecration-libation flames, and garlands of pure lightning, and gentle weaponry soft as moonlight, and wreaths of <s>Indra</s>-gems and <s>kumuda</s>-flower pearls and conch-shell pearl necklaces and frost and lotus-fiber, pure as ivory tusks, arising from the power of the accumulation of hundreds of wholesome deeds in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); whose faces are like freshly-bloomed lotuses, radiating with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows) emerging from the pair of dense gem-like brows in the halo of gentle, smooth, clockwise-turning radiance, white as the moon in the infinite sky, with innumerable brilliant arm-rays extending, curved like the beautiful bow of the hundred-eyed <s>Indra</s> stationed at millions of tips set with refined gold; who through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have nurtured the provisions of unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) through the relinquishment of hands, feet, eyes, faces, heads, their own flesh, blood, only sons with faces like young lotuses, wives, elephants, horses, chariots, ornaments, garments, food, seats, bedding, gems, gold, silver, all possessions, kingdoms, and the like; who are unattached; who have conquered the power of <s>Māra</s> (the tempter) with their garlands of pure radiance like the orb of the spotless autumn moon; whose forms are enveloped in halos of radiance like clusters of rising moonbeams from the eastern mountain, and rays of the young sun, and streams of lightning from clouds, and strands of tusks of <s>Indra's</s> elephant splitting golden mountains, and agitated milk-oceans of the netherworld, and intertwined corals and emerald crests and serpent-king bellies and lotus petals and moon-discs and peacock-feather tips and <s>makara</s> sea-creature crest-jewels and flawless <s>campaka</s> flower-heaps and excellent <s>vaidūrya</s> stones; who have themselves attained knowledge whose fire has incinerated the thickets of mental dispositions; whose lotus-feet are adorned by the stream of gem-and-gold flower-clusters clinging to the crowns of thousands of prostrating gods; whose feet are copper-colored like the soft reddish surface of a young elephant's palate, like the vermilion of dawn-clouds, like clusters of <s>aśoka</s> flower-buds; whose pure foot-lotuses gleam with the laughter-like radiance of delicate coppery nail-moons; who have uprooted the creepers of craving; who have destroyed the darkness of all delusion; who have become kinsmen of all the world; whose nature is of the highest affection without cause; whose domain is inconceivable knowledge; who have extracted the poison of the great serpent of passion and gathered the accumulation of supreme virtues through hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds; who have uprooted all the roots of the tree of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) through the power of wisdom acquired by the accumulation of merit; whose teachings are praised by the gods <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Śānta</s>; who are greatly compassionate; who are devoted to benefiting the world; who are sole protectors, without a second; who teach non-duality; who abide in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); who are skilled in the three matters of restraint; who have crossed the four floods; whose feet are well-established on the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>); who have long been familiar with the four means of attraction (<s>saṅgrahavastu</s>); who have abandoned the five limbs [of sensual desire]; who have transcended the five destinies; who are endowed with the six limbs; who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); who are adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>); who are guides of the eightfold noble path; who are skilled in the nine successive attainments of meditation; who are mighty with the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>); whose fame fills the ten directions; who are distinguished above a thousand sovereigns — three times at night and three times during the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, they survey the world.

body.text:
Sva Roy 259,2 - 261,3
[95] ko hīyate | ko varddhate | kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ śaṅkaṭaprāptaḥ | kaḥ sambādhaprāptaḥ | kaḥ kṛcchraśaṅkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ | ko 'pāyanimnaḥ | ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ | ko 'pāyaprāptaḥ | ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | ke 'dya mayā saṃsāramahāsamudrād uddharttavyaḥ | ko 'dya mayā kleśamahārakṣasāvalupyamāno mocitavyaḥ | ko 'dya mayā dāridrapannagair upadrūyamāṇaḥ paritrātavyaḥ | ko 'dya mayā dveṣānalasantapyamānamūrtiḥ saddharmavatṣeṇābhiṣiktavyaḥ | ko 'dya mayā mahāmohāndhakārāntarapraviṣṭasantāno timiratarālokam anuttaraṃ samādhivaraśikharam āropayitavyaḥ | kasyādya mayā sarvaduḥkhakṣayakaraṃ sanmārgāṣṭāṅgabhaiṣajyam upadeṣṭavyaṃ | kasyādya mayā dāridrakapāṭapuṭānantapāṭanaṃ vaktavyaṃ | kasyādya mayā jñānatimirāvaṣṭabdhanayanasya jñānāñjanam anupradeyaṃ | ko 'dya mahānigaḍababandhanān mocayitavya ity āha ca ||
body.translated_text: [95] Who is declining? Who is advancing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into difficulty, danger, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is tending toward the lower realms? Who has reached the lower realms? Who is leaning toward the lower realms? Who should I today rescue from the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)? Who, being seized by the great demon of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), should I today liberate? Who, being harassed by the serpents of poverty, should I today save? Whose form, burning in the fire of hatred, should I today anoint with the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s>? Whose lineage, entered into the darkness of great delusion, should I today raise to the supreme peak of noble <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the light beyond darkness? To whom should I today teach the medicine of the noble eightfold path that destroys all suffering? To whom should I today speak of the infinite breaking open of the door of poverty? To whom, whose eyes are gripped by the darkness of ignorance, should I today give the eye-salve of knowledge? Who should today be freed from great shackle-bondage? Thus he spoke. And it is said:

body.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |

body.translated_text: Even the ocean, abode of <s>makaras</s> (sea creatures), may transgress its bounds,

body.text:
Sva Roy 261,3 - 262,5
[96] atha bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalam imaṃ lokam avalokayati sma | adrākṣīd bhagavāṃ karṇaṃ sārthavāham atidaridravyasanapaṅke nimagnam atīvātmānam anuśocantaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar mahākaruṇāsañcodyamānahṛdayaḥ pātracīvaram ādāya bandhumatīyakād dāvān niṣkramaya bandhumatīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyām vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ piṇḍāya praviśantam avalokya rājāmātyaśreṣṭhibrāhmaṇagṛhapatipaurajanapadasārthavāhāḥ | ayaṃ bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ piṇḍāya praviśatīty aham evedaṃ bhagavataḥ pātraṃ pūrayiṣyāmīty anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ gṛhītvāvasthitāni |
body.translated_text: [96] Then the Blessed One, <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, surveyed this entire world. The Blessed One saw the merchant <s>Karṇa</s>, sunk in the mire of the affliction of extreme poverty, exceedingly lamenting over himself. And seeing this, his heart impelled by great compassion, taking his bowl and robes, he departed from the <s>Bandhumatī</s> forest and set out for <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Seeing the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyī</s> entering the capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> for alms, the kings, ministers, merchants, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, city and country people, and caravan leaders [thought]: 'The Blessed One, <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, is entering for alms — it is I who shall fill the Blessed One's bowl!' Many hundreds of thousands of beings stood ready with food and drink.

body.text:
Sva Roy 262,5 - 265,2
[97] atha bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ karṇasya sārthavāhahasyānukampayā vīthīmadhyena praśāntamatir abhinavoditadivasakarādhikatararuciradīptatanuḥ sandhyābhrarekhāvaguṇṭhita iva śakalaśaracandramāḥ kalpadruma iva surapuropavanād amṛtavidrumalatālaṅkṛta iva suvarṇayūpaḥ kāñcanasthālopanihita iva tailapradyotaḥ | samudgatānekavividharatnāṅkurakhacita iva ratnaparvataḥ kanakamalareṇudhūsārita iva rājahaṃsaḥ | airāvata iva mandākinīkama(6)lareṇuvibhūṣitaḥ siṃha iva manaḥśilādhātudigdhaḥ sakalabhuvanalakṣmīpuñja iva dedīpyamānamūrtir iva pādābhyām atiparamasuhṛtarathacaraṇasuruciraracitatalābhyāṃ pratinavavikacakamalasukumārakomalatalābhyāṃ śrīvatsasvastikanandyāvarttavardhamānamīnavibhūṣitatalābhyāṃ taruṇaśaśāṅkabimbatāmrasuparigatārcisuruciranakhābhyāṃ | sunirmalaikaprakāśasuniviṣṭadarśanīyutuṅganakhābhyāṃ nakhatilakapaṅktikhacittāpratimasujātadīrghavṛttāyatāṃ gulibhyāṃ mṛdusukumāratūlasaṃsparśapārṣṇibhyāṃ śriyā dedīpyamāno gaganatala iva bhāskaraḥ sakalam idaṃ digmaṇḍalam avabhāsayan karṇasya sārthavāhasya taṃ khaṇḍāvavarakam anuprāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: [97] Then the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, out of compassion for the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, with a tranquil mind, his body more resplendent and brilliant than the newly risen sun, proceeded through the middle of the street—like the full autumn moon veiled by streaks of twilight clouds; like a wish-fulfilling tree from the garden of the city of the gods; like a golden sacrificial post adorned with immortal coral creepers; like a lamp placed upon a golden plate; like a jeweled mountain studded with sprouts of many varied gems; like a royal swan dusted with the golden pollen of lotuses; like <s>Airāvata</s> adorned with the pollen of lotuses from the <s>Mandākinī</s> river; like a lion smeared with the mineral <s>manaḥśilā</s>; his form blazing like a mass of the splendor of all the worlds—with feet whose soles were fashioned with the most supremely beautiful, agreeable, chariot-wheel marks, whose soles were as tender and soft as a freshly blooming lotus, whose soles were adorned with the auspicious marks of <s>śrīvatsa</s>, <s>svastika</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, <s>vardhamāna</s>, and fish, with nails that were copper-red and beautifully radiant like the orb of the young moon, with nails that were supremely clear, luminous, firmly set, beautiful, and prominent, with toes that were incomparably well-formed, long, round, extended, and studded with rows of nail-marks, with heels of soft, delicate, cotton-like touch—blazing with splendor, illuminating the entire circle of the directions like the sun in the sky, he arrived at the hovel of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 265,2 - 268,2
[98] tato vipaśyinā samyaksambuddhena prataptatarakanakarasarāgapracurā | ghṛtāhutivarṣāsekādīpitānanapraphullakiṃśuk_aāśokaraktotpalakuraṇṭakaravīrasandhyābhracampakakusumbhamaṇḍagajatālupadmarāgāruṇataḍitsahasrātirekā prabhā samutsṛṣṭā | yayā sahasaiva khaṇḍāvavarakaṃ sāntarba hir vilīnakanakāvabhāsaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ | tad ālocya karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kim idam iti samutthitaḥ | paśyati bhagavantaṃ vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ dvātriṅśammahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtamūrtiṃ mūrtimantam iva dharmaṃ havyāvasiktam iva hutavahaṃ | taptakanakarasarāgakarṇikārakuṅkumakusumbhaharitālamanaḥśilāraktotpalaśaratsandhyānurañjitajaladaśikhivalāhamecakakāñcanarājapaṭṭhiṅgulakātimuktakuraṇṭakaprabhāmaṇḍalāvaguṇṭhitavigrahaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ karṇasya sārthavāhasyātimahāprasādo jātaḥ || kim aham bhagavate 'nupradāsyāmīty evam ātmāno vibhavam avalokayan paśyati māṣapūpakam ekaṃ sa taṃ gṛhītvā patnyāḥ kathayati bhadre mayā māṣapūpako 'yaṃ mā khalv ahaṃ riktahasto gṛhaṃ pravekṣyāmīty ānītaḥ | ayañ ca bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ paramadakṣiṇīyo hīnadīnānukampako 'tra ca svalpam api dānabījam uptaṃ dāridravyasanonmūlakaṃ bhavati | tad aham imaṃ māṣapūpakaṃ bhagavate 'nuprayacchāmīti | sā kathayaty āryaputra śobhanam evaṃ kriyatāṃ | etad api tāvat kuśalamūlaṃ saṃsārasukhahetubhūtaṃ bhavatīty
body.translated_text: [98] Then from the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, a radiance was emitted—more intense than the redness of liquid refined gold, exceeding the brilliance of a thousand lightning bolts; like a fully blooming <s>Kiṃśuka</s> tree kindled by the sprinkling of offerings of ghee; colored like <s>Aśoka</s>, red lotus, <s>Kurantaka</s>, <s>Karavīra</s>, twilight clouds, <s>Campaka</s>, safflower, <s>Maṇḍa</s>, <s>Gajatāla</s>, ruby, and crimson lightning. By that radiance, instantly the hovel, both inside and out, became as if permeated with the glow of molten gold. Noticing this, the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> arose, wondering 'What is this?' He saw the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, his form adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, like <s>Dharma</s> embodied, like a sacrificial fire fed with oblations, his body enveloped in a halo of radiance colored like liquid refined gold, <s>Karṇikāra</s>, saffron, safflower, orpiment, <s>manaḥśilā</s>, red lotus, autumn twilight-tinged clouds, peacock-tail, gold, royal silk cloth, <s>Hiṅgulaka</s>, <s>Atimuktaka</s>, and <s>Kurantaka</s>. And upon seeing him, supreme devotion arose in the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>. 'What shall I offer to the Blessed One?' Looking at his own possessions, he saw a single <s>māṣa</s>-cake (a cake made of black gram). He took it and said to his wife: 'My dear, I brought this <s>māṣa</s>-cake so that I would not enter the house empty-handed. But this Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, is a supreme field of merit, who has compassion for the lowly and wretched. Even a small seed of giving sown here uproots poverty. Therefore, I shall offer this <s>māṣa</s>-cake to the Blessed One.' She said: 'Noble husband, excellent! Let it be done so. Even this much serves as a root of merit, becoming the cause of happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 268,2 - 270,5
[99] evam ukte karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati | parīttam imaṃ māṣapūpakaṃ katham ahaṃ tādṛśo 'sminn eva pure bhūtvā adhunā īdṛśaṃ yadi parīttaṃ paśyātām eva rājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatipaurajanapadasārthavāhānāṃ bhagavate 'nupradāsyāmy api tu patre badhvā dāsyām evam anabhilakṣyo bhaviṣyāmīti viditvā taṃ khaṇḍāvavarakaṃ praviśya pattraṃ gaveṣṭum ārabdho na kiñcit pattram ārāgitavān | atha saḥ sārthavāhaḥ sutarāṃ samvignamānasaḥ hā kaṣṭam īdṛśo 'ham mandabhāgya iti dīrghamuṣṇañ cābhiniśvasya sahasaiva tasmāt khaṇḍāvavarakān niṣkramya mahatā pramādavegena taṃ māṣapūpakaṃ vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pātre pratipāditavān | pratipādya ca pādayoḥ praṇipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdho 'nena ahaṃ bhagavan kuśalamūlena deyadharmaparityāgena ita eva janma prabhṛti mā kadācid ekadivasam api daridraḥ syāṃ | āḍhyataraḥ syāṃ | paripūrṇajīvitopakaraṇaḥ | samanantaram eva karṇasya sārthavāhasya sahasaiva vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādayo nipatata mātrasyaiva yā 'tiparamavirūpā kṣāmatā sāntarhitā saiva pūrvakā varṇanibhābhinivṛttā |
body.translated_text: [99] Thus addressed, the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> reflected: 'This <s>māṣa</s>-cake is meager. How can I—once such a prominent person in this very city—now offer something so meager to the Blessed One in the full sight of the kings, ministers, brahmins, householders, citizens, and caravan leaders? Rather, I shall wrap it in a leaf and give it—thus I shall be inconspicuous.' Knowing this, he entered the hovel and began to search for a leaf, but he could not find any leaf at all. Then that caravan leader, his mind all the more agitated, sighing a long, hot sigh—'Alas, how wretched and unfortunate I am!'—suddenly rushed out of that hovel and, with a great surge of earnestness, placed that <s>māṣa</s>-cake into the bowl of the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>. Having placed it and prostrated at his feet, he began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, by this relinquishment of a gift, O Blessed One, from this very birth onward may I never be poor, not even for a single day! May I be supremely wealthy, with complete provisions for livelihood!' Immediately upon the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> falling at the feet of the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, that supremely ugly and emaciated appearance of his disappeared, and his former excellent complexion was restored.

body.text:
Sva Roy 270,5 - 272,273
[100] atha karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ prāṇidhānaṃ kṛtvotthito vipaśyī samyaksambuddhas tata eva pratinivṛtya bandhumatīyaṃ dāvaṃ gato 'tha karṇaḥ sārthavāhas tair bandhumatīyakaiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhaiś ca pratyabhijñātas tatraikaḥ sārthavāhas tān paurikān idam avocat | na vayaṃ bhavantaḥ karṇaṃ sārthavāham avasīdantam apy upekṣāmahe paṭañ ca prasāryāha || bhavantaḥ śakyaṃ bahubhir ekaḥ samuddhatuṃ na tv ekena bahavas tad yena vātra yat parityaktavyaṃ tad asmin paṭe 'nupradīyatām ity ukte harṣakaṭakakeyūrāṅgadakuṇḍalahārārddhahārāṅgulīyakāny anekālaṅkāraśatasahasrāṇy anupradattāni | anekāni ca kāśidukūlakoṭāmbakauśeyāparāntakaśūkṣmātimahārhavicitravastrayugalaśatāny anekāni tasya tasminn eva kṣaṇe vastrāṇām alaṅkārāṇāñ cātimahān rāśiḥ samvṛttaḥ | tataḥ karṇaḥ sārthavāhas tāṃ vibhūtim avalokya patnyāḥ kathayati | bhadre paśya sukṣetredānavījasyāṅkuraḥ prādurbhūta iti | sāpi prītiprāmodyajātā vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ namasyantī tāni vastrāṇi alaṅkārāṇi cāvavarakaṃ praveśayitum ārabdhā |
body.translated_text: [100] Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, having made his aspiration, rose up. The perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, turning back from there, went to the <s>Bandhumatī</s> grove. The caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> was then recognized by the merchants and caravan leaders of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. One caravan leader among them said to the citizens: 'Sirs, we shall not stand by and let the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> remain in distress.' And, spreading out a cloth, he said: 'Sirs, it is possible for many to lift up one person, but not for one to lift up many. Therefore, let each person give whatever they can spare upon this cloth.' When this was said, bracelets, armlets, arm-rings, earrings, necklaces, half-necklaces, finger-rings, and many hundreds of thousands of ornaments were given. And many hundreds of pairs of garments of <s>Kāśi</s> cloth, fine linen, cotton, silk, and <s>Aparāntaka</s> cloth—supremely valuable and variegated—at that very moment, a supremely great heap of garments and ornaments had accumulated for him. Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, looking at that wealth, said to his wife: 'My dear, see—the sprout of the seed of giving sown in a good field has appeared!' She too, filled with joy and delight, paying homage to the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, began to bring those garments and ornaments into the hovel.

body.text:
Sva Roy 273,1 - 274,2
[101] virūpo 'pi dārakas tat paitṛkam udyānaṃ praviśya kṣusdduḥkhopataptamānasas tām ātmīyāṃ paramavirūpatām eva punaḥ punaḥ saṃśocayan saṃlakṣayati | kim mayā pāpakarmakāriṇā paramaduḥkhabhāginā 'tivirūpeṇādhanyadarśanena jīvitā prayojanaṃ sarvathā praghātayāmy ātmānam ity udvignamanaḥ sahasaiva pāṭalāvṛkṣasyāgraśākhām āruḍho vṛkṣaśākhā ca bhagnā sahasaiva sārddhaṃ vṛkṣaśākhayā patito vedanārttaś cāvatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: [101] Meanwhile, the deformed boy (<s>Virūpa</s>) had entered his father's garden. With his mind tormented by the suffering of hunger, lamenting again and again his own supreme deformity, he thought: 'What use is life for me, a doer of evil deeds, of supreme misfortune, exceedingly ugly, of wretched appearance? By all means I shall kill myself!' With an agitated mind, he suddenly climbed to the top branch of a <s>Pāṭalā</s> tree. But the branch broke, and he suddenly fell along with the branch. Stricken with pain, he lay there.

body.text:
Sva Roy 274,2 - 278,3
[102] atra cāntare nāsti kiñcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam | aviditam avajñātam adrākṣīd vipaśyī samyaksambuddho divyena buddhacakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntā mānuṣyakena virūpadārakaṃ tathā duḥkhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar mahākaranīyo sañcodyamāno ṛddhayā tat sthānaṃ gatvā svaśarīraprabhām utsṛṣṭavān | kalpaśatasambhṛtāś ca bhagavato maitryāṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ || yaiḥ spṛṣṭamātrasyaiva virūpasya yā śarīre duḥkhavedanā sā prativigatā tac ca kṣuttṛṣaduḥkhaṃ pratiprasrabdhaṃ | sahasaivotthitaḥ paśyati vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasradurlabhadarśanam uttaptam dvātriṅśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇadyotitavigrahaṃ saha darśanāc cāsya bhagavato vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasyopari prasādo jātaḥ | tena ca haridrāraktakaṃ hastamātraṃ vastrakhaṇḍaṃ prāvṛtam āsīt tena tatprasādāviṣṭena śarīrād avatārya mahatā prasādavegena sahasaiva vipaśyinaḥ śāstur upari nikṣiptam ekañ ca karṇikārakusuman tac ca bhagavatā vipaśyinā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena tathādhiṣṭhitaṃ yathā tad vastrakhaṇḍakaṃ tathāgatasya kāyapramāṇikaṃ bhūtvā kāyaṃ praticchāditavān | karṇikārakusumañ copaviśakaṭacakramātraṃ bhūtvā cchattravad avasthitaṃ | tac ca dṛṣṭvā virūpasya dārakasyātimahān prasādo jātaḥ | sa mahatā praśādavegena vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādayor nipatya mahatā svareṇa praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [102] Now, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unperceived, or unrecognized by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. The perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, with his divine <s>Buddha</s>-eye, pure and surpassing that of humans, saw the deformed boy in such distress. Impelled by great compassion, he went to that place by supernatural power and emitted the radiance of his own body. And the rays of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) accumulated over a hundred <s>kalpas</s> were emitted by the Blessed One. The moment the deformed <s>Virūpa</s> was touched by them, the painful sensation in his body ceased, and the suffering of hunger and thirst subsided. He immediately rose up and saw the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, whose sight was more difficult to obtain than in hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, his form blazing with the thirty-two marks of a great being. And upon seeing the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, devotion arose in him. He had been wearing a small piece of cloth, the size of a hand, dyed with turmeric. Filled with devotion, he removed it from his body and, with a great surge of faith, suddenly cast it upon the Teacher <s>Vipaśyin</s>. And also one <s>Karṇikāra</s> flower. That was so blessed by the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, that the piece of cloth, becoming the size of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, covered his body. And the <s>Karṇikāra</s> flower, becoming the size of a cart-wheel, stood above like a parasol. Seeing this, supreme devotion arose in the deformed boy. With a great surge of faith, he prostrated at the feet of the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s> and began to make an aspiration in a loud voice:

body.text: anena dvipadāṃ śreṣṭha dāneneha virūpatāṃ |

children.translated_text: From this day forward, and may I obtain a beautiful form! [1]
May I be called <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> (Golden-colored), wrapped in golden-hued garments,

children.text: candanotpalagandhaś ca kāyād vaktrāc ca me bhavet |2|
children.translated_text: And may the fragrance of sandalwood and lotus emanate from my body and face! [2]
May I be like one of golden complexion, captivating all the world,
Free from all diseases, master of all the sciences! [3]
Endowed with all kinds of speech, free from all calamities,
Supreme among all, all-seeing, adorned with all excellences! [4]
May I become a perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, with all aims accomplished, tender toward beings,
Endowed with all stainless virtues, glorious, possessing all resources, and happy!' [5]

body.translated_text: 'By this gift, O best of bipeds, may I abandon my deformity

body.text:
Sva Roy 278,3 - 280,2
[103] athaitat prāṇidhānakaraṇasamakālam eva virūpasya dārakasya sahasaiva sā virūpatāntarhitā surūpaḥ samvṛtto darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ suvarṇavarṇagātracchaviḥ sahasaiva cāsyākasmād ā kāśād āgatya suvarṇavarṇair vastraiḥ śarīrām ācchāditaṃ | mahārhaiś cāṅgadakuṇḍalādibhir alaṅkāraviśeṣair | devatābhiś ca karṇikārotpalacampakapadmakumudamāndārakādikam mahat kusumavarṣaṃ pātitaṃ | divyañ candanāgurukuṅkumatamālapatracūrṇavarṣaṃ pramuktam evañ codghuṣṭam aho tathāgatāvaropitasya dānabījasy_iṣṭho viśiṣṭhaś cāṅkuraḥ samutpanna iti | tena ca divyena puṣpacūrṇavarṣeṇa sarvan tad udyānaṃ jānumātreṇaughenāvasthitam atha bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhas tasmād udyānān niṣkramya bandhumatīyakaṃ dāvaṅ gataḥ |
body.translated_text: [103] At the very moment of making that aspiration, the deformity of the boy <s>Virūpa</s> suddenly disappeared. He became beautiful, handsome, charming, with a bodily complexion of golden hue. And suddenly, from the sky, without any apparent cause, golden-colored garments came and covered his body, along with special ornaments such as bracelets, earrings, and the like. And the gods rained down a great shower of flowers—<s>Karṇikāra</s>, lotus, <s>Campaka</s>, water lily, white water lily, <s>Māndāra</s>, and others. A divine rain of sandalwood, aloe, saffron, and <s>Tamālapatra</s> powder was released. And a cry was raised: 'Oh, the sprout of the seed of giving sown by the <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen—desired and distinguished!' By that divine rain of flowers and powder, the entire garden was filled waist-deep. Then the Blessed <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, departed from that garden and went to the <s>Bandhumatī</s> grove.

body.text:
Sva Roy 280,2 - 283,2
[104] karṇo 'pi sārthavāho bhāryām uvāca | bhadre so 'smākaṃ putraḥ kva gato yam āgamyāsmākam īdṛśī vipattir abhūd iti | sā kathayaty udyānaṃ gacchāmīti tena samākhyātaṃ | tad gaccha śīghraṃ mā sa tatrodvignamanā ātmānaṃ praghātayiṣyatīti | karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati | kin nāmāsāv asmākaṃ putraḥ kīdṛśo veti | sā kathayaty āryaputra paramavirūpadarśano virūpākhyaś ceti || tataḥ sārthavāhas tvaritagatipracāratayā tad udyānaṃ gataḥ paśyati ca virūpakumāraṃ suvarṇavarṇakāyam atimahārhasūkṣmasuvarṇapītavastrācchāditaśarīraṃ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitam atimanoharaṃ darśanadevakumāram iva paramayāśriyā dedīpyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punar aho dhanyaḥ saḥ puruṣo yasyāyaṃ putraḥ ity evam uktvā taṃ kumāram uvāca || dāraka kasya tvaṃ putra iti | sa kathayati karṇo nāma sārthavāhastasyāhaṃ putra iti | karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati | viheṭhito 'ham anena kumāreeti vicintya samabhivṛddhakutūhalo 'nimiṣam abhivīkṣyamāṇaḥ punas taṃ kumāram uvāca | bhoḥ kumāraḥ satyaṃ kathaya kasya tvaṃ putra iti virūpaḥ kathayati kim atra vicāryate | satyam evāhaṃ karṇasya sārthavāhasya putra iti | sa kathayaty aho 'ham anena kumāreṇa suviḍambitaḥ kṛta iti | matvā kathayati | kumāra śrutam mayātivirūpa sa iti tvaṃ cābhirūpaḥ | tata kenopāyenābhirūpatā tavābhinivṛtteti ||
body.translated_text: [104] The caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> also said to his wife: 'My dear, where has our son gone? Because of him, such misfortune has befallen us.' She said: 'He said he was going to the garden.' He said: 'Then go quickly, lest he, with an agitated mind, kill himself there!' The caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> asked: 'What is the name and appearance of our son?' She said: 'Noble husband, he is of extremely ugly appearance and is named <s>Virūpa</s> (Deformed).' Then the caravan leader, moving swiftly, went to that garden. He saw the prince <s>Virūpa</s> with a body of golden complexion, his form clothed in supremely valuable, fine, golden-yellow garments, adorned with all ornaments, exceedingly captivating, blazing with supreme splendor like a divine prince. Seeing him, he said: 'Oh, how fortunate is the man whose son this is!' And he addressed that prince: 'Boy, whose son are you?' He replied: 'My father is a caravan leader named <s>Karṇa</s>.' The caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> thought: 'I am being deceived by this boy!' Reflecting thus, with growing curiosity, gazing without blinking, he asked the prince again: 'Young man, tell the truth—whose son are you?' <s>Virūpa</s> replied: 'Why do you question this? Truly, I am the son of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>.' He said: 'Oh, I have been thoroughly tricked by this boy!' Thinking so, he said: 'Prince, I have heard that he is extremely ugly—but you are handsome. So by what means has this beauty come about for you?'

body.text:
Sva Roy 283,2 - 287,3
[105] virūpaḥ kumāraḥ prītivikasitākṣo mahatā svareṇovāca |
body.translated_text: [105] The prince <s>Virūpa</s>, with eyes blooming with joy, said in a loud voice:

body.text: adya dāridraduḥkhāgniparitāpitacetasā |

children.text: vṛkṣaśākhām āruhya mayā hy ātmā nipātitaḥ |1|
children.translated_text: Having climbed a tree-branch, I threw myself down. [1]
Having fallen, afflicted with broken limbs, I became unconscious;
Motionless and breathless, I lay for just a moment. [2]

children.text: tato vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ satvānāṃ hy anukampakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the perfectly enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the compassionate one toward beings,
out of compassion for me, O protector, came to this garden. |3|
Bearing the thirty-two marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), with a complexion like refined gold,
filling the ten directions with radiance like molten gold. |4|

children.text: prabhayā tasya gātram me spṛṣṭamātraṃ suśītayā |
children.translated_text: The moment his supremely cool radiance touched my body,
all of this was refreshed by an incomparable stream of ambrosia. |5|
My suffering of hunger, thirst, and affliction, entirely inauspicious,

children.text: tatkṣaṇaṃ praśamaṃ yātaṃ cetanāñ cāptavān ahaṃ |6|
children.translated_text: at that instant subsided, and I regained consciousness. |6|

children.text: kim etad iti sotsāham utthito 'haṃ munin tadā |
children.translated_text: 'What is this?' With enthusiasm I then rose, and the <s>Muni</s>—
I beheld [him], exceedingly beautiful, the abode of the world's fortune. |7|

children.text: dṛṣṭvā draṣṭavyaratnam me tan nāthaṃ parayā śriyā
children.translated_text: Having seen that jewel worthy of beholding, that protector, shining with supreme glory,

children.text: vidyotantaṃ diśaḥ kṛtsnāḥ prasādo hy abhavat pūrā |8|
children.translated_text: illuminating all the directions—faith indeed arose in me completely. |8|
Then, with a joyful heart, a small piece of cloth,
dyed with turmeric, I cast toward him with supreme delight. |9|

children.text: karṇikārasya me puṣpam kaṃ tasyaiva sadyateḥ |
children.translated_text: A <s>karṇikāra</s> flower of mine, [thrown] toward him with devotion—

children.text: kṣiptaṃ tac copari muneḥ chattravat samavasthitaṃ |10|
children.translated_text: that, cast upward above the <s>Muni</s>, remained hovering like a parasol. |10|
Then too, with a joyful heart, bowing at his feet,
I, in whom faith had arisen, made this aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): |11|
'By this gift, O Protector, may I this very day cast off my ugliness

children.text: parityajya surūpaś ca bhaveyaṃ hi bhavārṇave |12|
children.translated_text: and become handsome in the ocean of existence! |12|
May I be draped in golden-yellow garments of golden hue,

children.text: candanotpalagandhaś ca kāyād vaktrāc ca me bhavet |13|
children.translated_text: and may the fragrance of sandalwood and lotus emanate from my body and mouth!' |13|

children.text: ity etat praṇidhānañ ca mayā kṛtam idañ ca me |
children.translated_text: This aspiration I made, and this
form and complexion of such a kind, delightful, have manifested in me. |14|

children.text: mahārhāṇi ca vastrāṇi pītāny atimṛdūni ca |
children.translated_text: And garments of great value, yellow and exceedingly soft,
suddenly appeared upon my body at that very instant. |15|
The gods released from the firmament this rain of flowers,
and powders of sandalwood, <s>aguru</s> (aloeswood), <s>tamāla</s>, <s>tagara</s>, and the like. |16|

children.text: hāhākāro mahāṃś caiva dundhubhiś ca manoharaḥ |
children.translated_text: A great cry of wonder arose, and a captivating kettledrum [sounded];

children.text: namas te bhagavan buddha iti ghoṣa udīritaḥ |17|
children.translated_text: 'Homage to you, Blessed <s>Buddha</s>!'—such an exclamation was uttered. |17|

children.text: etat kṛtvādya kuśalaṃ mamedaṃ rūpam īdṛśaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having performed this virtuous deed, this form of mine,
pleasant, with a complexion resembling gold, has manifested. |18|
Thus.

body.translated_text: 'Today, with a mind tormented by the fire of poverty and suffering,

body.text:
Sva Roy 287,3 - 288,3
[106] athaitad upaśrutya karṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ sahasaiva sahasraiḥ prasādakaṇṭakitasarvaromakūpaḥ kṛtāñjalir vipaśyinaṃ tathāgataṃ muhur muhur namasyamānaḥ paramaprītisaumanasya jātaḥ surūpaṃ putram animiṣam abhivīkṣya prāha | putra āgaccha gacchāva ity atha surūpaḥ kumāraḥ pitāyaṃ mamety utpannabahumānaḥ pituḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā svāgataṃ tātety uktvā pitrā sārddhaṃ gantuṃ saṃprasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, hearing this, the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, instantly, with all the pores of his body bristling with faith, with joined palms, bowing again and again to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, filled with supreme joy and gladness, gazing at his handsome son without blinking, said: 'Son, come, let us go.' Then the prince <s>Surūpa</s>, recognizing 'this is my father,' arose with great respect, paid homage at his father's feet, said 'Welcome, father,' and set out to go with his father.

body.text:
Sva Roy 288,3 - 290,291
[107] śakrasya devānām indrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate | tasyaitad abhavat ayaṃ karṇaḥ sārthavāho bhagavati buddhe kṛtādhikāraḥ tan nāyam arhati tṛṇāgāre vastum iti viditvā viśvakarmāṇaṃ devaputram āmantrayate | gaccha viśvakarman karṇasya sārthavāhasya catūratnamayañ caturdvāram ardhāṣṭamatalakaṃ gṛham abhinirmimīṣveti | tato viśvakarmaṇā śakrasya devendrasya pratiśrutya tatkṣaṇād eva bandhumatīrājadhānīm āgatya catūratnamayeṣṭakastambhasañcitam uttuṅgarucirāṭṭālakaṃ gavākṣaniryūhakapotamālāsuvinyastāṅgāphalakanāgadantakam atyuccārddhāṣṭamatalakam atiramaṇīyatoraṇopaśobhitadvāraṃ śarajaladharābhrakūṭahimanikararāśiśikaramṛṇālāvadātocchritacchatradhvajapatākam āmuktapaṭudāmakalāpaṃ sakalapuravaropaśobhāniketabhūtam atirucirakanakamayābhinavaviniḥsṛtatāmracūtapallavopaśobhitamukham aṣṭāṅgaśītalāmbuparipūrṇakumbhopaśobhitadvāram aparimitarajatavaidūryasphaṭikamusāragalvendranīlamahānīlādiratnaparipūrṇānekanidhisahasrāpūryamāṇaṃ śeṣānardhadravyopakaraṇaparipūrṇaṃ gṛhavaram abhinirmitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The knowledge and vision of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, extends below [to the human realm]. This thought arose in him: 'This caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> has performed a meritorious deed toward the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore he does not deserve to dwell in a grass hut.' Knowing this, he summoned the divine prince <s>Viśvakarman</s>: 'Go, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, and magically create for the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> a house made of four kinds of jewels, with four doors, and seven and a half stories.' Then <s>Viśvakarman</s>, having assented to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, at that very instant came to the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s> and magically created a supreme mansion: built of bricks and pillars of four kinds of jewels, with lofty and beautiful watchtowers, with well-arranged lattice windows, projecting balconies, pigeon-galleries, boards, panels, and elephant-tooth brackets, exceedingly tall with seven and a half stories, adorned with exceedingly beautiful arched gateways, with parasols, banners, and flags raised aloft—white as autumn clouds, mountain peaks of mist, heaps of snow, sprays of water, and lotus stalks—hung with festoons of sharp-pointed garlands, serving as the abode of the splendor and beauty of the entire city, its entrance adorned with freshly sprouted copper-colored mango leaves made of exceedingly beautiful gold, its doors beautified with pitchers filled with cool water of the eight qualities, filled with innumerable thousands of treasuries brimming with unlimited silver, <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), crystal, <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), sapphire, great sapphire, and other jewels, and the rest filled with various goods, equipment, and supplies.

body.text:
Sva Roy 291,1 - 298,2
[108] atha karṇaḥ sārthavāho gṛham āgato bhāryayā cāsya hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditayā sauvarṇena bhṛṅgāreṇārgham anupradattaṃ | uktaś cāryaputra tvatpuṇyānubhāvād īdṛśaḥ kenāpi bhavanavaram abhinirmitam ity atha karṇaḥ sārthavāhas taṃ bhavanavaram abhivīkṣya paramaprītisaumanasya jātaḥ sutarāṃ buddhe bhagavati utpannaprasādopajanitaromāñcaḥ śirasi kṛtakarapuṭāñjalir namas tasmai bhagavate tathāgatāyārhate samyaksambuddhāyācintyācintāmaṇaye 'nuttarāya puṇyakṣetrāyety uktvā praharṣapūrṇavadanakamalaḥ prāha ||
body.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> arrived home. His wife, overjoyed, delighted, and elated, offered him water of welcome (<s>argha</s>) from a golden pitcher. She said: 'Noble lord, by the power of your merit, this supreme mansion has been created by someone.' Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, gazing upon that supreme mansion, was filled with supreme joy and gladness. With faith in the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> intensified, the hairs of his body standing on end, with palms joined above his head, he said: 'Homage to that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, the inconceivable wish-fulfilling jewel, the unsurpassed field of merit!' And with a face like a lotus full of joy, he spoke:

body.text: aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitaṃ |

children.translated_text: where the seed sown by me bears fruit this very day! |1|

children.text: kva tat parīttaṃ dānaṃ me sarvasaṃskāvavarjitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Where is that meager gift of mine, devoid of all ceremonial preparation?

children.text: kva cedaṃ ramyam uttuṅgaṃ hemaratnamayaṃ gṛhaṃ |2|
children.translated_text: And where is this lovely, lofty house made of gold and jewels? |2|

children.text: kva tat kuḍyāvaśeṣan me gṛhaṃ śokavivardhanaṃ |
children.translated_text: Where is that house of mine, nothing left but walls, that increased my grief?
And where is this [mansion], white as the moon freed from clouds? |3|
Where is that house with windows [made of] holes by mice and insects?

body.translated_text: 'Oh, what a field made of virtues, free from all faults,

Sva Roy 298,2 - 299
[109] atha karṇaḥ sārthavāhas tīvraprasādavegāvarjitacittasantatiḥ saṃlakṣayati | bhagavantam āgamya mayaivaṃ vibhūtir āsāditā yan nv ahaṃ prathamato bhagavantaṃ vipaśyinaṃ tathāgatam asmin gṛhe praveśya saśrāvakagaṇaṃ bhojayeyam iti viditvā mahatā satkāreṇa vipaśyinaṃ tathāgataṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham antargṛhe upanimantrya śatarasenāhāreṇa saptāhaṃ bhojayitvā pādayoḥ praṇipatya yāvajjīvaṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritavān |
body.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, his mental continuum captivated by an intense surge of faith, reflected: 'By resorting to the Blessed One, I have attained such prosperity. What if I were first to invite the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s> into this house and feed him together with his assembly of disciples?' Knowing this, with great reverence, he invited the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s> together with his monastic community into the inner house, fed them with a meal of a hundred flavors for seven days, bowed at his feet, and for as long as he lived, offered all provisions.

body.text:
Sva Roy 299,2 - 307,4
[110] athāparasmin divase sa kṣetrapālako bhṛtakapuruṣaḥ pratyuṣasi svāminānurūpadattāṃ bhaktapuṭikām ādaya kṣetraṃ saṃprasthito 'śrauṣīd antarmārge sa bhṛtakapuruṣo 'nyatarasyopāsakasyāntikād yathā karṇena sārthavāhena māṣapūpakam ekaṃ buddhe bhagavaty anupradāyaivamvidhā śrī prāpteti śrutvā ca punaḥ sa puruṣas tam upāsakam uvāca | bhoḥ sādho ke tasya bhagavato guṇā iti | sa upāsakaḥ kathayati | bhadramukha kā me śaktis tasya bhagavato viśeṣavihitān guṇān vaktuṃ | eka hī saṃkṣepataḥ śrūyatāṃ | sa hi bhagavān samyaksambuddha pravarapuruṣalakṣaṇālaṅkṛtaḥ kāñcanādriprakāśaḥ śaśāṅkārkatulyātirekaprabhaḥ sūrataḥ suvrataḥ śāntacittaḥ suvākyaḥ suveṣṭaḥ sugātraḥ suvaktraḥ sunetraḥ sukarmā sudharmā kṣamāvān pratibhāvān | vinetā sunetā nayajño damajñaḥ kṛtajñaḥ sucakṣaḥ praśāntendriyaḥ suinītendriyāśvo mahādharmarājo mahāsattvasāro mahālokanātho mahājñānaketus mahāvādiśūro mahāpuṇyakośo mahādharmahetus mahāsārthavāho dharmadātā mahākarṇadhāro mahādakṣiṇīyaḥ tṛṣācchedako mahāmohavināsakaḥ krodhanirvāpako mokṣasaṃsthāpakaḥ kāpathāc cyāvakaḥ satpathoddeśakaḥ śaṃsayacchedakaḥ satyasaṃdarśakaḥ kleśanirvāpako māravidhvaṃsako lokanistārako brahmaṇābhyarccitaḥ śakrasaṃpūjitaḥ sarvalokādhikaḥ sarvalokārthakṛt sattvottamaḥ sarvaduḥkhāntakṛta sarvavit | anayavinayaviśārado 'tītasarvāsravo vādimukhyair nādhiṣṭhitaḥ sarvadoṣair asaṃbhrāmitaḥ sarvārtham abhyudyataḥ rūpavān śīlavān dhyāyavān vīryavān jñānayuktas tathā niḥspṛho nirjvaro niṣprapañco nirāyāsavṛttiḥ pravṛttikṣayopāyasaṃdarśakaḥ sarvasatveṣu maitrāsayo pāpamukto 'dhimokṣānvito 'nuttaro nāyako daiśikaḥ kleśarogārditānāṃ mahāvaidyabhūtaḥ svayambhūḥ vibhuḥ saṃyatātmāprameyaprabhāvo 'lpakṛtaḥ susantoṣavān kālavān arthavān jñānavān nirjitakleśaśatruḥ praśāntāgnir akṣobhyadharmo mahādakṣiṇīyaḥ paraṃ duḥkhitaṃ lokam ajñānapaṅke nimagnaṃ samavalokya tasmāt svayañ cāpi śaktaḥ samuddhartum ātmāprabhāvānurūpātmanaḥ sarvasattvānukampārtham evaṃ prakārottamā buddhi tasmāc caivam uttāreyaṃ jagad duḥkhitaṃ mocayeyaṃ kathaṃ bhītānām āśvāsayeyaṃ kathaṃ saṃsāramagnam abhyuddhareyaṃ kathaṃ dahyamānam āhlādayeyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ cittam evaṃ samutpādya vīryañ ca kṛtvā paraṃ janmakoṭīsahasreṣu pūrvavac cānnapānāśrayopānahobhojanachatrayānāsanādīn ramyāṇi hastyaśvadārātmajān dāsadāsī śirolocanāny ātmamāṃsāni cotkṛtya seṣmāṇisadvajreṇe syenarūpāya vuddhātmanā sarvasatveṣu sarvair upāyair hitaṃ cintayan sarvakālañ ca jīrṇāturasannasaṃūḍhasaṃbhrāntasaṃkṣubhyamānān avasthitān avekṣya sarvātmān āśvāsya santo 'py asanto yathācārya saṃśevinā dānaśīlakṣamāsattvasaprajñādhyānādyair guṇair janmakoṭīsahasrair anekair śivāṃ bodhim agryām anuprāptavān api ca | kas tasya sarvāgrasattvasya samyaksambuddhasya vikhyātakīrteḥ kṛpākhyātaviśvāsadharmasya vijñānapūrṇasya vistīrṇavīryasya nistīrṇasarvapratijñasya nirmuktadoṣasya nirvāntamohasya śāntasya dāntasya sarvendriyārtheṣv aśaktasya viśveśvarasyāntikaṃ deham āsādita tasyāprameyaprabhāvaprabhālaṅkṛtajñānakośasya sampūrṇacandraprakāśātirekānanasya surendrāsurendroragaiś ca bhaktyā prasādena nityavandyasya pradīptaujasā puṇyakīrter maharṣiprasūtasya niṣkrāntahemaprakāśasya dharmeśvasyāgradharmeṣu pāraṅgatasyāgrasattvasya nāthasya nāgasya muktasya dhīrasya vīrasya devātidevasya samyaksambuddhasya kas tasya śaknoty aśeṣān guṇān vaktum ||
body.translated_text: [110] Then on the next day, that hired man, the field-guard, taking the food-packet given by his master at dawn as was customary, set out for the field. On the way, that hired man heard from a certain lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>) that the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> had obtained such prosperity by offering a single bean-cake to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. Having heard this, that man said to the lay devotee: 'Good sir, what are the virtues of that Blessed One?' The lay devotee said: 'Good friend, what power do I have to speak of the specially constituted virtues of that Blessed One? But hear just one summary: That Blessed One is the perfectly awakened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), adorned with the marks of the supreme person, brilliant as a golden mountain, of radiance surpassing the moon and sun, of excellent vows, of good conduct, of tranquil mind, of beautiful speech, of fine appearance, of beautiful limbs, of beautiful face, of beautiful eyes, of good deeds, of good <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with patience and brilliance. A trainer, a good guide, knower of conduct, knower of restraint, grateful, of good vision, with pacified senses, with well-trained faculties, a great king of <s>Dharma</s>, of great heroic essence, a great protector of the world, a great banner of knowledge, a great champion of discourse, a great treasury of merit, a great cause of <s>Dharma</s>, a great caravan leader, a giver of <s>Dharma</s>, a great helmsman, supremely worthy of offerings, a cutter of thirst, a destroyer of great delusion, an extinguisher of anger, an establisher in liberation, one who turns from the wrong path, a pointer to the right path, a cutter of doubt, a revealer of truth, an extinguisher of defilements, a destroyer of <s>Māra</s>, a deliverer of the world, worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, honored by <s>Śakra</s>, superior to all worlds, working for the welfare of all worlds, the supreme being, the maker of an end to all suffering, omniscient, skilled in training and discipline, one who has overcome all outflows, not overcome by the chief of debaters, unshaken by any fault, devoted to every purpose, beautiful in form, endowed with morality, with meditation, with vigor, united with knowledge, without craving, without fever, without elaboration, of effortless conduct, a shower of the means to the cessation of [cyclic] activity, of friendly intent toward all beings, freed from evil, endowed with determination, unsurpassed guide and teacher, a great physician for those afflicted by the disease of defilements, self-born, all-pervading, self-controlled, of immeasurable power and glory, of few needs, well-contented, timely, meaningful, wise, with the enemy of defilements vanquished, with fire extinguished, of unshakable <s>Dharma</s>, supremely worthy of offerings. Having seen from above the suffering world sunk in the mire of ignorance, and being himself able to deliver it, in accordance with his own power and glory, for the sake of compassion toward all beings, with this supreme kind of wisdom [he thought]: "How shall I deliver this suffering world? How shall I liberate it? How shall I console the fearful? How shall I raise up those sunk in <s>saṃsāra</s>? How shall I refresh those who are burning?" Having thus generated a firm resolve and exerting supreme effort, through hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, as before, [giving] food, drink, shelter, sandals, meals, umbrellas, vehicles, seats, and such things, elephants, horses, wives, sons, servants male and female, and cutting out his own head, eyes, and bodily flesh, with blood, jewels, and the diamond [of resolve], in the form of a hawk, with the soul of a <s>Buddha</s>, thinking of the welfare of all beings by all means at all times, and looking upon those who are aged, afflicted, confused, bewildered, and agitated, consoling them with his whole self, though virtuous associating even with the non-virtuous like a teacher, through generosity, morality, patience, heroic endeavor, wisdom, meditation, and other virtues, through countless hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, he attained the supreme, auspicious <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). Moreover—who can speak of the complete virtues of that foremost of all beings, the perfectly awakened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) of renowned fame, whose compassion proclaims trustworthiness in <s>Dharma</s>, who is filled with discernment, of expansive vigor, who has fulfilled all his vows, freed from all faults, with delusion extinguished, peaceful, tamed, unattached to all sense-objects, lord of all, whose treasury of knowledge is adorned with immeasurable power and glory, whose face surpasses the radiance of the full moon, who is constantly worshipped with devotion and faith by the lords of the gods, the lords of the <s>asuras</s>, and the <s>nāgas</s>, of blazing splendor and meritorious fame, born of the great sages, of radiance surpassing that of gold, the lord of <s>Dharma</s>, one who has reached the far shore in the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost of beings, a protector, a great being (<s>nāga</s>), liberated, steadfast, heroic, the god above gods, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>—who can speak of all his virtues?'

sarvasadrūpalāvaṇyasampadbhiḥ samalaṅkṛtaṃ |

children.text: vapur buddhād ṛte nāsti anyasyedṛśam uttamaṃ |1|
children.translated_text: Equal to that of the <s>Buddha</s>; no other possesses such supreme [form]. [1]

children.text: nāsti buddhasamaṃ pātraṃ nāsti buddhasamaḥ sukhī |

children.text: nāsti buddhasamo dānto nāsti buddhasamaḥ prabhuḥ |3|
children.translated_text: There is no tamed one equal to the <s>Buddha</s>; there is no lord equal to the <s>Buddha</s>. [3]

children.text: nāsti buddhasamaḥ śāstā nāsti buddhasamaḥ pitā |
children.translated_text: There is no teacher equal to the <s>Buddha</s>; there is no father equal to the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: nāsti buddhasamo bandhur nāsti buddhasamaḥ suhṛt |4|
children.translated_text: There is no kinsman equal to the <s>Buddha</s>; there is no friend equal to the <s>Buddha</s>. [4]
Without possessiveness, without intoxication, without fear, without weariness, without blemish,
Having crossed the wilderness of existence, without rival, without affliction— [5]

children.text: kāntaḥ śāntaḥ śucir dāntaḥ smṛtimān balavān vaśī |
children.translated_text: Beautiful, peaceful, pure, tamed, mindful, powerful, self-controlled—
For one who has worked for the welfare of all beings, there is no other equal to the <s>Buddha</s>. [6]

children.text: samāsato guṇaiḥ sadbhir viśeṣair vidhivad yataḥ |
children.translated_text: In brief, by good qualities and special excellences, properly considered,
Let it be understood that even in the three worlds there is none equal to the <s>Buddha</s>.' [7]

body.translated_text:
[111] Moreover:
'There is no body adorned with all the endowments of beauty, grace, and splendor

body.text:
Sva Roy 309,2 - 312,5
[112] tac chrutvā bhṛtakapuruṣaḥ prasādakaṇṭakitaḥ sahasaivotpannātidurllabhapratibhānas tam uvāca || karṇena sārthavāhena tṛṣṇayānupradattaṃ māṣapūpakam evaṃvidhe paramadakṣiṇīye bhagavati vipaśyini tathāgate tatkṣaṇād evaiṣa sārthavāho 'daridraḥ syām ity evaṃvidhaṃ cintāmaṇiratnabhūtaṃ tathāgatam āsādyātiparīttavibhavamātrakahetabhūtaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān | ahan tu punar yad bhagavantaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyakasambuddham anekakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrair apy anāsādya darśanam atidarśanīyam anuttaram anantarakalpaśatasahasrasambhṛtāśeṣasattvapravṛtottamapuṇyasambhārānupravṛttakāruṇyam anekavidhasāṃsārikakleśaviṣamahoragopadaṣṭa_atidīnānukampakaṃ patitajanaviśeṣavatsalam anupakṛtabāndhavam anekakālānāsāditavibhavo 'ham anayābhiparīttayā kṣetrapālitārjitayā bhaktabhikṣayā pratipādayitum āsādayāmi | tadā tādṛśaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kariṣyāmi yena sarvasattvottamo bhaviṣyāmīty āśayodgīrṇavacanāvasānasamanantaraṃ bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksambuddhas tasya cetaso cittam ājñāya ṛddhayā gatvāgrataḥ sthito 'drākṣīt sa bhṛtakapuruṣo vipaśyinaṃ tathāgatam asecanakadarśanam abhiruciracārucāmīkarāmaragiriśikharatararuṇavikiraṇavisaracitāntarodbhāsitabhāsurataraśarīradyutiṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paramaprītisaumanasya jāto 'timahatā prasādavegena tāṃ bhaktapuṭikām ādāya bhagavato vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pātre pratipādya tīvreṇa prasādavegena pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: [112] Hearing this, the hired man, his hair standing on end with faith, and suddenly possessed of an exceedingly rare inspiration, said to him: 'The caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>, having given a bean-cake out of craving to such a supremely worthy recipient—the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>—that caravan leader at that very moment [thought]: "May I become wealthy"—and having thus found a <s>Tathāgata</s> who is like a wish-fulfilling gem, he made an aspiration that was merely the cause of extremely limited resources. But I, though I may not find the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), whose appearance is supremely beautiful and unsurpassed—[one whose] supreme accumulation of merit arisen from the practice for all beings was gathered over hundreds of thousands of incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (eons), impelled by compassion; who has compassion for the supremely wretched ones bitten by the great serpent of the poison of various afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>; who has special tenderness for fallen beings; who is an unrepaid kinsman—even I, of resources never before obtained over countless ages, am now in a position to offer [even] this food obtained as alms earned by guarding fields, this meager [offering]. Then I shall make such an aspiration by which I shall become the foremost of all beings!' And immediately upon the conclusion of these words uttered from aspiration, the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, knowing the thought in his mind, went by supernatural power and stood before him. That hired man saw the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, whose beauty was undiminishing, whose body-radiance shone forth brilliant and resplendent, illuminated within by the scattered rays of the peak of a golden immortal mountain. And seeing him, filled with supreme joy and delight, with an exceedingly great rush of faith, he took that food-packet and placed it in the bowl of the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>. Then, with an intense rush of faith, falling at his feet, he began to make his aspiration:

body.text:
Sva Roy 312,5 - 314,3
[113] anena nātha puṇyena itaḥ prabhṛti janmanaḥ |

children.translated_text: May I be one who contemplates the welfare of all beings, primarily endowed with compassion. [1]
Just as you, endowed with the [major] marks, have attained the unsurpassed <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening),
So may I too attain the incomparable <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). [2]
Just as you teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and just as omniscience

children.text: prāptaṃ tathāham apy eva sarvajñatvam avāpnuyāṃ |3|
children.translated_text: Has been attained by you, so may I too attain omniscience. [3]

children.text: nirjitas te yathā māro dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Māra</s> has been conquered by you and the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) has been set in motion,
So may I too, having conquered [Māra], set in motion the <s>Dharmacakra</s>. [4]
Having crossed over, you deliver [others], O Protector, from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence);

children.text: atvān bahūṃs tathā cāhaṃ tārāye munisattama |5|
children.translated_text: Having crossed over many, so too shall I deliver [them], O supreme sage.' [5]

body.translated_text: [113] 'By this merit, O Protector, from this birth onward,

body.text: atha sa bhagavān vipaśyī samyaksasambuddhaḥ sakalajaladagambhīrodāttena svareṇoccair uvāca | bhadramukha |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, in a voice deep and noble like the full ocean, spoke aloud: 'Good friend—

children.text: jitveha māraṃ sabalaṃ prasahya bhīmaṃ samantād abhiniṣpatantaṃ |6|
