Thus [he spoke].

body.translated_text: You shall indeed become one of great power, a teacher on earth named <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (Accomplisher of All Goals),

body.text:
Sva Roy 314,3 - 316,3
[114] atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhas taṃ puruṣam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau vyākṛtya prakrānto 'yañ ca vṛttānto bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ samantato niḥsṛtaḥ | yāvad rājñāṃ bandhumatā śrutaṃ | śrutvā ca punas tena svayam evāgatya tatakuśalamūlasaṃbhārotsāhitamatinā sa puruṣo 'ti mahatā satkāreṇa hastiskandhe samāropya bhavanaṃ nītvārdhāsanaṃ niṣādyārddharājyānupradānena pūjitaḥ | sa kathayati | mahārāja nāhaṃ kāmair arthī tadanujānīsva māṃ pravrajya brahmacaryañ carāmīti | sa rājñānujñātaḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitaḥ sa tatra yāvad āptabrahmacaryaṃ caritvā kālagato nirmāṇaratiṣu deveṣūprapannaḥ | bandhumān api rājā kālagataḥ | tasya putro rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ | so 'pi kiñcit kālaṃ rājyaṃ kārayitvā kālagato 'mātyair mahatā satkāreṇa surūpo rājye pratiṣṭhāpitas tena ṣaṣṭhivarṣahasrāṇi dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāritaṃ | tataḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā tuṣitadevanikāye upapannaḥ |
body.translated_text: [114] Then <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, having prophesied that man's [attainment of] unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>Samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), departed. And this account spread throughout the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When King <s>Bandhumān</s> heard [of this], having heard, he himself came, and with his mind inspired by the accumulation of that man's roots of merit, he honored that man with the greatest reverence, mounting him upon the back of an elephant, taking him to the palace, seating him upon half the throne, and honoring him with the gift of half the kingdom. He [the man] said: 'Great king, I have no desire for pleasures. Please permit me to go forth and practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>).' Permitted by the king, he went forth into the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Having practiced the holy life there to its fulfillment, at the time of death he was reborn among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods. King <s>Bandhumān</s> also died. His son was established in the kingdom. He too, after ruling for some time, died. The ministers then established <s>Surūpa</s> (the handsome one) in the kingdom with great honor, and he ruled the kingdom righteously for sixty thousand years. Then, at the time of death, he was reborn in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven.

body.text:
Sva Roy 316,4 - 318,5
[115] kiṃ manyase mahārājānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena surūpro nāma rājā 'bhūd iti | na khalv evaṃ dṛṣṭavyaṃ | api tv eṣa suvarṇavarṇaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena surūpo 'nāma rājābhūd yad anena vipaśyini tathāgate haridrāraktaṃ vastrakhaṇḍam anupradataṃ praṇidhānañ ca kṛtaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākenānena devamanuṣyeṣv anantaṃ devyamānuṣyakaṃ sukham anubhūtaṃ yatra yatropapadyate tatra tatra suvarṇakāyaḥ suvarṇavarṇavastrācchāditaśarīraḥ karṇikārakusumavarṣaṃ cāsya jātisamaye prapatati sma || yāvad etarhy apy evaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyo yat kāyād asakṛd apanīte vastre 'nyad vastraṃ tatkṣaṇād eva śarīre samutpadyata iti | yo 'sau karṇaḥ sārthavāho 'yam evāsau divākaraḥ sārthavāhas tena kālena tena samayena yā sā karṇasya sārthavāhasya bhāryā | eṣaiva divākarasya sārthavāhasya bhāryā | dāsī kāśisundarī dāsaḥ pracaṇḍo 'grāmātyas tena kālena tena samayena |
body.translated_text: [115] What do you think, great king—was that King <s>Surūpa</s> at that time someone else? It should not be seen thus. Rather, this <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> was King <s>Surūpa</s> at that time. Because he offered a piece of turmeric-dyed cloth to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s> and made an aspiration, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> (deed) he experienced infinite divine and human happiness among gods and humans. Wherever he was reborn, there his body was golden, his body was covered with golden-colored garments, and a rain of <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers fell at the time of his birth. Even now, as the one called <s>Puṇyamaheśa</s> (Lord of Great Merit), when his garment is repeatedly removed from his body, another garment arises on his body at that very instant. He who was the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s>—he is this very caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. She who was the wife of the caravan leader <s>Karṇa</s> at that time—she is this very wife of the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>. The slave-girl was <s>Kāśisundarī</s>; the slave was <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, the chief minister at that time.

body.text:
Sva Roy 318,5 - 320,321
[116] punar api rājā 'jātaśatruḥ sthavirānandam idam avocat | kiṃ bhadantānanda suvarṇavarṇena bhikṣuṇā karma kṛtaṃ | yasya karmaṇo vipākenādūśy anapakārī śūle samāropitaḥ | pravrajyañ cārhatvaṃ prāptam iti | sthavirānandaḥ kathayati | bhūtapūrvaṃ mahārājātīte dhvani candro nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāñ ca manuṣyānāñ ca buddho bhagavān asau 'nyatamāṃ rājadhānīm upaniḥsṛtya viharati sma | tena khalu samayenānyatamasmiṃś ca vihāre 'nyatamo bhikṣuḥ dhārmakathikaḥ sa kālena kālam āgatāgatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | tasya mahān lābhasatkāra utpadyate |
body.translated_text: [116] Again, King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said to the elder <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, what <s>karma</s> (deed) was performed by the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, by the ripening of which he, though innocent and having done no harm, was impaled on a stake? And [what karma led to] his going forth and attaining <s>arhatship</s>?' The elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'In the past, great king, in a former age, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Candra</s> (Moon) arose in the world—a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone (<s>Sugata</s>), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. He had gone forth to a certain royal capital and was dwelling there. At that time, in a certain monastery, a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> who was a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher would from time to time teach the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who came [to listen]. Great gain and honor arose for him.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 320,3 - 323,4
[117] yāvad apareṇa samayenājito nāma bhikṣuḥ dhārmakathiko yuktamuktapratibhānaś citrakatho madhurakatho | janapadacārikāñ caran taṃ vihāram āgataḥ sa catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ dharma deśayaty ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavaśāne kalyāṇaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ samprakāśayati | tena sarva evāsau karvaṭanivāsījanakāyo 'bhiprasāditaḥ | sa lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ | tasya naivāsikasya dhārmakathikasya bhikṣor lābhasatkārasamucchinnas tasyaitad abhavad ajitena me bhikṣuṇā lābhasatkāra samucchedaḥ kṛtaḥ | tad yāvad eṣa ihāvatiṣṭhate tāvat kuto me lābhasatkāro bhaviṣyati | upāyam asya gamanāya cintayitavyam iti | punaś cintayati | asatkārabhīravaś caiva bahuśrutāḥ | asatkāro 'sya prayoktavya iti viditvānyatamāṃ brāhmaṇakumārikām āha | bhaginy ahan te vāsoyugam anupradāsyāmy etam ajitaṃ bhikṣuṃ dūṣaya mayā sārddham abrahmacārīti | sā kathayaty ārya yady aham evaṃ vakṣyāmi tat ko māṃ pariṇeṣyati | nanu yāvajjīvam mātāpitṛpoṣyā bhaviṣyāmīti | sa kathayaty ahaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathā na mahājanaviditaṃ bhaviṣyati | yadā tvaṃ svair ālāpena kathayiṣyasīti | api tu yadāyaṃ tṛbhiś caturbhiḥ parair bhikṣubhiḥ sārddhaṃ niṣaṇṇa ihāvatiṣṭhate | tayā pratijñātam evaṃ kariṣyāmīti |
body.translated_text: On another occasion, a <s>bhikṣu</s> named <s>Ajita</s>, a <s>Dharma</s> teacher, gifted in fitting and free eloquence, a varied and sweet narrator, arrived at that monastery while wandering through the countryside. He taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies—good at the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end—proclaiming the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) that is well-phrased, complete, pure, and stainless. By this, the entire population dwelling in that market town was inspired with faith. He received robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. The <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk who had been there [already] lost his gains and honor. This thought arose in him: 'The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> has cut off my gains and honor. As long as he stays here, how will I receive gains and honor? I must devise a stratagem for his departure.' He then thought further: 'The learned fear dishonor. Dishonor must be brought upon him.' Knowing this, he said to a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> maiden: 'Sister, I shall give you a pair of garments. Slander this <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> [by saying] "He has committed unchaste conduct with me."' She said: 'Venerable one, if I say such a thing, who will marry me? Will I not be dependent on my parents for life?' He said: 'I will arrange it so that the general public will not know of it. You will say it only in your own private conversation.' 'But when this one is seated here with three or four other <s>bhikṣu</s>s—' She agreed: 'I will do so.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 323,4 - 326,4
[118] yāvad aparasmin divase sa dhārmakathiko bhikṣur bhikṣubhiḥ sārddhaṃ layanadvāre niṣaṇṇaḥ kathāsāṃkathyenāvatiṣṭhate tayā ca brāhmaṇadārikayā gatvābhihitaḥ | ārya pravrajitā yūyam iti kṛtvā vayam iha visrabdhā upasaṃkramitavyaṃ manyāmahe | tat katham etad yuktaṃ yad aham anenāpy ajitena bhikṣuṇā haṭhād gṛhītvā vikumārī kṛteti | tatas tair bhikṣubhiḥ karṇau pidhāyābhihitaṃ | bhagini maivam vada naitac chrotavyam iti | tatas tena dhārmakathikena bhikṣuṇā na sādhu kṛtaṃ na sādhu kṛtam ity uktvā ajitasya bhikṣor avarṇo niścāritaḥ | yāvac chravaṇaparaṃparayā 'jitena bhikṣuṇā śrutaṃ śrutvā kathayati | ka evam āheti | eṣa dhārmakathiko bhikṣur iti | sa yena dhārmakathiko bhikṣus tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkrāmya kathayati | bhadanta kim mayā tavāparādhaṃ kṛtaṃ yad evam avarṇaniścāraṇaṃ me kṛtavān asīti | tena tasyāntike cittaṃ pradūṣya kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritaṃ tādṛśaṃ tvayā pāpakarma kṛtaṃ yena tvaṃ śulam arhasīti | tac chrutvā ajitasya bhikṣor etad abhavat | duḥkhito 'yaṃ tapasvy upahataś ceti viditvā pātracīvaram ādāya yathāparibhuktaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratiśamāyya tasmād vihārān niṣkramya saṃprasthitaḥ | tañ ca saṃprasthitam avalokya bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaḥ sa ca karvaṭakanīvāsījanakāyas taṃ nivarttayitukāmāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhā ||
body.translated_text: On another day, the <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk was seated at the door of the cave-dwelling with other <s>bhikṣu</s>s, engaged in discussion. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> maiden went and said: 'Venerable ones, thinking that you are renunciants, we have confidently come to visit. But how is it fitting that this <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> seized me by force and violated me?' Then those <s>bhikṣu</s>s, covering their ears, said: 'Sister, do not say such things! This should not be heard!' Then the <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk said: 'Not well done! Not well done!'—and spread ill-repute about the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s>. Eventually, through word of mouth, <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> heard [of it]. Having heard, he asked: 'Who says this?' 'This <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk.' He went to the <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk and, having approached, said: 'Venerable sir, what offense have I committed against you, that you have spread such ill-repute about me?' The other, having corrupted his mind against him, uttered harsh verbal action: 'You have committed such evil action that you deserve the stake!' Hearing this, this thought arose in the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s>: 'This one is distressed, wretched, and wounded.' Knowing this, taking his bowl and robe, tidying the lodging he had used, he departed from that monastery and set out. Seeing him depart, the <s>bhikṣu</s>s, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>s, and the population of the market town, wishing to bring him back, followed behind.

body.text:
Sva Roy 326,4 - 329,330
[119] tasya dhārmakathikasya bhikṣoḥ kaukṛtyam utpannaṃ na śobhanaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ yal lābhasatkārakāraṇād īdṛśam apāyagatisamvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtam ity utpannavaimanasyo gacchāmy enaṃ kṣamāpayāmīti tvaritatvaritaṃ tasmād vihārān niṣkramyātisamvignamanā aśrudhārāvasicyamānadīnavadano bāladāraka ivoccaiḥ prarudaran paśyatā teṣām anekeṣāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatiśatasahasrāṇām ajitasya bhikṣoḥ pādayor nipatyātyayam atyayato deśayitum ārabdhaḥ | kṣamasva bhadanta yathā bālena yathā mūḍhena yathāvyaktenākuśalena lābhasatkārābhibhūtena mayā tavābhūtenāvarṇo niścāritas tad atyayam atyato deśayata kṣamasvānukampām upādayeti | ajito bhikṣuḥ kathayati | āyuṣmān kṣāntam ity uktvātīvasaṃvignacitto 'nyatamaṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkam ābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtim upasthāpya tena tasminn eva paramasamvegadravīkṛtacetasā udyacchatā ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā yāvat sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca samvṛttaḥ | sa vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam utpatya tasya mahato janakāyasya manāṃsy abhiprasādyan vividhāni prātihāryāṇi pradarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | sa ca dhārmakathiko bhikṣus taṃ gaganatalas tam avalokya hā kasṭam īdṛśasya mayā maharṣer antike cittaṃ pradūṣitam ity uktvā mūrchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Remorse arose in that <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk: 'What I have done is not fitting—that for the sake of gains and honor I have committed such karma leading to the lower realms of rebirth.' Troubled in mind, [he said:] 'I shall go and beg his forgiveness.' Rushing out from that monastery with the utmost urgency, his mind deeply agitated, his wretched face streaming with tears, weeping loudly like a young child—before the eyes of those many hundreds of thousands of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and householders—he fell at the feet of the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> and began to confess his transgression as a transgression: 'Forgive me, venerable sir! As one who is foolish, as one who is deluded, as one who is unwise, as one who is unskilful, overpowered by gains and honor, I have spread false ill-repute about you. I confess this transgression as a transgression. Forgive me, out of compassion!' The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ajita</s> said: 'Venerable one, it is forgiven.' Having said this, with an extremely agitated mind, he went to a certain tree root and sat down, crossing his legs, straightening his body, and establishing mindfulness before him. With his mind melted by supreme urgency, striving, exerting, and endeavoring, having realized this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unsteady—he became worthy of veneration, honor, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Like a royal goose with outstretched wings, flying up to the sky, he began to display various miracles to the delight of that great multitude. And the <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk, looking up at him in the sky, said: 'Alas, woe! I have corrupted my mind against such a great sage!'—and fell unconscious to the ground.

body.text:
Sva Roy 330,1 - 332,333
[120] atrāntare bhagavāṃś candraḥ samyaksambuddho mahākaruṇayā parigatahṛdayaḥ mā khalv ayaṃ dhārmakathiko bhikṣur uṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ chardayitvā kālaṃ kariṣyatīti viditvā ṛddhayā taṃ karvaṭakam āgataḥ | tato bhagavatā candreṇa samyaksambuddhena cakrasvastikanandyāvartajālāvavaddhenānekapuṇyaśatanirjātena bhītānām āśvāsanakareṇa kareṇa sa dhārmakathiko bhikṣuḥ śirasi parāmṛṣṭaḥ | spṛṣṭamātraś ca bhagavatā sa bhikṣuś cetanāṃ pratilabhyotthito 'tyayam atyayato deśayitum ārabdhāḥ || atha bhagavāṃś candraḥ samyaksambuddhas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthā bhāṣate |
body.translated_text: At that point, the Blessed <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, his heart pervaded by great compassion, knowing that 'this <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk may vomit hot blood and die,' came to that market town by supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Then the Blessed <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, with his hand—marked with the wheel, <s>svastika</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, and net, produced from a hundred merits, bestowing reassurance to the frightened—touched the head of that <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk. The moment he was touched by the Blessed One, that monk regained consciousness, rose, and began to confess his transgression as a transgression. Then the Blessed <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, at that moment spoke these verses:

body.text: puruṣasya hi jātasya kuṭhārī jāyate mukhe |

children.text: cchinnatti hi yayātmānaṃ vācā durbhāṣitaṃ vadan |1|
children.translated_text: with it he cuts himself, speaking ill-spoken words. |1|

children.text: yo nindyajanaṃ praśaṃsati praśaṃsyañ ca janaṃ vinindati |
children.translated_text: He who praises one who deserves blame and blames one who deserves praise—

children.text: sa cinoti mukhena taṃ kaliṃ kalīnāṃ yena sukhaṃ na vandati |2|
children.translated_text: he accumulates by his mouth that misfortune by which he does not find happiness. |2|

children.text: alpamātro hy ayaṃ kalir ya ihākṣaiḥ svadhanaṃ parājayet |
children.translated_text: This is but a small misfortune—that one should lose one's own wealth here at dice;

children.text: ayam atra mahattaraḥ kalir yaḥ sugateṣu manaḥ pradūṣayet |3|
children.translated_text: this is the greater misfortune—that one should corrupt one's mind toward the well-gone ones (<s>Sugata</s>s). |3|

children.text: śataṃ sahasrāṇi nirarbudānāṃ ṣaṭtriṅśataṃ pañca caivārbudāni |
children.translated_text: A hundred thousand <s>nirarbuda</s> [hells] and thirty-six, and five <s>arbuda</s>s—

children.text: yān āryagarhī narakān upaiti vācaṃ manaś ca praṇidhāya pāpakaṃ |4|
children.translated_text: these are the hells that the reviler of noble ones enters, having directed evil speech and mind. |4|

children.text:
( for a verse in Tibetan corresponding to Udānavarga VIII.6)
cittapradūṣaṇāhetoḥ satvā gacchanti durggatiṃ |
children.translated_text: Because of corrupting the mind, beings go to lower realms (<s>durgati</s>);
because of purifying the mind, beings go to good realms (<s>sadgati</s>). |5|

body.translated_text: 'For a man who is born, an axe is born in his mouth;

body.text: ity eṣa bhagavāṃś candra samyaksambuddhastāṃ parṣadaṃ dhārmayā kathayā yāvat saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the Blessed <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having gladdened that assembly with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text:
Sva Roy 333,2 - 336,5
[121] kim manyase mahārājānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena dhārmakathiko bhikṣur abhūd iti | na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyam api tv eṣa eva suvarṇavarṇaḥ tena kālena tena samayena tasya bhikṣor antike citta pradūṣya kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena pañcajanmaśatāni narakeṣu pattvā manuṣyeṣu cotpannaḥ pañcajātiśatāni adūṣy anapakārī śūlam āropito yāvad etarhy api tenaiva karmavaśeṇādūṣy anapakārī śūlam ārāpito yady anena tat karma kṛtvā nātyayam atyayato deśitaṃ syāt tad eṣa pañcajanmaśatāny ekaikasmiṃ mahāniraye pakvaḥ syāt | pañcajanmaśatāni preteṣu pañcajanmaśatāni tiryakṣupapannaḥ syāt | yad anena bhagavataś candrasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane brahmacaryañ caritaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākenaitarhy anena bhagavacchāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti || tasmāt tarhi mahārāja ātmano duḥkham anvicchatā na pareṣām antike cittapradūṣaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ || ayaśobhītena ca na pareṣām ayaśo 'nupradeśyaṃ | ātmanaḥ sukham anvicchatā pareṣām api sukhopasaṃhāraḥ kartavya ity athāsmin dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe 'nekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mahāṃ viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ | kaiścit śrotāpattiphalaṃ kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ kaiścid anāgāmiphalaṃ kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ | kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittāny utpāditāni | kaiścit śrāvakabodhau | kaiścic caraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni | yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyasthāpitā ||
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, Great King? Was it someone else who was that <s>Dharma</s>-teacher monk at that time, in that era? It should not be viewed thus. Rather, it was this very <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>. At that time, in that era, having corrupted his mind against that monk, he uttered harsh verbal action. As the ripening of that karma, having fallen into the hells for five hundred births, and then being born among humans, for five hundred births, though innocent and without offense, he was mounted upon a stake. Even now, by the force of that very karma, though innocent and without offense, he was mounted upon a stake. If, having committed that karma, he had not confessed his transgression as a transgression, he would have been cooked in each of the great hells for five hundred births [each]; for five hundred births among the <s>preta</s>s (hungry ghosts); for five hundred births born among animals. But because he practiced the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the teaching of the Blessed <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>—as the ripening of that karma, now, having renounced in the teaching of the Blessed One, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.' 'Therefore, Great King, one who does not seek suffering for oneself must not corrupt one's mind toward others. And one who fears ill-repute must not spread ill-repute about others. One who seeks happiness for oneself must bring about happiness for others too.' Then, while this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great distinction. Some realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotāpattiphala</s>); some, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); some, the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); some, having renounced, through the complete abandonment of all afflictions, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Some generated the mind of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>); some, toward disciple-enlightenment (<s>śrāvakabodhi</s>); some took upon themselves the precepts of conduct and practice. The majority of that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text:
Sva Roy 336,5 - 339,3
[122] atha divākaraḥ sārthavāha ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kṛtakarapuṭaḥ sthavirānandam etad avocat | āryānanda mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'ntarggṛhe upanimantrya ṣaḍrasenāhāreṇa bhojayitvā ekaiko bhikṣuḥ śatasahasrakeṇa cīvareṇācchādayitavya iti vicintitaṃ sa ca bhagavān parinirvṛtas tad icchāmy āyīnandapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgham adhunā bhojayitum iti || sthavirānandaḥ kathayati | sārthavāhaivaṃ kuruṣvāhaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi sarva eva jāmbūdvīpāvasthitā bhagavataḥ śrāvakā ihāgamiṣyantīti | atha divākaraḥ sārthavāhaḥ praharṣapūrṇamanā rājagṛhasya nagarasya bahir maṇḍalavāṭakam apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalaṃ samucchritadhvajapatākaṃ candanavārisiktam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpāṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopadhūpaghaṭikopanibaddham atiruciravitānatoraṇam atiramaṇīyaṃ kārayitvā tām eva rātriṃ śucipraṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyam evotthāyāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvodakamaṇī pratiṣṭhāpya sthavirānandasya dūtena kālam ārocayati | samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase | ity
body.translated_text: Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, with palms joined, said to the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Noble <s>Ānanda</s>, I had intended to invite the monastic community of <s>bhikṣu</s>s headed by the <s>Buddha</s> to the inner house, to feed them with a meal of six flavors, and to clothe each <s>bhikṣu</s> with a robe worth a hundred thousand [coins]. But that Blessed One has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, I wish now to feed the monastic community of <s>bhikṣu</s>s headed by the Noble <s>Ānanda</s>.' The Elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Caravan leader, do so. I will act in such a way that all the disciples of the Blessed One abiding in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will come here.' Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, his mind full of joy, had a circular enclosure prepared outside the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>—cleared of stones, gravel, and rubble, with raised banners and flags, sprinkled with sandalwood water, hung with festoons of silk garlands, strewn with various flowers, perfumed with fragrant incense from censers, with exceedingly beautiful canopies and arched gateways, exceedingly delightful. That very night, having prepared pure and excellent food and refreshments, rising early in the morning, having arranged the seats and set out water pitchers, he announced the time to the Elder <s>Ānanda</s> by messenger: 'It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready. May you come when you think it fit.'

body.text:
Sva Roy 339,3 - 341,5
[123] atha sthavirānando nabhastalam utplutya ṛddhyā sakalam idaṃ jambudvīpam vilīnakanaka_vabhāsayā prabhayāvabhāsya svayam eva gaṇḍīm ākoṭya sajalajaladharagambhīraodāttena svareṇodghoṣitavān ye bhagavataḥ śrāvakā ṛddher lābhinas te svakīyayā ṛddhyā āgacchantu ye pṛthagjanās te madīyayā ṛddhyā āgacchantv iti | tatas tāṃ gaṇḍīm upaśrutya himavadvindhyamalayapāriyātrakagandhamādanasumeruyuganghareṣādhārakhadirakasudarśanāśvakarṇanimindharādiṣu sakānanasaritasusītā samudrapattanavaradrumavihārāvaśaṣu meṭhīśūnyāgāraśmāśānādiṣu ca ye bhikṣavaḥ samādhisamāpattisukhalābhinnaḥ prativasanti tatkṣaṇaāt sarvam idaṃ nabhastalamaśokakiṃśusadṛśaiḥ sandhyālohitair iva jīmūtavṛndair ācchādayanto rājagṛhanagaram āgatya tasmiṃ maṇḍalavāṭe 'vatīrṇāḥ | tatkṣaṇād eva tisraḥ koṭyo bhikṣuṇyāḥ 'sannipatitaḥ | ekā kṣīṇāsravaṇāṃ | dvitīya śaikṣaṇāṃ | tṛtīyā pṛthakagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ tato yathā vṛddhikayā prajñapteṣu sveṣu sveṣv āśaneṣūpaviṣṭāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, leaping into the sky, by supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) illuminated this entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with radiance like molten gold, and himself striking the bell (<s>gaṇḍī</s>), with a voice as deep and noble as a rain cloud filled with water, he announced: 'Those disciples of the Blessed One who have obtained supernatural powers—let them come by their own powers. Those who are ordinary persons—let them come by my supernatural power.' Then, hearing that bell, the <s>bhikṣu</s>s who dwelt in the forests, rivers, cool retreats, ocean ports, excellent tree monasteries, hermitages, empty houses, and charnel grounds at <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, <s>Iṣādhāra</s>, <s>Khadiraka</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>Nimindhara</s>, and other [mountains]—absorbed in the bliss of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) and meditative attainments—at that very instant, covering the entire sky, like evening clouds in autumn, crimson as <s>aśoka</s> and <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers, came to the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> and descended at that circular enclosure. At that very instant, three <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions) of <s>bhikṣu</s>s assembled: the first [group] of those whose outflows were destroyed (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>), the second of learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and the third of virtuous ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). Then, in due order of seniority, they sat down in their respective appointed seats.

body.text:
Sva Roy 341,5 - 345,1
[124] atha divākara sārthavāhaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇam āryasthavirānandapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayati | yāvad bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhuktavadantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ śatasahasreṇa tricīvareṇācchādayitukāmas taṃ bhikṣusaṃgham avalokya prītimanā abhavat | suvarṇavarṇaś ca tasyāśayam avagamyāha alpotsuka tvaṃ bhava hi | aham eva bhikṣusaṃghaṃ suvarṇavarṇapītena tricīvareṇācchādayāmīti || tataḥ suvarṇavarṇena bhikṣuṇā tasminn eva kṣaṇe svaśarīrāt suvarṇapītāni vasrāṇi avatāryāvatārya śatasahasramūlyānāṃ yathā vṛddhikayā tisṛṇāṃ bhikṣukoṭīnāṃ tricīvaram anupradattaṃ || atrāntare 'nekair devatāsahasrair hā hākāro muktaḥ | vividhāni ca vādyāni saṃpravāditāni | divyañ ca puṣpapūrṇavarṣam utsṛṣṭaṃ yathāsau nānādigdeśābhyāgato janakāyo rājā cājātaśatruḥ sāntaḥpurakumārāmatyapaurajānapadasahāyas taṃ tathāvidham āścaryam avalokya vismayotphullalocanas trir udānam udānayaty aho puṇyaphalavipākaḥ aho puṇyānāṃ sāmarthya aho dakṣiṇīyakṣetrāvaropitasya dānabījasyānatikrānto vipākas tat kena nāma viduṣā evaṃvidhaṃ puṇyaphalavipākam abhisamīkṣya taddakṣiṇīyakṣetre dānaṃ na deyam ity evam anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi śirasy āñjalim upanidhāya namo buddhāyety uccair ghoṣitavanto 'tha sthavirānandena dakṣiṇādeśanā kṛtā |
body.translated_text: [124] Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the noble elder <s>Ānanda</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands satisfied them with pure and excellent hard and soft foods. When he knew that the community of monks had finished eating, had washed their hands and had their bowls removed, wishing to clothe the community of monks with a hundred thousand sets of three robes, he looked upon the assembly and was filled with joy. <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, understanding his intention, said: 'Be at ease, for I myself shall clothe the community of monks with golden-yellow sets of three robes.' Then, at that very moment, the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s>, removing golden-yellow garments again and again from his own body, with interest as it were, offered sets of three robes worth a hundred thousand each to three <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of monks. At that moment, many thousands of gods raised a cry of wonder. Various musical instruments were played. A divine rain of flowers was released. The great multitude that had come from various regions and countries, and King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> together with his inner palace, princes, ministers, citizens, and countryfolk, gazing upon such a marvel with eyes wide open in amazement, three times uttered an exclamation: 'Oh, the ripening of the fruit of merit! Oh, the power of merit! Oh, the unfailing ripening of the seed of giving sown in a worthy field of merit! What wise person, having observed such a ripening of the fruit of merit, would not give a gift to such a worthy field of merit?' Thus many hundreds of thousands of beings, placing their joined palms upon their heads, loudly proclaimed: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!' Then the elder <s>Ānanda</s> delivered the dedication of merit.

body.text:
Sva Roy 345,1 - 346,3
[125] tato divākaraḥ sārthavāha uthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthibyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena sthavirānandas tenāñjalīṃ praṇamya trir udānam udānayatīdaṃ bhadantāsmākaṃ na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa pūrvapretena śravaṇabrāhmaṇair yad ānandenāsmākaṃ kṛtaṃ pracchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrā iti ||
body.translated_text: [125] Then the caravan leader <s>Divākara</s>, rising from his seat, adjusting his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms in the direction of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, three times uttered this exclamation: 'Venerable Sir, what has been done for us was not done by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and brahmins—what <s>Ānanda</s> has done for us is this: he has dried up the ocean of our tears of blood!'

body.text:
jagati daityanarāmarapūjita vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya |
bhavasahasrasudurlabhaṃ darśana saphalam adya munes tava darśanaṃ |1| ity
body.translated_text: 'O you who are worshipped in the world by demons, humans, and gods, free from birth, old age, death, and disease, whose sight is more difficult to obtain than in thousands of existences—fruitful today is the sight of you, O sage!' [1]

body.text:
Sva Roy 346,3 - 5
[126] atha sthavirānandas tāṃ sarājikāṃ parṣadaṃ dharmyayā kathayā sandarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃgraharṣya tair devatāśatasahasrair anekaiś ca rājagṛhavāsibhiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair namasyamāna utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ | evam alpam api bhagavati buddhe kṛtam analpaphalam bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: [126] Then the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened that assembly together with the king by means of a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, being saluted by those hundreds of thousands of gods and by many hundreds of thousands of beings dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, rose from his seat and departed. Thus, even a small deed done for the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> bears no small fruit.

body.text:
Sva Roy 346,5 - 347,3
ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ (6) teṣān tathāgato hy avadat |

children.text: teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evamvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ |1|
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation—thus speaks the great ascetic. [1]

body.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) which arise from a cause—the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

body.text: [127] deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ śākyabhikṣubuddhākaraguptasya yad atra puṇyan tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasattvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalavāptaya iti ||
body.translated_text: [127] This is the religious gift of <s>Buddhākaragupra</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> monk following the excellent <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Whatever merit there is herein, may it be for the attainment of the fruit of supreme knowledge by the entire multitude of beings, with teachers, preceptors, and parents at the fore.
